Voir ces messages d’appel au don, ça peut être pénible. Nous le savons. Et on doit bien vous avouer que nous préférerions ne pas avoir à les écrire…
Mais voilà : c’est crucial pour l’Humanité. Si ce titre existe toujours aujourd’hui, c’est grâce au financement régulier de nos lectrices et lecteurs.
- C’est grâce à votre soutien que nous pouvons exercer notre métier avec passion. Nous ne dépendons ni des intérêts d’un propriétaire milliardaire, ni de pressions politiques : personne ne nous dicte ce que nous devons dire ou taire.
- Votre engagement nous libère aussi de la course aux clics et à l’audience. Plutôt que de chercher à capter l’attention à tout prix, nous choisissons de traiter les sujets que notre rédaction juge essentiels : parce qu’ils méritent d’être lus, compris, partagés. Parce que nous estimons qu’ils vous seront utiles
À l’heure actuelle, moins d’un quart des lectrices et lecteurs qui viennent plus de 3 fois sur le site par semaine nous aident à financer notre travail, par leur abonnement ou par leurs dons. Si vous voulez protéger le journalisme indépendant, s’il vous plaît, rejoignez-les.

https://taz.de/Deutsche-Digitalstrategie.author: Svenja Bergt
https://taz.de/Deutsche-Digitalstrategie.text:
Deutsche Digitalstrategie : Im KI-Wettrennen gibt es eine sinnvolle Abzweigung
Die führenden KI-Nationen kann Deutschland getrost vorbeiziehen lassen. Gezielte Investitionen in wichtigen Bereichen sollte man aber nicht verschlafen.
E in Börsengang der Superlative steht in den kommenden Wochen in den USA an: Das KI-Unternehmen Anthropic plant sein Debüt, erwartet wird eine Bewertung im Billionenbereich. Der überwiegende Teil des US-Wirtschaftswachstums geht Analysen zufolge mittlerweile auf Tech-Investitionen inklusive Rechenzentren zurück. Und Werbung für KI-Produkte als Alltagsbegleiter ist omnipräsent.
Und Deutschland so? Hier fordern Bundeskanzler und Digitalminister beim Digitalgipfel unisono mehr Tempo bei der Entwicklung und Nutzung der Technologie. Gleichzeitig ist nur ein winziger Bruchteil im Haushalt für KI vorgesehen.
Wer sich diese Diskrepanz anschaut, kann leicht zu dem Ergebnis kommen: Deutschland verschläft hier was. Etwas Entscheidendes. Etwas, das Wirtschaftswachstum bringen könnte. Und wenn wir nicht mitmachen beim globalen Wettrennen, wird Deutschland höchstens die Krumen aufsammeln können, die die KI-Nationen USA und China fallen gelassen haben.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Doch diese Sichtweise blendet wesentliche Faktoren aus: Zunächst ist überhaupt nicht ausgemacht, dass das, was KI-Unternehmen in den USA gerade bauen, als Geschäftsmodell taugt. Auch wenn sie mittlerweile etwa Abos für ihre KI-Chatbots verkaufen und Werbung einbinden, und sich mit beidem Geld verdienen lässt, sind die Dimensionen von tragfähigen Geschäftsmodellen noch weit entfernt. Zumal Unternehmenskunden, die die Technologie einsetzen, langsam merken, dass KI sie ganz schön teuer kommen kann. Und anfangen nachzurechnen, ob der Preis die Leistung rechtfertigt. Dazu kommt: Gerade in den USA sind die Proteste gegen Rechenzentren vielerorts stark, weil sie die Energiepreise in die Höhe schießen lassen und der Umwelt schaden.
Das heißt nicht, dass Deutschland und Europa die Technologie ignorieren sollten. Im Gegenteil. Schließlich entstehen neue Abhängigkeiten, wenn Nutzer:innen, Firmen oder Behörden hierzulande KI einsetzen wollen und dafür auf US-Modelle zugreifen müssen. Doch es gibt einen Weg zwischen Überhypen und Ignorieren: gezielte Investitionen.
Bei den Frontier-Modellen, also den leistungsfähigsten KI-Modellen von Unternehmen wie Anthropic und OpenAI, wird Europa nicht mithalten können. Zu wenig Risikokapital, zu wenig Big Tech, denn für das Training dieser großen Sprachmodelle braucht es Unmengen an Daten. Dafür gibt es andere Bereiche, in denen Unternehmen hierzulande punkten könnten: bei industriellen Anwendungen, in der Robotik, bei spezialisierten Modellen für sensible Einsatzzwecke von Gesundheit bis Verwaltung, in denen man vielleicht lieber nicht auf einen US-Anbieter mit all seinen Risiken und Nebenwirkungen setzen will.
Dieser Ansatz strahlt natürlich nicht so schillernd wie die neuesten Topmodelle aus den USA. Dafür sind auch die Abgründe – von Ressourcenverbrauch über Emissionen bis Urheber- und Persönlichkeitsrechtsverletzungen – weniger tief.

du site ou de l’application

https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.title: Crystal Palace v Liverpool, Sunderland v Chelsea, and more: Premier League – live
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.author: Simon Burnton
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.text:
GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-3 Liverpool (Isak, 89 mins)
Now Isak has his goal! Another break in which he combines with Munoz: an excellent pass plays the Spaniard down the right, a low ball infield finds Wirtz and he touches to Isak, who takes his chance expertly!
Chance for Isak, but Henderson saves! Liverpool break from their own penalty area: Wirtz hoofs the ball clear, Isak and Munoz exchange passes and the Swede carries it to the edge of the area before shooting low, hard, and too close to the keeper.
Munoz tees up Wirtz for another first-time shot, but this one’s too close to Henderson. It hasn’t been an overwhelming performance from Liverpool by any means, but Palace look a beaten side now (cue inevitable comeback).
Munoz throws himself over Lerma’s foot and is rightly booked for diving. Mac Allister confronts Lerma in the aftermath, and both players also end up with yellow cards.
Rio Ngumoha, a 76th-minute substitute, takes an extraordinarily optimistic shot, from maybe three yards short of the byline and 15 yards wide of goal. It had almost no chance of going in even if it was on target, which it very emphatically was not.
Brilliant chance for Crystal Palace! A defensive slip allows Richards to run through on the right and square to Pino, but it’s a bit behind him and he’s forced to take a touch, and by the time he shoots Alisson has raced off his line and the shot hits the keeper!
Palace are trying, a bit clumsily at present, to find a way back into this game. Osorio tries to find a way past Kerkez, but the Liverpool defender throws himself to the ground and wins a free kick.
Another chance for Liverpool, but Mitchell slides in to block a cross-shot from Barcola, who has switched to the right flank at half-time and looks much more threatening for it.
A point of information from Grant Kempton, regarding the Igor Thiago red card: “Just to correct. Chema was booked ... taken off at half time because of the booking. But its still force into the face so booking and red card sounds right.” Ah fair dos.
GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-2 Liverpool (Wirtz, 54 mins)
Liverpool double their lead! Barcola is played down the right and sends in a nice low cross, possibly aiming for Isak, but it runs to Wirtz and he strokes it into the corner!
Two players run clear for Crystal Palace, and Wharton just has to slide the ball across for Strand Larsen to turn it in! But his pass is abysmal, Strand Larsen can’t reach it, and he’ll be grateful in the circumstances that he was about 10 yards offside when the ball was played through.
“Re the Thiago sending-off, we saw last week with the shirt-pull on Isak that wasn’t punished precisely why players over-exaggerate,” writes Andy Flintoff. For sure, but if someone hits your chin and you go down holding your forehead, you’re not drawing the referee’s attention to a foul, you’re cheating.
GOAL! Ipswich 0-2 Bournemouth (Davis own goal, 46 mins)
The second half has started with a bang at Ipswich! An own-bang! Christie shoots from the left of goal, with his left foot and not from a great position, but you don’t win the lottery unless you buy a ticket, and the ball comes off Leif Davis and flies into the net!
“I haven’t seen the hands to the face, I’m busy cooking and with no TV in the kitchen I can’t watch but am just following here,” writes George Ronczy. “If Andres was hit in the neck and grabbed his forehead, he should get booked for simulation.” Absolute and complete agreement from me: the officials may decide that Igor Thiago’s push was violent enough to deserve a red card, it seemed harsh to me but an argument can be made for it. However Andres certainly overdramatised the situation and there should be repercussions for that also.
In the third of three minutes’ stoppage time at Palace a Szoboszlai corner is flicked on to Araujo, five yards out, but he can’t react in time to do anything with it and the ball ends up in Henderson’s hands.
An absolutely unstoppable penalty from Pascal Gross to double Brighton’s lead. Kelleher goes he right way, but that ball is top-corner-bound and there’s nothing he can do about it.
I’ve now seen the penalty incident at the Stadium of Light, and it looks to me like the main reason Brobbey went down was that his right foot caught his left ankle, and he thus tripped himself up. He was, though, being bothered by Colwill, who made no attempt to play the ball and may well have made contact with that right leg before the self-trippage.
The Palace game is pure chaos. About 80 seconds after his goal Mac Allister is flinging himself around the Liverpool penalty area to block Timber’s shot.
GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-1 Liverpool (Mac Allister, 40 mins)
Szoboszlai whips in the ball from a right-wing free-kick, and Mac Allister escapes his marker, meets it at the near post, and sends a low header beyond Henderson!
Saved! Mitchell’s deep cross falls to Kamada, and unlike Barcola he manages to control his volley. But the shot flies too close to Alisson, who pushes it away!
What a miss! Szoboszlai’s cross finds Barcola beyond the far post, completely unmarked and able to watch the ball dip towards his instep and pick his spot! Unfortunately the spot he picks is approximately 40 rows back in the stand.
The ball came off a Palace player, and offside it is. An escape for Liverpool, who were controlling this game for a while but are certainly not dominating it currently.
Goal disallowed! Some penalty-area ping-pong ends with the ball at Strand Larsen’s feet, five yards out, and he turns it in! But he’s given offside! VAR will have a look at this, of course, and the question is who the ball came off …
Brentford’s Igor Thiago is sent off for “pushing an opponent in the face with force”. Chema Andres had been hassling him for about 20 seconds of constant mini-fouling, and eventually Thiago has had enough of it and gives him a push. His hand catches his opponent’s chin, he goes down clutching his forehead, and VAR does the rest. It wasn’t nothing, for sure, but neither was it what Chema Andres pretended it was.
It’s much more open now at Selhurst Park. Araujo goes into the book for a foul, and then a Liverpool counter is curtailed by a poor pass and a good interception from Wharton.
“Liverpool fan here, but still, surely a push is a push?” writes Ric Latham of that push on Barcola. “It wasn’t shoulder to shoulder, the defender wasn’t challenging for the ball, all he was doing was (successfully) preventing Barcola from getting his head anywhere near it. It’s a stone cold pen in either box, and saying otherwise just normalises the idea that players should get away with things like this because it wasn’t clear enough. Maddening.” In the time it takes to read this email Tony Harrington, the referee, gives two soft free-kicks for pushing or blocking and it’s the inconsistency that’s really maddening. There were two hands on his back, but I didn’t see the defender’s arms straighten as they would if there was a real shove going on.
Brighton move to second in the league! A cross from the right is kind of cleared, from which another cross from the right is kind of cleared, at which point Diego Gomez seizes possession, decides he’s had enough of crosses, and bangs a left-footer into the top corner from 25 yards!
Szoboszlai now crosses from the left, Gakpo, beyond the far post, cushions it back across goal and it runs across the goalline without anyone there to turn it in! Palace haven’t been out of their half for a while.
At Selhurst Park Barcola tries to meet a cross from the right and gets a fairly gentle push in the back as he does so. He goes down, but a penalty for that would be a bit much.
A disastrous goal for Ipswich! Chris Walton, the home side’s keeper, tries to take the ball past the onrushing Evanilson, fails, is dispossessed, and the rest is a formality!
A glimpse of goal for Palace, as Mitchell’s driven cross is met by Strand Larsen, but he can’t do much more than get a foot to it, and he deflects it limply wide of goal, from where it’s cleared for a throw-in.
I’m focusing, for now, on Crystal Palace v Liverpool, where Isak has just had half a chance, but rather than racing onto the ball he rather meandered up to it, and his shot then hit a defender.
Fabian Hurzeler on what makes Brighton good: “Brilliant at the basics. That’s our foundation. That’s what made us strong and hopefully will make us strong in the future. It’s not about first outplaying the opponent, it’s about outworking the opponent.”
Marco Rose is asked to identify Ipswich’s threat to Bournemouth today, and his response is, I have to say, vicious: “They want to win the game, I’m quite sure. It’s a nice ground.”
Hello world! We have four intriguing Premier League matches ahead of us today, with the teams currently fourth (Chelsea) and sixth (Liverpool) in the table playing away to the teams in 20th (Sunderland) and 19th (Crystal Palace), while the early afternoon’s big clash, between Brighton and Brentford, gives us the prospect of Brighton – with more than a quarter of the season played mind you – moving to second in the table. Plus, bubbling away in the background, half a game in the Scottish Premiership, the best part of three in the WSL and a side-order of FA Cup action. So, and to summarise, welcome! Here are the 2pm Premier League fixtures:
Brighton v Brentford
Crystal Palace v Liverpool
Ipswich Town v Bournemouth
Sunderland v Chelsea
And then at 4.30pm:
Manchester United v Aston Villa

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.title: Iran suggests blasts are not US attacks as both sides report ships hit
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.author: Katherine Hearst
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Iran suggests blasts are not US attacks as both sides report ships hit
Iranian media suggested explosions in southern Iran on Saturday evening were related to Iranian military activities rather than US strikes while both sides reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iranian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait.
President Donald Trump had hinted at renewing major attacks on Iran after last week's US midterm elections but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation, which Iran has said it would respond to by striking US and Israeli targets.
Both sides have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.
Iran's state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iranian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said two vessels had hit mines and a third had caught fire.
The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait.
Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on November 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets.
Reporting by Reuters

‘Spiritual darkness’: US ambassador to Israel says critics of Iran war are blinded by Satan
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has drawn criticism after saying that critics of US war on Iran are "in spiritual darkness" and claiming that those who disagree with intervention have been blinded by Satan.
Huckabee's comments were posted online over the weekend, attracting backlash from conservative commentators who called for him to be removed from his role as a diplomat.
The comments were made during a live interview with Israeli commentator Amir Tsarfati on The Anchor Podcast.
In the interview published on October 23 by Behold Israel, Tsarfati asked Huckabee to comment on the attitude of European governments towards US military action against Iran. He asked if there was a "mental issue" or a "spiritual issue."
“I think it's a spiritual issue,” Huckabee replied.
“I know it sounds a little funny for an ambassador to be talking like this, but look, I see this as spiritual darkness, spiritual blindness.”
He continued: “Because Satan has blinded the minds of those and has captured their thinking.”
“I really do believe that there is something deeper than just the obvious geopolitical issues at bay,” he added.

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has drawn criticism after saying that critics of US war on Iran are "in spiritual darkness" and claiming that those who disagree with intervention have been blinded by Satan.

“I know it sounds a little funny for an ambassador to be talking like this, but look, I see this as spiritual darkness, spiritual blindness.”

In a conversation about how Iran is a threat to the US and Israel, Huckabee also castigated European governments for being sceptical of any US intervention.
Andrew Day, a senior editor of The American Conservative, attacked Huckabee’s comments. He said it was inappropriate for a US ambassador to talk like that about those who are against the war.

Other social media users also called for Huckabee's removal from his diplomatic position.
Huckabee, a former Arkansas governor and evangelical Christian, has been a prominent supporter of Israel.
The remarks come amid continuing debate in the United States over the war and its political consequences.
Republican loss
Iran's Armed Forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi said the Republican Party's losses in the US midterm elections reflected Washington's failure to defeat Iran.
“The political and electoral developments in the United States, and the successive defeats of the Trump administration and its allies in various arenas, are less the result of superficial fluctuations in domestic politics than a reflection of a larger, undeniable reality: defeat in the face of a powerful Iran's will,” Shekarchi said, according to Iranian media.
He said the United States was a victim of “strategic attrition”, domestic crises and battlefield defeats, adding that the setbacks had shaken the foundations of US power.
“This strategic defeat stands as living proof of the fact that the global balance of power will never be shaped to the advantage of hegemonic powers,” he said.
The remarks followed a major Republican setback in the midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
President Donald Trump acknowledged that the war with Iran had played a part in his party's losses, although he continued to defend his decision to launch the military campaign.

What is happening in the occupied West Bank?
Three Palestinians have been wounded after being severely beaten with clubs by Israeli settlers near Salfit city in the central occupied West Bank, Wafa reports, citing local sources.
According to the sources, the group were attacked in the Wadi al-Shaer area, and suffered severe wounds to their heads, abdomens and lower spines, with one of them sustaining a broken jaw.
Meanwhile, in the town of Sinjil, northeast of Ramallah, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians farmers attempting to gather the olive harvest, seizing one of their vehicles.
In Jerusalem, the Israeli authroities issued demolition and stop-work notices for four residential and agricultural structures in the community of Abu al-Nuwar, near the town of al-Eizariya.
The Palestinian-run Jerusalem Governorate said this comes just days after the authorities announced the closure of the only read leading to Abu al-Nuwar, as well as the nearby al-Wadi al-A'raj and al-Muntar areas.
Meanwhile, Al Jazeera reports that Israel deported 14 western activists who were attempting to protect Palestinians as they harvested their olives. The Human Rights Defenders Fund said the group were arrested on Friday near Ramallah after being atacked by Israeli settlers.
October has seen an unprecedented surge in Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians attempting gather the olive harvest compared to previous years. OCHA documented 377 olive-harvest-related settler attacks across the West Bank between September 1 and November 2, 2026, outstripping the total recorded during a any previous olive harvest season.

Augmentation du Smic : un petit parfum de Mai-68
« On peut augmenter le Smic à condition de ne pas nuire à l’emploi. » À la veille de l’ouverture de la Conférence sociale, le ministre du Travail, Jean-Pierre Farandou, a mis en garde. Le mieux évidemment serait de ne pas l’augmenter du tout, ce que dit le patronat.
Au XIXe siècle, on mettait en garde au sujet de la suppression du travail des enfants, par exemple. À l’époque du Front populaire à propos des congés payés, etc. Bien sûr les temps changent.
Mais en ces jours qui par certains côtés ont un petit parfum de Mai-68, on peut rappeler qu’avec une économie à l’arrêt pendant plus d’un mois, 13 millions de travailleurs en grève, le Smic avait été augmenté, avec les accords de Grenelle, de 35 %…
Et s’il advenait que quelques petites ou moyennes entreprises en soient affectées pourquoi ne pas faire appel à une grande et belle solidarité inter-patronale. « Les champions du CAC 40 affichent des performances éclatantes », titrait vendredi Le Figaro économie, avec pour beaucoup d’entre eux des profits et des bénéfices records en hausse de 30 %.
Le journal des intelligences libres
« C’est par des informations étendues et exactes que nous voudrions donner à toutes les intelligences libres le moyen de comprendre et de juger elles-mêmes les événements du monde. »
Tel était « Notre but », comme l’écrivait Jean Jaurès dans le premier éditorial de l’Humanité, le 18 avril 1904. 122 ans plus tard, il n’a pas changé.

Je veux en savoir plus !

https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/mythe/t.title: « Trois pièces » de Jean-Pierre Sarrazac : coudre les vieux mythes à ceux d’aujourd’hui
https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/mythe/t.author: Jean-Pierre Léonardini
https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/mythe/t.text:
« Trois pièces » de Jean-Pierre Sarrazac : coudre les vieux mythes à ceux d’aujourd’hui
On doit à Jean-Pierre Sarrazac, maître en études théâtrales formé au contact de Bernard Dort, nombre d’ouvrages importants, tels, entre autres, L’Avenir du drame. Écritures dramatiques contemporaines (Circé Poche) ou Poétique du drame moderne (Seuil). Il a ainsi approfondi les connaissances sur Strindberg, Brecht, Beckett, Bernard-Marie Koltès…
Il a mis au jour les fécondes notions de rhapsodie et de drame-de-la-vie, en prônant la nécessité de la parabole, qu’il illustre dans ses œuvres théâtrales. Dès 1976, c’était Lazare lui aussi rêvait d’Eldorado, mise en scène de Thierry Bosc.
Depuis, plus d’une vingtaine de ses pièces ont été montées, dans des réalisations, notamment pour la France, d’Olivier Perrier, Jean-Louis Hourdin, Christian Schiaretti, Claude Yersin ou Jacques Lassalle… Aujourd’hui, Jean-Pierre Sarrazac publie Trois pièces1.
Dieu et Satan réitèrent le calvaire de Job, en la personne de J.B., chômeur alcoolique.
La première, Ajax, met en jeu la figure allusive du guerrier homérique presque aussi fort qu’Achille. Son nom ne sera que murmuré, lors de son retour au village natal en ruines, face à la jeune femme horrifiée par les massacres qu’il a orchestrés. Des voix invisibles commentent un dialogue sans merci.
En voilà une parabole, issue d’un antique récit à l’usage de nos jours. La Fin des possibilités en est une autre. J’avais eu la chance d’assister, à Lisbonne, en 2015, à la mise en scène de cette pièce en langue portugaise par les soins de Fernando Mora Ramos. Dieu et Satan (dit l’Adversaire), réitèrent le calvaire de Job en la personne de J.B., chômeur alcoolique et suicidaire qui les met en échec…
Dans La Boule d’or, enfin, nous voici trente ans après Mai-68, dans l’amère désillusion d’intellectuels orphelins d’une révolution qui n’a pas eu lieu. Un grand écrivain, une journaliste qui a rompu les amarres avec l’organe de presse qui devait tout changer, un journaliste qui y est resté, une jeune stagiaire objet de désirs, l’imprécateur, qui tend un piège à tous…
Les ombres portées de Sartre et de Nizan surplombent l‘affaire. Une œuvre forte, à l’imaginaire ancré tout près de la Sorbonne où Sarrazac a enseigné, non loin de La joie de lire, la librairie de François Maspero en ces temps d’effervescence.
La Boule d’or, qui a été montée jusqu’au Brésil, témoigne à l’envi du talent singulier de Jean-Pierre Sarrazac, qui sait coudre aussi bien les vieux mythes à ceux du jour, sans jamais perdre de vue le caractère indispensable d’une éthique d’écriture au-dessus de tout soupçon. Théâtrologue et auteur dramatique à la fois. L’espèce est rarissime. C’est à noter.
Trois pièces, 226 pages, 15 euros, Circé Théâtre.
Au plus près de celles et ceux qui créent
L’Humanité a toujours revendiqué l’idée que la culture n’est pas une marchandise, qu’elle est une condition de la vie politique et de l’émancipation humaine.
Face à des politiques culturelles libérales, qui fragilisent le service public de la culture, le journal rend compte de la résistance des créateurs et de tous les personnels de la culture, mais aussi des solidarités du public.
Les partis pris insolites, audacieux, singuliers sont la marque de fabrique des pages culture du journal. Nos journalistes explorent les coulisses du monde de la culture et la genèse des œuvres qui font et bousculent l’actualité.
Aidez-nous à défendre une idée ambitieuse de la culture !
Je veux en savoir plus !

Could Iraq’s Kurdish region return to two separate administrations?
A political impasse between the KRG and PUK threatens to break up the semiautonomous northern region into zones of governance.
Disagreements between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) over the formation of a new government have led to the threat of two rival administrations emerging in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, analysts say.
The dispute between the two dominant political forces in the semiautonomous Kurdistan Regional Government, which traditionally has operated under a power-sharing agreement, escalated after a parliamentary session was held last week in Erbil without the PUK’s participation.
PUK leader Bafel Talabani responded by withdrawing his party from the government, and a threat is growing that a rival administration could be formed in the party’s Sulaimaniyah base.
Independent Kurdish politician Yasin Aziz said the latest developments have deepened the historical divisions between the KDP and PUK.
“I believe the spectre of two administrations in Kurdistan is now very close, and the outlines of such a scenario are becoming clear. … The events have been painful and rapid. The differences between the two parties were significant and have now led to a breakdown in relations,” Aziz told Al Jazeera.
“There had been hopes that the two sides would reach an agreement, but activating parliament without the PUK deepened the divisions between the KDP and PUK.”
The KDP, which is led by Massoud Barzani, is the biggest party in the region, and its strongholds are in Erbil and Dohuk.
Two powers
Since the first Gulf War in 1990 and 1991 and the establishment of a US-led “no-fly zone” in northern Iraq, Iraq’s Kurds have largely governed themselves, separate from the national government in Baghdad.
The Iraqi Constitution enacted after the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq recognised the northern Kurdish region as a federal entity with its own legislative, executive and judicial powers.
There is a historical precedent for the possible separation of powers in this region between two rival authorities. When a conflict erupted between elements of the KDP and PUK in the 1990s, the two parties formed separate local governments in Erbil and Sulaimaniyah, respectively.
While there have been no recent violent flare-ups between the two parties, political distrust remains deep.
During the sixth parliamentary elections in the region on October 20, 2024, the KDP won 39 seats and the PUK 23. This left a 16-seat gap between the two parties.
But the KDP’s ability to form a new government was still dependent on reaching an agreement with the PUK and other parties, such as the New Generation Movement, which secured 15 seats in the last election.
The PUK has so far refused to collaborate, so after a two-year wait, the KDP reactivated the regional parliament on Wednesday without its rivals.
Divisions but no conflict
Although the rivalry between the two parties is longstanding, Aziz argued that the current crisis is more serious and deeply rooted than previous political disputes.
“Given the political stubbornness of both parties, I do not expect an agreement or understanding to be reached soon,” he said. “Both sides must make concessions to each other. The party willing to make greater concessions will demonstrate greater concern for the Kurdistan region.”
Aziz was clear in laying blame for the deepening divide.
“The responsibility for deepening this conflict lies with the leaderships of Kurdistan’s two main parties,” he said. “Their failure to recognise the risks posed by continuing these disputes is one of the reasons we have reached this point.”
Subhi Mandalawi, a member of the KDP, blamed the current impasse on the refusal of the PUK to form a new government with the KDP.
“Following the Kurdistan parliamentary elections, the PUK delayed the formation of the new government. They were counting on the KDP being unable to secure the legal quorum needed to convene a parliamentary session,” Mandalawi told Al Jazeera. “But we held a parliamentary session without the PUK in 2018 as well, and they subsequently joined the government and parliament.”
Mandalawi insisted that the door remains open for the PUK and other political parties but warned that prolonged divisions would lead to deeper problems for the Kurdish region.
“Continuing to obstruct legislative institutions two years after the elections is unacceptable and harms the Kurdistan region domestically, regionally and internationally,” he said.
“Threatening to divide the Kurdistan region is a hasty, ill-considered and unrealistic decision. No party leader can take such a step, and the PUK would be the biggest loser if it went ahead with it.”
Despite the differences, there is little risk of a return to conflict between the two parties. “We are brothers, and there can be no fighting among us,” Mandalawi said.
Separation threats
Mahmood Khoshnaw, a senior PUK official, said the KDP’s decision to convene parliament without his party has worsened political tensions in the region.
“Activating parliament without the PUK represents a departure from the principle of partnership and from political realities, and there will be consequences. If a prime minister is appointed in Erbil, we will take the same step in Sulaimaniyah. Whatever the KDP does, we will do the same in Sulaimaniyah,” Khoshnaw warned.
“The situation in the Kurdistan region is heading towards chaos unless the crisis is addressed rationally and realistically. Activating parliament without reaching an understanding with the PUK has had a negative impact on relations between the two parties.”
Despite this, there are questions about whether Sulaimaniyah could legally separate from the Kurdish regional government.
Ramadan Albadran, an independent political analyst and constitutional affairs expert, said the dispute is not a constitutional issue about the KDP’s convening of parliament but a deep political crisis with the potential to create security repercussions for the region.
The Iraqi constitution also provides no mechanism for dividing the region into zones of influence between the KDP and PUK.
“If the PUK moves to separate Sulaimaniyah from the Kurdistan region, that would not be a legal or constitutional act,” Albadran said.
“If it takes place without a mandate from the elected Kurdistan Regional Government, it would be closer to an act of rebellion since there is no legal provision permitting withdrawal from or the dismantling of a region in this manner.”

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: US datacenter demand spurs increased fossil fuel pipeline projects as rules are discarded
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Tom Perkins
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Datacenters are spurring a boom in fossil fuel pipeline projects at a time when the Trump administration is gutting rules that protect from disasters along the lines, a new review of federal records shows.
The report, compiled by the Environmental Integrity Project, also found pipelines are being built to meet demand for natural gas exports fueled by wars in Ukraine and Iran. Federal records identified almost 200 pipeline projects that are proposed or in the works, and would collectively span 17,000 miles (27,000km).
Not only has the Trump administration targeted laws that protect the environment and human health from pipelines’ risks, it has also pledged not to enforce regulations around them, the report adds.
The findings bring into focus a little-considered environmental threat in artificial intelligence and datacenter proliferation – the US already records about 1.7 pipeline accidents, spills, fires or explosions per day, and these projects would almost certainly lead to more.
The pipelines could help supply the at least 98 gas-fired power plants proposed to serve datacenters, and, if all the lines are completed, they would transport about 40% more natural gas daily than what the system carries today.
“This is the largest boom in a couple decades … and it coincides with all this deregulation,” Alexandra Shaykevich, research manager with the Environmental Integrity Project, said. “That’s concerning because the pipelines do usually operate safely, but they can leak and explode, and so there are big risks for communities across the United States.”
Most of the pipelines would carry natural gas across 42 states, though many of them are concentrated in several fossil fuel-producing regions. About 42 are in or cross Texas, 27 are in Louisiana, and nine each are in Pennsylvania and Illinois.
Advocates say they’re especially worried because of the wide-ranging attacks on foundational environmental protections, from the Clean Water Act to the Endangered Species Act, that until recently have been wielded to stop the riskiest projects, protect from accidents or hold polluters accountable.
The report states that over 25% of the projects have requested an expedited environmental review, and the administration is largely using legally dubious mechanisms to push them through, like invoking the “energy emergency”. That has accelerated permit approvals, reduced the scope of environmental studies, and limited public and community input, the report alleges.
Meanwhile, the administration has used the Defense Production Act to push through projects over the objections of states. In March, it jump-started the Santa Ynez oil pipeline in Santa Barbara, California, despite the state shutting it down in 2015 following a major spill that harmed about 150 miles (240km) of coastline. The act is also being used to attempt to ram through controversial plans for the 125-mile (200km) Constitution pipeline that would run from Pennsylvania to upstate New York, which the latter has opposed.
The Trump administration in January issued a memo stating that it would “refrain from taking any enforcement action” against companies that violated Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration regulations. By 2025, it had already cut the average number of enforcement actions initiated in half, recording only 117.
The administration is also raising the risk of accidents and explosions by allowing companies to increase the pressure of pipelines in densely populated areas and letting them conduct fewer pressure tests, the report alleges.
It has made changes like this despite the regularity of accidents, including some that are deadly. The report points to a March 2023 disaster in which a crack in a gas pipeline in West Reading, Pennsylvania, caused an explosion in a chocolate factory that killed seven workers and injured 10 others. Last month, two workers were killed when a New Mexico pipeline exploded.
The pipelines could also destroy thousands of acres of federally protected wetlands. At least 81 of the projects are expected to damage more than 19,000 acres (7,700 hectares) of federally protected wetlands, the report found. This also comes as the Trump administration attempts to strip 94% of federal wetland protections.
The dangers of this are felt in south-west Louisiana, which holds a large concentration of pipelines because of the high number of export terminals along the Mississippi River. These already cut through and harmed sensitive wetlands and fishing grounds, said James Hiatt, executive director of For a Better Bayou.
“The people who live here carry the risks and bear the burden while the profits go elsewhere,” Hiatt said.

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/bande-de-g.title: « Nous vivons cette épreuve chaque hiver » : à Gaza, des dizaines de milliers de réfugiés privés d’abris après des pluies diluviennes
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/bande-de-g.author: La rédaction avec AFP
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/bande-de-g.text:
Des pluies diluviennes dans la bande de Gaza ont entraîné l’inondation de dizaines de milliers de tentes de personnes déplacées, les privant d’abri, et faisant plusieurs blessés, ont indiqué ce samedi 8 novembre les autorités locales.
Le génocide, ce n’est pas que les bombes et la famine. C’est aussi empêcher les survivants de se protéger du froid, des rats et des maladies. Environ « 70 000 tentes abritant des dizaines de milliers de personnes déplacées ont été inondées durant la première journée » à cause d’une dépression qui touche le territoire palestinien, a indiqué le bureau de presse du gouvernement contrôlé par le Hamas ce 8 novembre.
« Des dizaines de murs et de toits fissurés se sont effondrées, faisant des blessés, dont certains dans un état grave » à travers la bande de Gaza, complète la même source. Depuis le début de la matinée, des centaines de familles ont été vues en train de fuir les camps de déplacés inondés dans le centre et le nord de la bande de Gaza, ainsi que dans la ville de Gaza.
La Défense civile du territoire a reçu plus de 1 500 appels d’urgence pendant la nuit, selon son porte-parole, qui précise à l’AFP que ses équipes opéraient « sans aucun équipement ni moyens ». L’organisme de premiers secours, qui opère sous l’autorité du Hamas, ne peut « pas faire face seul aux conséquences de cette dépression », a insisté le porte-parole, qui a « lancé un appel d’urgence à la communauté internationale et aux organisations humanitaires ».
Une énième catastrophe humanitaire à Gaza
« Nous n’avons pas pu sauver les matelas et tous nos vêtements ont été trempés », a déclaré à l’AFP Oum Mohamed al-Hersh, 45 ans, qui vit avec sa famille dans une tente dans l’ouest de Gaza. « Nous vivons cette épreuve chaque hiver. » « Mes enfants me demandent où nous allons dormir ce soir et je n’ai pas de réponse », a confié Maryam Odeh, habitante de Deir al-Balah de 34 ans, qui se désole de « ne plus savoir comment (les) protéger ».
Khaled al-Najjar, 41 ans, s’inquiète lui aussi pour sa famille, en raison du risque d’effondrement des tentes et « du froid et des maladies qui se propagent ». Dans un communiqué, la coalition des organisations de la société civile palestinienne a mis en garde contre le risque de propagation de maladies et « la catastrophe » menaçant les habitants de Gaza. Elle a également appelé à « faire pression sur Israël pour que l’aide humanitaire puisse entrer sans restriction ».
L’Autorité palestinienne, basée à Ramallah, a appelé la communauté internationale à prendre des mesures immédiates, affirmant que la guerre menée par Israël à Gaza avait aggravé les conditions de vie déjà désastreuses dans cette région, rapporte l’agence officielle Wafa.
Selon Mustapha Qazzaat, conseiller municipal de Gaza et responsable de la commission d’urgence de la bande de Gaza, les autorités israéliennes empêchent l’entrée de maisons préfabriquées destinées à héberger les personnes déplacées et ont limité l’entrée des tentes.
Le territoire palestinien « a besoin de 200 000 caravanes de toute urgence, ainsi que de matériel pour déblayer les décombres des maisons et des bâtiments détruits, dégager les artères principales et rétablir d’urgence l’électricité et le chauffage », a-t-il déclaré à l’AFP.
Pour une information libre sur la Palestine
Nous avons été l’un des premiers médias français à défendre le droit des Palestiniens à disposer d’un État viable dans le respect des résolutions de l’ONU. Et nous avons inlassablement défendu la paix au Proche-Orient. Aidez-nous à continuer de vous informer sur ce qui se passe là-bas. Grâce à vos dons.
Je veux en savoir plus !

Watch: Footage shows Palestinian families struggling to drain rainwater from their tents
8 November 2026 10:45 GMT
Footage shot by photojournalist Mahmoud Hamda shows displaced Palestinian families wading through the rain water that has inundated their tents.
Young children can be seen ankle deep in murky water, trying to sweep it with brooms from their makeshift homes.
Heavy rains in the territory have deluged around 70,000 tents. Scarce aid- particularly shelter materials like tent poles and mobile homes- has left Palestinians exposed to the elements for the fourth winter in a row.
Israel's razing of Gaza's infrastructure- including water and sewage networks- and its healthcare system, means that Palestinians are particularly vulnerable to the onset of disease.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe
‘Terrorism’ investigation launched after government officials say suspect likely influenced by far-right ideology.
Poland has begun two days of national mourning after an armed man killed six people in central Krakow, as the national prosecutor’s office opened a “terrorism” investigation.
The 24-year-old Polish suspect opened fire on Saturday in the heart of Krakow’s historic city centre. A British national was among those killed, according to police, and nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia were among the 15 wounded, authorities told the PAP news agency.
Three more bodies were later found at the suspect’s home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about 150km (93 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.
The suspect was also wounded during police action and is in critical condition in hospital.
Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said on social media on Sunday it had “launched an investigation today into yesterday’s attack in Krakow”, adding it was probing “the killing of six people … using a firearm, and the attempted murder of many others, including police officers, this act constituting a terrorist offence”.
Daniel Prokopowicz, a spokesperson for the office, said it was “highly likely” that the killings in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski and Krakow were carried out by the same person, but that investigations were ongoing.
According to media reports, the suspect, Michal O, had a valid gun licence and no prior criminal record.
Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski stated the attacker was influenced by far-right and ultranationalist ideologies and views.
Meanwhile, Krakow’s main market square and the surrounding streets remained closed on Sunday, with police allowing only essential service workers.
Many nearby cafes were closed and flags at the city hall were at half-mast. Mourners placed candles in several locations in the area.
The traditional hourly trumpet call from St Mary’s church on the square was suspended for 12 hours to commemorate the dead, the first time this has happened since 1939, the Polish Press Agency reported.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/saudi.author: MEE staff

Saudi Aramco tower damaged after Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh
A building belonging to Saudi state oil giant Aramco was damaged in Riyadh on Sunday as Saudi Arabia reported a series of missile attacks launched by Yemen’s Houthi movement.
An official at Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry said Aramco's administrative building sustained minor damage after falling shrapnel struck it.
No injuries or deaths were reported, the official said, adding that the relevant authorities had responded and taken the necessary measures.
A Reuters witness reported seeing windows blown out across several floors of the Aramco Tower in the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD), one of the Saudi capital’s main business districts.
The damage followed reports of loud explosions in Riyadh and an early-warning alert issued by Saudi Civil Defence. Authorities later said the danger had passed.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh on Sunday.
It later reported intercepting two cruise missiles in the capital and the kingdom’s southern region.
Earlier, coalition spokesperson Major-General Turki al-Maliki said another ballistic missile launched towards the Eastern Province had been intercepted.
The developments came amid escalating fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, following the collapse of a 2022 truce and renewed military operations in Yemen.
The latest missile interceptions came a day after the Houthi-run Health Ministry said Saudi-led coalition air strikes had killed at least 33 people, including eight women and 13 children, in the village of al-Shariyah near Sanaa.
Health Ministry spokesperson Anees al-Asbahi said at least 39 others were wounded in Saturday’s attacks, which he said targeted homes, roads, paramedics and Civil Defence teams in the Bani Hushaish district, east of the capital.
There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition on the reported strikes, and Al Jazeera said it could not independently verify the casualty figures.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree also claimed that the coalition had carried out 105 air strikes and missile attacks over 24 hours, targeting Sanaa and seven other governorates.
He put the total number of attacks since the latest escalation began at 4,369.
Saree said the Houthis had carried out six operations targeting Aramco facilities, Riyadh airport and Saudi military positions on both sides of the border.
The latest escalation follows a campaign launched by Yemen’s internationally recognised government last month to retake territory held by the Houthis, including Sanaa. The group has controlled the capital since 2014.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity
About 850,000 people lose power after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure in Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv.
More than 600,000 people in Ukraine’s eastern Dnipropetrovsk region are without electricity after a Russian overnight attack on an energy facility, a Ukrainian energy provider has said.
Residents across the Pavlohrad, Samarivskyi, Kamianske and Dnipro districts, as well as the city of Dnipro, faced electricity outages on Sunday, power company DTEK wrote in a Telegram post.
Engineers were at the scene attempting to restore the damaged facility, but “repairs are being complicated by repeated attacks”, DTEK said.
Ukraine is bracing for yet another harsh winter of war as Russia ramps up daily aerial attacks, raining down drones and missiles on the power network.
Another 250,000 Ukrainians were left without power in the Kharkiv region in northeastern Ukraine on Sunday after Russia struck an infrastructure facility there.
“No casualties have been reported, ” said Mykola Baksheyev, mayor of Zlatopil city, on Telegram.
“Power engineers are currently working to repair the damage; however, the exact timeframe for restoring the electricity supply remains unknown.”
The attacks came a day after Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy said a massive attack on energy facilities had plunged residents in five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying attacks to put pressure on Kyiv at United States-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.
Russia’s Ministry of Defence stated on its Telegram channel that its forces will “continue to carry out strikes against Ukrainian fuel and energy infrastructure facilities” that they say are used to aid the Ukrainian military.

La vague bleue est telle que Trump n’a pu contester les résultats. La répudiation du président nationaliste est d’une ampleur tellurique. Désormais majoritaires au Congrès, les démocrates ont les coudées franches pour concrétiser leur triomphe, à savoir entraver les politiques et nominations trumpistes et mener le combat contre les inégalités inscrit dans leur campagne. À deux ans des présidentielles, le parti de l’âne sait ce qui arrive à ceux qui ne tiennent pas leurs promesses.
Donald Trump vient de perdre sa quatrième élection en cinq scrutins et ce sera la dernière. La Constitution lui interdit de se présenter pour un troisième mandat et aucun élu au Congrès n’aurait l’idée saugrenue de voter un amendement visant à changer cet état de fait. Sans doute encore moins dans ses propres rangs. Apparu comme un faiseur de miracles au sein d’un parti qui se voyait condamné par les évolutions démographiques du pays, le milliardaire a envoyé par le fond le Grand Old Party d’Abraham Lincoln.
La répudiation est d’une ampleur tellurique. Les républicains perdent le vote populaire par une marge insensée : autour de quinze millions de voix (Barack Obama en avait dix d’avance en 2008 sur John McCain). https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
With 99 percent of votes counted, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s party wins 31 percent nationally.
South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) party faces a major setback after last week’s municipal elections, leaving it in a weak position in coalition talks to form city governments.
With 99 percent of the votes counted on Sunday, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s ANC had 31 percent nationally against 25 percent for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA).
That represents a drop of roughly 14 percentage points from its 2021 local elections performance.
Former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party won about 10 percent of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest of the ballots were split between hundreds of smaller parties.
Final results are expected to be announced at 6pm (16:00 GMT) on Sunday.
While still the largest party in South Africa, the ANC’s support has steadily eroded as voters grow increasingly frustrated with corruption and the party’s failure to tackle unemployment, which tops 34 percent more than three decades after the end of apartheid.
Failures in basic services, such as water and electricity, have also contributed to the ANC’s vote share falling in local elections over the past 15 years.
The party failed to win an outright majority in any of the eight major metro areas, including Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Coalition talks
Since no party won more than 50 percent of the votes in many cities, including South Africa’s commercial hub Johannesburg, the ANC and DA will have to team up or hash it out with smaller parties to form municipal governments.
Parties will have 14 days to negotiate before city councils are formed.
ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the result “catastrophic” for the ANC but said the party would not go begging for positions when coalition talks begin soon.
“When the people tell us we have fallen short, … the honest answer is not to argue with them but to go home and put our house in order,” Mbalula said on Saturday.
In Johannesburg, the DA led the count with about 35 percent of the votes, compared with 20 percent for the ANC.
That could give DA veteran Helen Zille, who campaigned on fixing potholes and leaking water pipes, a good chance of becoming mayor, depending on the coalition agreements reached.
The DA said in a statement that it would initiate coalition discussions with “political parties that share a commitment to clean and accountable government, rooting out corruption, service delivery for all, the rule of law, and non-racialism”.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?
Israel’s former military chief has been given the first opportunity to form a government after an inconclusive election amid deep political divisions.
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been given the opportunity to form a new government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections, raising the possibility of an end to his long tenure in power.
President Isaac Herzog selected the former military chief on Saturday, following consultations with political parties. Eisenkot has 28 days to cobble together a coalition to form a government. If he fails to form a new administration within that period, he can seek a 14-day extension.
“Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, posted on X.
However, the 66-year-old faces a difficult challenge as many of the opposition parties hold sharply conflicting positions on national security, religion and the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has a 61-seat majority in Israel’s 120-member parliament, the Knesset.
As a result, Arab-led parties hold a potentially decisive role in determining who governs Israel, even as Eisenkot and his prospective partners refuse to rely on their support.
So what do we now know about Eisenkot’s possible paths to power, and can he succeed in unseating Netanyahu?
Can Eisenkot unite Israel’s divided opposition?
Eisenkot’s potential coalition spans his Yashar party, the centre-left Democrats led by Yair Golan, Naftali Bennett’s centre-right Together party and Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu (Israel Our Home).
Overall, they control 48 seats, well short of a majority.
Arab-led parties Ra’am (United List) and the Joint List (comprising three parties – Hadash, Ta’al and Balad) – jointly holding 19 seats – have endorsed Eisenkot’s attempt to form a government. Their backing would give the broader anti-Netanyahu camp a combined 67 seats.
Hadash is an Arab-Jewish party, Ta’al advocates for the rights of Palestinian citizens of Israel, and Balad demands equal rights for all its citizens.
However, Eisenkot has ruled out bringing Arab parties into his government, while Lieberman has repeatedly rejected forming a minority administration dependent on their support. Golan’s Democrats have been more willing to partner with Ra’am and the Joint List.
“We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” Golan said after the election.
How many seats does Netanyahu’s coalition have now?
Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition has fallen from the 64 seats it secured in 2022 to 53, eight seats short of a majority.
His Likud is the largest individual party with 27 seats, while Eisenkot’s Yashar won 21.
Netanyahu’s efforts to remain in power suffered a further setback when United Torah Judaism, a longtime ultra-Orthodox ally, declined to endorse him or any other candidate during consultations with Herzog.
While the decision hurts Netanyahu’s prospects of regaining power, it did not rule out the party supporting him in future coalition negotiations if their demands were met, particularly compulsory military service for ultra-Orthodox Jews, which they reject.
What is a minority government?
If Eisenkot is unable to put together a coalition, he could potentially lead a minority government backed by Arab parties from outside.
A minority government is formed when the parties holding cabinet positions do not collectively control a majority of seats in parliament. Instead, they depend on support from lawmakers outside the governing coalition to remain in power and pass legislation.
Eisenkot could establish such an administration with his four-party bloc relying on external parliamentary support from Ra’am and the Joint List.
Under this arrangement, the Arab-led parties would not necessarily receive cabinet positions or formally join the coalition.
They could instead negotiate policy concessions in exchange for their parliamentary support.
In 2021, Ra’am joined a government led by Bennett, becoming the first independent Arab party to participate in an Israeli governing coalition.
That administration collapsed after 18 months, mainly due to disagreements over the illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and Palestinian statehood. Most Israeli parties do not support the creation of a sovereign Palestinian state as part of the so-called two-state solution.
Netanyahu, who has been in power for most of the past 20 years, has openly rejected Palestinian statehood and has pushed settlement expansions that are the biggest hurdles in the realisation of Palestinian statehood. Settlements are considered illegal under international law.
What are the other possible paths to forming a government?
Beyond a minority government, Eisenkot could attempt to secure a parliamentary majority by bringing Israel’s two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, into his coalition.
Together, they hold 13 seats, which would give Eisenkot’s bloc exactly the 61 seats required for a majority.
However, such an alliance would require compromises over military conscription exemptions for ultra-Orthodox religious students, an issue that has long divided Israeli politics.
Eisenkot and his allies, particularly Lieberman, have criticised the exemptions. But Lieberman has recently indicated that he is open to compromise.
While United Torah Judaism has refused to endorse Netanyahu, Shas backed the beleaguered prime minister.
Another option would be a unity government involving Eisenkot’s Yashar, Bennett’s Together party, Lieberman’s Israel Our Home and Netanyahu’s Likud.
Such an alliance would command 67 seats, but would require Eisenkot and his partners to abandon their central election pledge to remove Netanyahu from power.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government within the required time, Herzog could give Netanyahu an opportunity to form a governing coalition.
Should both leaders fail, parliament could nominate another candidate. If no government emerges after a process lasting 100 days, Israelis could be heading to the polls again.
Why does this matter?
The negotiations could determine not only who becomes Israel’s next prime minister, but also which political parties control key ministries and shape policies on the economy, military conscription and the occupied Palestinian territory.
Several members of Eisenkot’s opposition bloc have previously held senior government positions, including in the coalition that removed Netanyahu from power in 2021.
Bennett, who served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022, has long opposed the establishment of a Palestinian state and advocated annexing large parts of the occupied West Bank.
During Israel’s 11-day war on Gaza in May 2021, Bennett, then an opposition politician, backed Netanyahu’s military offensive in the Palestinian enclave. More than 250 Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks.
Meanwhile, Lieberman served as finance minister in Bennett’s government and previously held the defence portfolio under Netanyahu.
He previously proposed swapping some Arab communities in Israel proper for Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank in the context of a final peace deal with the Palestinians.
Lieberman’s party backs illegal settlement expansion, including E1, and annexing all of Area C, 60 percent of the occupied West Bank already under full Israeli control. E1, which stands for East 1 settlement, is a 12sq km corridor with thousands of housing units. It will cut the West Bank into two parts.
Eisenkot himself served in Netanyahu’s wartime cabinet before leaving the government after disagreements over the conduct of the genocide in Gaza. He has not opposed the genocide but criticised Netanyahu for prioritising his political survival over security considerations.
He has called the idea of a Palestinian state “delusional”, and he supports “strengthening” illegal settlements.
Academic Neve Gordon says an Eisenkot government could bring notable changes to Israel’s domestic politics, particularly by reversing parts of Netanyahu’s judicial overhaul.
“If Eisenkot is able to establish a government, he will likely be able to stop the judicial overhaul by cancelling the legislation that the Netanyahu government put in place, particularly in relation to the way Supreme Court judges are chosen,” said the law professor at Queen Mary University of London.
Gordon also expects a new government to establish an independent inquiry into the October 7 attacks and potentially introduce legislation preventing politicians facing trial for serious offences from becoming prime minister.
Palestinian citizens of Israel, Gordon said, could also benefit if Arab-led parties support the government from outside the coalition.
“The government is likely to allocate funds to Palestinian towns, adding funds to neglected infrastructures, schools and the like, while also spending more money on policing in order to clamp down on crimes and the high murder rates,” he said.
When it comes to Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, Gordon expects far less change.
“Here the changes will be merely cosmetic,” he said, arguing that Eisenkot’s prospective coalition remains predominantly right-wing and opposed to Palestinian statehood.
Gordon suggested that a new government might attempt to restrain some Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, but questioned whether such efforts would succeed because of the close relationship between settlers and Israeli security forces.
“And I do not foresee any substantial change in policy in the Gaza Strip,” he said.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Messi becomes first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Messi becomes first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards
The Argentinian scored 26 goals in regular season, topping the charts and leading Inter Miami to the MLS Cup playoffs.
Lionel Messi has become the first player to win back-to-back Golden Boot awards in Major League Soccer after leading his club Inter Miami to a second-place finish in the Eastern Conference.
MLS defending champions Miami earned a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season on Saturday.
The Argentinian superstar did not score but set up the first two goals at Miami’s Nu Stadium, both from corners, to help secure home advantage for his club in the first two playoff rounds.
Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada’s brace soon after the break led to a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko’s late strike.
Runaway overall leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record for a season with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. At 23-3 with eight draws, Nashville won the East and broke the mark of 74 points set by Miami in 2024.
Miami finished second in the East on 60 points as third-place New England failed to take advantage of Inter’s draw with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando to end on 58.
At Miami, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring.
Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0.
De Paul made it three before half-time, but Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors early and bagged a second in the 55th minute.
In the 90th minute, Aloko bagged the equaliser, reacting first to the ball as Smalls’s shot ricocheted off the post.
A visibly frustrated Messi hit the post in stoppage time before Aloko came inches from bagging an unlikely winner with a thunderous shot into the outside netting.
Messi’s 26 goals this season were enough to make him the first to successfully defend the top goal-scoring honour. Petar Musa of Dallas was second with 22 goals but did not score in his club’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado.
The 39-year-old finished with 29 goals the previous season, becoming the second player in league history to score at least 25 times in back-to-back years.
Messi recently retired from international football after an illustrious 21-year career with the 2022 world champions, but recently signed a contract extension with the MLS club through 2028.
Inter Miami are the holders of the MLS Cup, which they won in Messi’s second season with the club in 2025.
Playoffs for this season’s MLS Cup begin on November 19.
Messi’s men will face Columbus to begin the MLS playoffs. Other East matchups send New England against Philadelphia, Charlotte against Chicago and top seed Nashville against the wild-card winner, Orlando or Cincinnati.
Columbus took advantage of the Cincinnati loss with a 4-3 victory at Chicago to finish seventh and avoid the wild-card round.
