https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Stimulant overdoses on the rise as opioid deaths decline, but treatment is complex
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Hannah Harris Green
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Overdoses involving stimulants are on the rise in many parts of the country, according to recently available data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, but experts say recognizing and responding to them is more complex when compared with opioid overdoses.
“The rate of overdose decline was not nearly what we expected” in California, said Dr Taylor Nichols, an emergency and addiction medicine physician based in Sacramento.
Nichols said that stimulants “filled the gap” left by declining fentanyl overdoses. Methamphetamine and cocaine are the most common illicit stimulants.
While fentanyl-involved overdose deaths dropped to pre-pandemic levels nationally for the first time in 2025, per provisional CDC overdose fatality data, deaths involving cocaine went up in 13 states and deaths involving methamphetamine went up in eight states. In some states, like Arizona, non-fatal stimulant overdoses are reaching record highs.
Public health messaging has been effective at teaching people to recognize opioid overdoses and respond to them with naloxone, but education about stimulant overdoses and how to handle them hasn’t been as clear-cut.
“As a bystander, it is a lot more challenging to decide whether something is a stimulant overdose when you compare to how clear-cut a true opioid overdose is,” said Stephen Murray, director of SafeSpot Overdose Hotline, a safety service for people using drugs alone run out of Boston medical center.
A former paramedic, Murray runs overdose response trainings for paramedics across the country. When someone’s breathing has slowed down dramatically or stopped, it’s a clear sign of opioid overdose, but stimulant overdoses vary widely.
“A stimulant overdose can be as simple as releasing too much stimulation into your brain and into your body,” said Nichols. Extreme overstimulation strains the heart and brain, leading to heart attacks and strokes.
Nichols and Murray both recommend learning how to recognize strokes and other stimulant overdose symptoms. The Be Fast mnemonic (Balance loss, Eyesight changes, Face droop, Arm [or leg] weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911) lays out signs of stroke. Stimulant-induced shortness of breath, seizure and chest pain also warrant immediate medical attention.
Calling 911 is advised for any overdose, but bystanders do successfully save lives using naloxone without involving medical professionals. There are no equivalent tools for bystanders witnessing a stimulant-induced heart attack, stroke or seizure. If someone loses consciousness during a stimulant overdose, it could indicate opioids are involved as well, and it is safe to use naloxone to reverse the possible opioid component.
High doses of stimulants are especially dangerous in hot climates.
“You can develop hyperthermia, where your body gets too hot, and that can end up resulting in significant brain damage or death,” Nichols explained. People using stimulants sometimes forget to eat or drink, but Murray said that a conscious effort to stay hydrated can prevent overheating.
Dalton Barrett, a paramedic and manager of opioid settlement funds in rural Edgecombe county, North Carolina, recommends getting stimulant overdose patients as calm as possible while waiting for an ambulance to arrive. That means getting rid of external stimulation, like music, bright lights and crowds.
“What we don’t want to happen is we get over there, and now they’re aggressive with the EMS staff, and now law enforcement’s coming, and the person gets tased or maced or put in handcuffs,” Barrett said. These kinds of altercations are distressing for patients, and can also make it harder for emergency responders to treat them.
Prolonged, sleepless stimulant binges can also lead to psychosis and paranoia.
“I have a history of meth and stimulant use, and have been in quasi-meth psychosis before,” Murray said. “Telling someone that [their delusion] is not happening doesn’t make it feel less real.” Murray instead suggests validating that the experience is scary. “If you’re preparing for an EMS arrival for someone you love, just make sure that that person isn’t going to be perceived as being threatening,” Murray said. This can mean calmly looking around the space and clearing anything that might appear incriminating, like a weapon.
Ideally, Murray said, emergency medical services and law enforcement coordinate to keep patients safe, especially when they need to be restrained. One way he recommends advocating for patients who are forcibly restrained is to make sure they’re receiving medical sedatives as well.
Most fatal stimulant overdoses also involve other substances, but Murray notes that older men with heart health problems are most at risk of dying from stimulants alone.
“The people who die have the American diet and lack of exercise sort of stuff going on. Then when you mix in high-potency stimulants, especially if people are injecting them, that is a deadly combination,” he said, adding that he wishes that people could talk openly with their doctors about their drug use and health, because broader strategies to improve heart health can also help prevent stimulant overdoses, even when someone continues to use stimulants. Still, drug criminalization and abstinence-only messaging make this difficult.
He continued: “It is really challenging for us to study how we could improve people’s health in this situation, because we just tell people not to use drugs, when we know that millions of people every year in the US spend billions of dollars on stimulants.”

https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/n.title: The efficiency trap: why optimising everything can backfire, badly
https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/n.author: Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend
https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/n.text:
We have all been there: packed shoulder to shoulder on the train while the person beside us coughs and sneezes. A protective flu jab offers some reassurance, but so does the thought that there will be a hospital bed for you, should you need it. Yet, in England, about 95% of adult hospital beds were occupied at the height of flu season last year.
If hospitals were hotels, that level of occupancy would be good business, and we would commend them for their efficiency. But do we really want a hospital to have so few beds in reserve that it’s just one bad flu week away from having to treat patients in corridors?
This is the subtle thing about efficiency. We usually assume that more of it must be better. But we can become so focused on improving one thing that we lose sight of the others. You can try to arrange your calendar so that every minute is accounted for, but you’ll soon start running over and end up behind. A gap between meetings might seem like inefficiency, but it’s what allows your schedule to recover when something unexpected happens.
Mathematicians have a name for the pursuit of efficiency. We call it optimisation. Give us something to minimise or maximise – cost, time, fuel, profit – and we will try to find the best possible answer. For most of human history, people optimised by common sense. But computers have enormously expanded what can be effectively tackled, from airline schedules to supply chains. The gains for society have been extraordinary. But there are at least three traps to beware of in the relentless pursuit of optimality.
The hospital bed story illustrated the first one: weakening a system’s robustness by squeezing out too much slack. An empty bed can be redundant on a quiet Tuesday night, but it’s somewhere precious to put the next patient when flu cases surge. If you judge a system by its performance under ordinary conditions, you can lose the ability to cope with extraordinarily challenging ones.
A second trap is having a too-narrow definition of “best”. Take the city of Milton Keynes. Designed by urban planners in the late 1960s, it has an American-style grid system. As the city began to be built out, roundabouts rather than traffic lights became a defining feature of its road junctions; today there are about 130 of them. The roundabouts were great for traffic flow, but they came with a now-notorious cost. Have you ever taken the coach from Oxford to Cambridge? An hour in, you get great views of Milton Keynes, but a busload of queasy passengers, as the coach negotiates one roundabout after another. Slow down, swing left, curve right, accelerate. It’s hard to appreciate the seamless merging of vehicles when your stomach is churning.
Traffic flow is important, to be sure. Engineers find it convenient to optimise because it’s relatively easy to measure. Passenger comfort, on the other hand, is harder to quantify. In a case like this, optimisation gives you the best answer to the question you asked, but can deliver unwelcome answers to questions you failed to consider.
A third trap appears when attempts to optimise collide. Even if every part of a system is acting optimally, the system as a whole may not. On 6 May 2010, US financial markets gave a dramatic demonstration of the effect. In the middle of an already falling market, the S&P 500 suddenly plunged another 5% in just five minutes. The whipsaw on the upside was even wilder; within 10 minutes, the market had recovered. Hundreds of individual securities briefly traded at absurdly low prices.
One trigger for these violent fluctuations was an automated program selling 75,000 futures contracts, worth more than $4bn. Other automated traders reacted nearly instantly. Then their responses fed back on one another, and liquidity evaporated. The algorithms’ actions may have been individually sensible in isolation, but they combined to produce collective turmoil.
Which brings us to artificial intelligence. AI is one of the most spectacular triumphs of optimisation in history. During training, enormous numbers of parameters are repeatedly adjusted so that a model gets better at predicting language, writing computer programs, answering scientific questions and giving legal advice. Unfortunately, AI now has the potential to make all three optimisation traps more treacherous than ever. The first trap – the urge to remove the slack – could tempt organisations to dispense with the human oversight that looks redundant in the age of quicker-witted algorithms. Why retain experienced staff when a machine can handle the routine chores? But in cutting that human capacity, you may lose the ability to spot and handle exceptional circumstances.
The second trap – a blinkered view of what “best” means – arises if we regard intelligence as whatever scores highest on a leaderboard. We are remarkably good at building AI systems that do well on measures such as user satisfaction, but we are finding it much harder to optimise them for judgment or empathy. Indeed, researchers have found that training algorithms on human preferences can encourage AI to sycophantically agree with us rather than tell us uncomfortable truths.
Then there is the third trap. AI systems are increasingly interacting with one another, often at blinding speeds and in vast numbers – especially in the era of agentic AI – and we worry that their interactions could generate unpredictable, dangerous behaviour. Recently, an OpenAI agent broke into a non-public Medicare statistics portal in Australia, while public logs suggested that hundreds of other agents were coordinating attempts to gain access to Australian government health data. Although those attempts have not been shown to be part of the Medicare breach, they certainly revealed something disturbing: hundreds of agents apparently working together in unauthorised ways. The concern here goes beyond what any given AI may or may not do; it’s about what happens when swarms of them join forces.
As optimisation becomes more powerful, avoiding these traps becomes more important. The challenge is not simply finding the best answer. It is deciding what “best” really means – and knowing what not to optimise away.
Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend are mathematics professors at Cornell University and the authors of Big Math (John Murray).
Further reading
The Efficiency Paradox: What Big Data Can’t Do by Edward Tenner (Vintage, £16.99)
The Unaccountability Machine: Why Big Systems Make Terrible Decisions (Profile, £11.99)
Optimal Illusions: The False Promise of Optimization by Coco Krumme (Bantam, £25.99)

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.title: NFL week nine: Jets v Chiefs, Rams v Commanders, Broncos v Panthers and more – updates
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.author: Graham Searles
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2.text:
Score updates
- Broncos 13-14 Panthers
- Cowboys 17-10 Colts
- Jets 12-21 Chiefs
- Lions 16-6 Dolphins
- Browns 6-6 Saints
- Giants 6-8 Eagles
- Rams 13-13 Commanders
Still tight as knicker elastic across most the NFL.
🏈 Bengals joint-top of AFC North with 34-17 win in Madrid
 
🏈 What do the midterms mean for the NFL? | Email Graham
 Updated 
Key events
Broncos 13-14 Panthers 0:21, 3rd quarter
Even Devon Key had no idea he had made an interception. He didn’t celebrate. Anyway the Broncos are driving and have a 1st down after a short throw to Pat Bryant. Denver need to go about 60 yards.
PICK! Broncos 13-14 Panthers 1:35, 3rd quarter
Ouch. Carolina are on the one-yard line after a blatant pass interference call on Jahdae Barron. They go for the pass on 1st down with some trickery but it doesn’t work out. Just dish it to Chuba, surely?! Hubbard gets denied, maybe not.
Wait!!!! Is that SEAN PAYTON’s music! The head coach challenges the previous play for an interception. The ball bounces off Tommy Trembles leg and then is just picked up by Devon Key before it hits the deck. It is going to be an interception. They are reviewing … it is!
What an insane sequence. They really should have run the ball on 1st down. Did Pete Carroll teach them nothing?
Broncos 13-14 Panthers 2:21, 3rd quarter
Carolina are starting to wear out Denver now with the running game. Chuba Hubbard runs straight over a defender for 10 yards. Young then finds Waller again and the Panthers are about 12 yards from the end zone. They are just playing lights out right now. The Broncos are in deep trouble.
- J Gibbs eight yard rush
On 4th and 1 the Lions swing for the fences and give it to their home run hitter Jahmyr Gibbs. I think those analogies make sense … anyway he speeds out wide to the right, finds the edge and races in for the score. That is Gibbs’ 11th touchdown of the season. He only needs two more to over take Terrell Davis on 61 scores in the first four seasons of a career. The Lions running back is something truly special.
Broncos 13-14 Panthers 6:20, 3rd quarter
Bryce Young is on fire right now. He hits John Metchie on the sideline with a perfectly timed pass then finds Jalen Coker with a quick release as he evades a sack. Just too good from the young quarterback. Carolina are at their own 40-yard line on 2nd down.
SACK! Broncos 13-14 Panthers 8:46, 3rd quarter
Denver are quickly into the 3rd and long and is rocked!!! Patrick Jones delays his pass rush and brings the QB down. This game has turned completely on its head and the crowd are loving it. Bryce Young will be out to extend the lead with 87 yards to travel.
TOUCHDOWN! Jets 12-21 Chiefs 10:20, 3rd quarter
- P Mahomes to T Kelce for one yard
Taylor Swift is enjoying that one. The tight end takes the shovel pass and smashes over for the score on 4th down. Jets need more than field goals now.
Denver keep tabs on Carolina in the red zone and bring up 3rd and 9. Young unleashes a fastball to Darren Waller who races from right to left across the face of the end zone. The big tight end leaps, comes down with it and Carolina have the lead!! The 34-year-old Waller seriously rolling back the years.
TOUCHDOWN! Rams 13-10 Commanders 11:29, 3rd quarter
- B Corum two yard rush
Another team struggling in the first half is off to the races after the break. Blake Corum finishes off the eight play, 69 yard drive.
Broncos 13-7 Panthers 14:04, 3rd quarter
A 21-yard pass to Darren Waller and 10-yard rush from Chuba Hubbard get Carolina off to an electric start after the break. They keep the momentum rolling with a 10-yard throw to Mitchell Evans. 25 yards to go for the lead in three plays.
It’s GOOD! Lions 9-3 Dolphins 9:14, 3rd quarter
- J Bates 33 yard field goal
A false start penalty kills the drive and the Lions settle for three points. Jared Goff misses an easy throw into the turf with the NFL’s best offense looking anything but.
PICK! Lions 6-3 Dolphins 10:54, 3rd quarter
The Lions intercept Malik Willis and are knocking on the door of the red zone after the run back by Chuck Clark. On 3rd and short, who else? Jahmyr Gibbs skates over the line to gain for the 1st down. 14 yards to go for a Detroit touchdown.
TOUCHDOWN! Cowboys 17-7 Colts, half-time
- D Prescott to C Lamb for 44 yards
Wooooo! Dak Prescott goes bombs away to a wide open CeeDee Lamb who beats the chasing defender on the goalline for the touchdown!
- Broncos 13-7 Panthers
- Cowboys 10-7 Colts
- Jets 12-14 Chiefs
- Lions 6-3 Dolphins
- Browns 3-3 Saints
- Giants 6-8 Eagles
- Rams 6-10 Commanders
Some pretty filthy games out there but everything is very tight. Lot’s of lead changes to come, please, football gods!
Jets 12-14 Chiefs 12:51, half-time
Jason Sanders misses a field goal on his fifth try and Mahomes is BACK quickly to help move the Chiefs into field goal range. Harrison Butker misses the boot and gets another go and misses again. Both just wide right. That can’t be good with Justin Tucker waiting to replace him on the practice squad.
It’s GOOD! Broncos 13-7 Panthers 0:04, 2nd quarter
- W Lutz 48 yard field goal
So close! The ball bounces off Troy Franklin’s hands for what would have been a touchdown. They take the field goal.
Patrick Mahomes gets sacked on consecutive plays and is holding an arm as he walks off to the sideline. KC desperately hoping it isn’t serious.
Broncos 10-7 Panthers 0:20 2nd quarter
Denver cruise into field goal range. You can’t make mistakes like that with a defense as soft as Carolina’s. All the air immediately out of the balloon after scoring on an impressive drive.
Broncos 10-7 Panthers 1:27, 2nd quarter
Oh no. Big mistake from Carolina as kicker Ryan Fitzgerald continues his rubbish day at the office by booting it out of bounds. Denver on their 40 with lots of time to extend their lead.
- B Young to T Tremble for 10 yards
WOW! The big tight end goes up high in the left side of the end zone and just comes down in bounds. Incredible catch from Tommy Tremble. Bryce Young cashes in on the Bo Nix interception on 14 play, 86-yard drive. Game on!
Broncos 10-0 Panthers 1:35, 2nd quarter
Riley Moss has joined Jaylen Waddle in being evaluated for concussions for the Broncos. On 3rd and 9 the Panthers get 8 with a pass to Waller. What are they going to do? They’re gambling. Chuba Hubbard finds the gap to the left and rips off 24 yards!!! What a play! Almost 1st and Goal for Carolina.
Jets 12-14 Chiefs 2:16, 2nd quarter
- J Sanders 54 yard field goal
Field goals are keeping the Jets in the fight as Jason Sanders bags his fourth of the day.
Broncos 10-0 Panthers 2:14, 2nd quarter
On 3rd and 17 Bryce Young slings one for 20 yards to Tet McMilliand then pushes the Panthers over midfield with a 10-yard slant to Darren Waller.
- P Mahomes to K Walker for 25 yards
The QB and running back hook up again to retake the lead. Kenneth Walker takes the dump off short throw and rumbles the rest of the way. Quick strike after the Jets fumble.
Jets 9-7 Chiefs 6:21, 2nd quarter
Wrong then! Braelon Allen fumbles it to the Chiefs on the first play of the drive. Great peanut punch from Nick Bolton to shake the ball loose.
Jets 9-7 Chiefs 6:29, 2nd quarter
Right then! The Jets get a stop and Geno Smith is trotting out with the chance to grab a two-score lead in KC. The veteran QB has about 80 yards to travel if he is to pull it off.
Meanwhile Carolina have just picked off Bo Nix!!! He had a receiver open for what would have been a touchdown but didn’t get the ball deep enough. Underthrown.
Broncos 10-0 Panthers 10:23, 2nd quarter
Bad news for Broncos fans, Jaylen Waddle has left the game with an injury.
In other news Odell Beckham Jr has been signed by the Minnesota Vikings!
It’s GOOD! Jets 9-7 Chiefs 8:12, 2nd quarter
- J Sanders 49 yard field goal
The hat-trick for the kicker puts the Jets back on top, just.
It’s NO GOOD! Broncos 10-0 Panthers 11:44, 2nd quarter
Rough one for the Panthers. Ryan Fitzgerald misses from 43 yards way wide to the right.
TOUCHDOWN! Cowboys 10-7 Colts 14:08, 2nd quarter
- D Prescott to J Ferguson for 10 yards
Dallas retake the lead with a big gamble on 4th down. They rolled the dice and it paid off.
- P Mahomes to K Walker for seven yards
The QB finds his running back wide open short of the goalline and he jogs in for the score. All the defenders went right, Walker went left and that was that.
TOUCHDOWN! Rams 3-10 Commanders 14:00, 2nd quarter
- J Daniels to V Jefferson for seven yards
Washington on top as they bid to stay in the race for the NFC East crown.
TOUCHDOWN! Giants 6-8 Eagles 2:09, 1st quarter
- S Barkley three yard rush
Something to smile about for Philadelphia. There is hope of ending their six-game losing streak yet. They bag a two-point conversion to boot.
Jets 6-0 Chiefs 1:55, 1st quarter
Kansas City are across midfield after a 11-yard strike to Xavier Worthy then they cruise into the red zone after a 21-yard gain from a short pass to Rashee Rice. Excellent lead blocking from his teammates.
- B Nix to C Sutton for three yards
Denver are 3rd and 4 and Adam Trautman catches a Bo Nix pass to move the chains as the quarterback boots out to the right and finds the open tight end. Nix comes out and hits his trusty big man Courtland Sutton on the slant. Easy.
More? You want more?! Rams 3-3 Commanders. Still only one touchdown scored across seven games. C’mon lads sort it out!
More field goals: Jets 6-0 Chiefs, Giants 6-0 Eagles
Broncos 3-0 Panthers 4:26, 1st quarter
Carolina’s defense is really struggling giving away a third costly penalty already then Sean Payton beats the blitz with a screen pass that goes for 19 yards to Evan Ingram. An illegal Denver shift knocks them just out of the red zone. 1st and 15.
PICK! Lions 3-0 Dolphins 3:57, 1st quarter
Rough one from Jared Goff who throws a wobbler to C Johnson. Calvin is that you? Sadly not. Chris Johnson intercepts for Miami and the Dolphins pick it up at midfield after a penalty pushed them back 10 yards.
TOUCHDOWN! Cowboys 3-7 Colts 6:13, 1st quarter
- S McGowan two yard rush
Indy are in the red zone after a Dak Prescott fumble. Jonathan Taylor rumbles them to 1st and Goal then Seth McGowan jams it home at the attempt. Taylor fantasy owners are furious!
Broncos 3-0 Panthers 8:04, 1st quarter
Not quite a three and out but almost as good. Panthers punt after picking up one first down. A nervous start in the face of stiff pressure from the Broncos.
Would you believe it?! No touchdowns, only field goals on the menu. Rams 0-3 Commanders.
And one more: Jets 3-0 Chiefs. Jason Sanders bangs it through to put the New York Jetropolitans ahead in Kansas City.
In other field goal news: Cowboys 3-0 Colts, Giants 3-0 Eagles, Lions 3-0 Dolphins
It’s GOOD! Broncos 3-0 Panthers 11:09, 1st quarter
- W Lutz 26 yard field goal
A couple of Jonah Coleman runs get the Broncos to the goalline. Nix then barrels out of the pocket and just throws the ball short of Pat Bryant in the end zone. A delay of game knocks them back five yards … Panthers get some pressure and Nix runs the wrong way for so long he starts laughing after he just gets the ball past the line of scrimmage to avoid intentional grounding. He was almost sacked 24 yards behind the line, good save … I think.
Broncos 0-0 Panthers 14:02, 1st quarter
Nix rips two deep balls as the Broncos try and pick on the Panthers’ weak defense. The first one to Courtland Sutton is incomplete but the second forces a 27-yard gain via a pass interference penalty. The game plan is clear already. Throw, throw, throw some more. Makes sense considering their struggles running the ball. The Broncos move it into the red zone quickly.
Broncos 0-0 Panthers 14:56, 1st quarter
Here we go! Carolina kick it away to Denver. The Broncos run it back to the 45-yard line. Nice trot from Sean Fresch. Excellent field position for Bo Nix to go to work.
In more QB news Shadeur Sanders is starting for the Browns and Joe Milton for the Eagles. Happy news if you are starting opposition defenses in fantasy.
Ja’Marr Chase’s touchdown in Madrid means he joins Randy Moss to be the only players in NFL history with at least seven touchdown catches in each of their first six seasons. Not bad company to keep.
The Panthers meanwhile are top of the weird NFC South on 3-4 and looking to bounce back from two successive defeats.
The Broncos are in Panthers country looking for a fifth successive win as they keep finding a way with their unique brand of gritty football.
They won ugly last week with a dramatic goalline stand to deny the Kansas City Chiefs and cap their comeback from an 11-point deficit to win 28-24. It would mean they have now won 15 straight regular season games decided by one score, tied with the 2008-09 Indianapolis Colts for the longest streak in history. What’s more, it marked Bo Nix’s 13th fourth-quarterback comeback win, the most by a quarterback in his first three seasons since 1950.
With running back JK Dobbins struggling, the Broncos have unearthed a new asset out of the backfield in fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman, who had 104 yards and one touchdown from 15 scrimmage touches against the Chiefs.
Final score: (6-2) Cincinnati Bengals 34-17 Atlanta Falcons (3-6)
And that’s the end of that chapter. Cincinnati’s league-best passing attack was just far too much for Atlanta to handle. These Bengals look destined for the playoffs.
PICK! Bengals 31-17 Falcons 3:54, 4th quarter
That is the ball game at the Bernabéu. Needing three scores Michael Penix gets desperate and throws it straight at Barrett Carter who snaffles up the interception and with it the W. Cincinnati are heading to the top of the AFC North with Pittsburgh as they both sit 6-2.
The big injury news is that Myles Garrett returns for the Rams on defense. If the game wrecking defensive end is at full strength then the Commanders and Jayden Daniels could be in for a very rough afternoon. Garrett’s addition is a timely boost after the Rams lost Jaylen Watson for the reminder of the season with a shoulder injury.
Elsewhere the Cowboys are without star receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
Bengals 31-17 Falcons 7:57, 4th quarter
Oh my the Bernabéu looks beautiful doesn’t it? Inside the stadium Atlanta have the ball at their seven-yard line. And after a failed check down to Bijan Robinson they’re back at their four-yard line. Another couple of failed plays and the Falcons are punting. A huge failure after their defense managed to stop a visibly frustrated Joe Burrow.
Speaking of Burrow, he and Ja’Marr Chase have had a typically successful day. The Bengals quarterback is 23/28 for 260 yards and three touchdowns while Chase has nine receptions for 144 yards and a score.
Hola football fans, cómo estás? At the midpoint of the season week nine is underway in Madrid with the Bengals currently beating the Falcons 31-17. Before we see how that one finishes there are seven games coming at 12pm CST/1pm EST/6pm GMT (home teams listed second):
- (6-2) Denver Broncos v Carolina Panthers (3-4)
- (3-5) Dallas Cowboys v Indianapolis Colts (2-6)
- (2-6) New York Jets v Kansas City Chiefs (5-2)
- (5-2) Detroit Lions v Miami Dolphins (1-6)
- (5-3) Cleveland Browns v New Orleans Saints (2-5)
- (4-2-1) New York Giants v Philadelphia Eagles (2-6)
- (4-4) Los Angeles Rams v Washington Commanders (2-4-1)
A little bit of heat is on the Chiefs today as they host the Jets off the back of a two-game losing streak. On paper they should bounce back but the offensive weapons are still lacking for Patrick Mahomes so if Geno Smith and Braelon Allen can pick up where they left off last week (290 yards and two passing touchdowns and 147 rushing yards and a score respectively) then the Jets have a serious shot at an upset.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Dominant Lando Norris powers to victory in São Paulo F1 Grand Prix
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Giles Richards
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix after an incident-packed race at Interlagos, including a remarkable comeback for Max Verstappen who finished in second having started in 21st place.
Kimi Antonelli, the newly crowned world champion, struggled with tyre problems to make it to fifth place but with his teammate George Russell fourth it was more than enough to ensure Mercedes sealed the Formula One constructors’ world championship.
Norris delivered a strong drive at the Autódromo José Carlos Pace to complete an impressive win, with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar third, and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri sixth. Lewis Hamilton, on his 400th grand prix having taken a grid penalty for an engine change, made it to ninth place from 20th on the grid for Ferrari, with his teammate Charles Leclerc seventh.
Antonelli had led for the opening phase of the race having beaten Norris off the line but had issues with his car after his first pit stop, which appeared to be due to an imbalance in tyre temperatures, during which he went off track twice – the type of difficulties with which the Italian has not struggled all season. It allowed Norris into the lead from where the British driver was all but untouchable, across a range of wet and dry conditions with consummate control. Russell drove well but for a spin on exiting the pit lane which was costly.
In clean air out front the McLaren had immense pace that allowed Norris to dictate, even as there was late tension when rain swept the track in the final 10 laps, causing a flurry of pit stops for wet rubber. The track was treacherous but Norris had its measure to the flag, where he finished with a 14-second lead.
Verstappen had taken a full raft of new engine components that meant he had to start from 21st and making it up to second ranks among his best comebacks on a track where he has already delivered some mighty performances. In 2016 he came back from 16th to third in the wet, last year he also took third after starting from the pit lane and in 2025 he won from 17th on the grid. He showed similarly sharp decisiveness and touch to come through the field, making it up to second by just past the halfway point.
The result ensured that Mercedes have sealed their ninth constructors’ title and their first drivers’ and constructors’ double since Hamilton took the championship in 2020. They needed to outscore second-placed Ferrari by just three points in Brazil and comfortably closed out the championship.
The achievement is the culmination of a what has been a remarkable season for the team, dominant for the opening half of the year, having developed both the best car and the best engine for the complex new regulations of 2026, an advantage which they made the most of with the team winning the opening six races of the year.
They have since taken 12 wins in total with Antonelli scoring nine and Russell three from 20 meetings.
McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull developed their cars strongly to come back at them, with all three taking wins but Mercedes remained operationally strong and continued to maximise their return, even given they were nor bringing upgrades at the same rate as their rivals. Reliability has been their only real weakness, perhaps to be expected given the new regulations and will be something the team can be expected to address going forward.
For Norris and McLaren the victory represents a real result, delivered with impressive precision as the final set of upgrades they brought to this round, notably the front wing, appear to have paid off. Norris had shown great pace in qualifying with pole and proved that the car had similar form in race pace.
It is his third win this season, his second win in a row Brazil and the 14th of his career. Another affirmation that while the title is gone, he is still determined to make a decent fist of every opportunity and that with wins still on the table, McLaren can still be in the fight with Mercedes, Red Bull and Ferrari and will be buoyed with this performance as they look to 2027.

Trump says fresh strikes on Iran ‘highly unlikely’ if talks progress
8 November 2026 18:53 GMT
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that renewed strikes on Iran are “highly unlikely” provided negotiations progress over Tehran's nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump said in a phone interview reported by CNN, adding: “I would, if necessary, but we hit them really hard.”

Meanwhile, he said that the Iranian government maintains 10 percent of its missile capacity and 15 percent of its drone capabilities.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Peschel scores on debut as USA rout Germany 5-0 at women’s hockey worlds
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Guardian sport and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Emma Peschel celebrated her international debut with a goal as the United States shut out Germany 5-0 at the women’s ice hockey world championship on Sunday.
The 22-year-old defender scored with a wrist shot from the point to make it 2-0 in the opening period of the Group A game.
Casey O’Brien opened the scoring and added an assist in her second game for the US, having marked her debut with a goal and an assist in Friday’s 7-0 victory over Switzerland.
Alex Carpenter extended the lead to 3-0 in the second period before Abbey Murphy and Joy Dunne completed the rout with third-period goals.
Captain Hilary Knight registered an assist to extend her world championship records to 54 assists and 122 points. Defender Caroline Harvey added two assists, giving her five through the opening two games.
Goaltender Gwyneth Philips stopped all 13 shots she faced as the Americans recorded their second straight shutout, having outscored their opponents 12-0 to open the tournament.
“Today was another solid win under our belt, Germany is a talented team,” US coach John Wroblewski said. “We’re going to take the positives from this game and focus on turning our attention to our next test against Austria tomorrow.”
The Americans have won 10 of the past 14 world championships and arrived in Denmark as reigning world and Olympic champions, having claimed the 2025 title in the Czech Republic and gold at the Milan-Cortina Games in February, beating Canada in overtime in both finals. They will face Austria in another group-stage contest in Esbjerg on Monday.
All but one member of the American roster plays in the Professional Women’s Hockey League.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has dismissed a new US military initiative to restrict the movement of goods through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea as “merely wordplay”, as tensions over shipping routes and Washington's blockade continue.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Carlos Alcaraz beats error-prone Ben Shelton to win Paris Masters
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Reuters
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Carlos Alcaraz avenged his loss to Ben Shelton in the US Open last eight as he edged the American 7-6 (5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters on Sunday, clinching his ninth ATP 1000 title.
The world No 3 controlled the contest from the baseline to become the first Spaniard to win the tournament since David Ferrer in 2012, while Shelton was left frustrated by an erratic forehand.
“Today, it was one of the toughest challenges we have in tennis right now, facing Ben Shelton,” said Alcaraz, whose US Open title defence was derailed by the eventual finalist Shelton in a four-and-a-half-hour thriller in September. “He is doing better and better with every tournament so it’s going to be even tougher facing him. So I’m just really happy that I found the way.“
The first set remained deadlocked until the tie-break, where Shelton overshot the baseline three times on his forehand, allowing the Spaniard to take the set. The world No 4 capitalised on two double faults and wayward topspins from Alcaraz to go 3-2 up in the second, and extended the lead with two aces in the following game.
But Alcaraz fought back with a break of his own to make it 4-4, landing two cross-court winners as Shelton netted a forehand and went long with another. With Alcaraz leading 6-5, Shelton stumbled again while serving to stay in the match, overshooting two forehands before the seven-times grand slam winner clinched victory with a perfectly timed backhand down the line.
“It’s something I’ve been chasing for a long time,” Alcaraz said after finally winning the Paris Masters on his sixth attempt.
The Australian Open champion has now won three titles since the heartbreak at Flushing Meadows as he looks to end the year on a bright note at the ATP Finals starting next Sunday, followed by the Davis Cup finals later this month.

https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026.title: Nasa seeks next generation of astronauts to live and work on the moon
https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026.author: Keely Aouga
https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026.text:
Nasa has launched a callout for a new generation of astronauts as it searches for explorers who could live and work on the moon.
Opening applications for the latest expansion of its Artemis program, the US agency said successful candidates would help “shape humanity’s future in space” as it builds a base on the moon and plans the first crewed missions to Mars.
The news was announced on Saturday during a Kennedy Space Center air show promoting lunar exploration, as well as advances in aviation and technology.
“This is an extraordinary time to join Nasa’s astronaut corps,” said Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars.”
Nasa expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training the next class of astronaut candidates. The agency last opened applications for new astronauts in 2024, ultimately accepting 10 new astronauts out of more than 8,000 applicants in September 2025.
“For those who apply, becoming a Nasa astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at Nasa’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space.”
Since the 1960s, Nasa has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for increasingly challenging missions. The agency currently has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps.
Isaacman and other agency leaders recently laid out Nasa’s ambitions to return Americans to the moon in 2028. Both SpaceX and Blue Origin intend to support a crewed lunar landing.
All applicants must be US citizens, Nasa said, and have either a master’s degree in science, technology, engineering or mathematics; medical qualifications; training as a pilot; or two years’ work on a relevant doctoral program.
Three years of “related professional experience” are also required.
Applying pilots must have either 750 hours of pilot-in-command time of a high-performance jet, 1,500 total flight hours in another fixed-wing aircraft, or 1,000 total flight hours in a rotary-wing aircraft.
Applicants have until 11.59pm ET on Thursday, 3 December, to submit their applications.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: Israeli forces release Palestinian journalist Abou Shhadeh
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Israeli forces release Palestinian journalist Abou Shhadeh
Abed Abou Shhadeh says his detention was part of Israel’s political measures ‘to indimidate Arab society as a whole’.
Israeli authorities have released Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after detaining him for five days without charge.
Speaking after his release, Abou Shhadeh said on Sunday that his detention was part of “political measures” intended not only for him “but to intimidate Arab society as a whole”.
“In my view, the most appropriate response is to reaffirm among ourselves that we are on the right side, that our path is the path of truth,” he said, adding that he would continue his work as a journalist.
Abou Shhadeh was held in a Shin Bet intelligence facility in Petah Tikva, on the outskirts of Tel Aviv, after being detained on Tuesday on suspicion of “contact with a foreign agent”.
He was suspected of receiving money from foreign sources in order to support Israel’s Arab voters, according to the legal rights group Adalah, which is part of his defence team.
The accusation came after Abou Shhadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, spoke on the al-Midan podcast for the Arab48 website and appeared as an analyst on Al Jazeera.
He addressed topics similar to those discussed in Israeli media outlets, according to Hadeel Abu Salih, his legal counsel and a human rights lawyer with Adalah.
“It was obvious from the first day, from Thursday, that the police doesn’t have, any evidence in this context,” Abu Salih said. All of the suspicion relied on a public conversation he had with Palestinian intellectual Azmi Bishara when he was in Qatar.
“This is now being criminalised only because the speakers are Palestinians,” Abu Salih said. “Or when Palestinians are asking to analyse their political reality. The Israeli system turned that discussion and analysis into a criminal suspicion.”
“They were trying to say that he’s not a journalist, that he’s a political counsel.”
The lawyer said Abou Shhadeh was arrested in the middle of the night on Tuesday after 15 Israeli security officers raided his home in Jaffa and confiscated personal belongings, such as electronic devices and books, in front of his two children.
‘Campaign against the votes of… Palestinians’
His five-day detention was “part of the campaign against the votes of the Arabs and Palestinians in Israel”, Adalah founder Hassan Jabareen told Al Jazeera.
Jabareen said Israel sought to “delegitimise their votes” by the claims against Abou Shhadeh.
“He travelled to Doha as a journalist … he came back as a journalist. But he was arrested as an Arab political person,” Jabareen said. “They tried to use him in order to say that Arabs use illegal [means] in their political participation in the Israeli elections.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Tenerife’s Jesus De Miguel honoured in tearful tribute by teammates, fans
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Tenerife’s Jesus De Miguel honoured in tearful tribute by teammates, fans
Teammates choke back tears, fans chant his name and family are promised support by the club at memorial service.
Tenerife football club bids farewell to Jesus de Miguel
A bouquet of flowers marked the spot on the pitch where Jesus De Miguel fell five days earlier. His teammates returned to the stadium dressed in all black. Above them hung a banner that read “Eterno Demi 9” – Demi 9 forever – a reference to the number nine’s nickname.
In the stands, supporters chanted the name they had once roared to celebrate his goals for CD Tenerife. On Saturday, it was a wail to bid him goodbye.
Thousands gathered at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium in Santa Cruz, the capital of Tenerife in the Spanish Canary Islands, where the forward suffered a collision on Monday that resulted in his tragic death. Silence gave way to applause before the club’s centenary anthem was played.
‘Tremendously unfair’
On the makeshift stage, captain Enric Gallego struggled through his farewell speech.
He recalled a teammate so reluctant to inconvenience others that, when his car broke down, he walked home without asking for help.
“To speak of you in the past tense is tremendously unfair,” Gallego said, pausing to regain composure.
“It’s still hard to believe that this has happened to us, Demi, you’ll always be one of us. We’re still struggling to come to terms with the fact that you won’t be with us again.” 
A loss beyond football
Thundering applause greeted De Miguel’s parents, sister, wife and daughter – a family coping with its loss publicly, but alongside thousands who had gathered to share their grief.
Addressing the bereaved family, Gallego promised that De Miguel’s 18-month-old daughter, Carla, would grow up knowing what her father had meant to those around him.
The club has pledged to financially support Carla until she turns 18.
The solidarity erased the lines of football rivalry across the islands as Ultra Naciente, a supporters’ group from UD Las Palmas in the Canary Islands, placed a wreath on the pitch before the ceremony.
For Jose Diaz Muros, president of Tenerife supporters’ group Pena Iberica, the loss felt personal.
“When a player becomes part of your team, he also becomes part of your life: the conversations at home, the weekends and the memories you share with your family,” he told Al Jazeera.
“That is why a loss like this feels so close, even if you did not know him personally.”
‘Space to grieve’
De Miguel’s death was confirmed on Tuesday, hours after he was taken to hospital following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during Tenerife’s second-division match.
The tragedy has not only brought together football clubs all over Spain, but also raised questions about the response by Spanish football authorities to requests by players for a grieving period.
The Spanish players’ union, AFE, said footballers consulted across the categories unanimously favoured postponement because they did not feel emotionally ready to compete.
Las Palmas defender Alex Suarez expressed that distress publicly: “My head is not in football”.
Three Segunda fixtures were postponed, alongside a women’s match involving Costa Adeje Tenerife, but there was no blanket suspension of games.
The federation’s competition judge ruled AFE’s request inadmissible, saying the decision belonged to La Liga and Spanish football’s top division did not postpone its fixtures.
The governing bodies organised commemorative shirts, floral offerings, pre-match silence and pauses from the ninth minute, honouring De Miguel’s shirt number. Their joint statement presented the tributes as a way to remember him with dignity and respect.
While tributes were paid, AFE’s concerns remained unanswered and football played on.
“There was recognition of the grief, but the collective request was not met in full,” Albert Ortega, a Spanish football expert, told Al Jazeera.
Ortega believes that players’ emotional wellbeing still has less power to alter the calendar than institutional statements suggest. But he cautioned against assuming commercial interests alone explained the decision.
“We cannot demonstrate that money was the only reason for the decision. We can demand transparency about the criteria and the weight given to their views.”
Tenerife fan Diaz Muros acknowledged the difficulties of suspending fixtures, but said players’ concerns should have been addressed.
“Minutes of silence are important, but so is giving people space to grieve.”
Tragedy highlights players’ welfare
In Tenerife, questions were also raised at the resumption of action while an investigation into the collision and emergency response, including treatment and evacuation, were ongoing.
Santa Cruz de Tenerife’s chief prosecutor, Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui, told the Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings over the collision seemed unlikely. He cited the distinction between injuries arising during sporting play and deliberate aggression.
Meanwhile, the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee has deferred its decision on goalkeeper Owono, but EFE reported a potential suspension of up to 12 matches.
Spanish football expert Ortega argued that prevention of such incidents requires attention that goes beyond individual responsibility.
“Having a written protocol is the starting point,” he said. “Its effectiveness is demonstrated when the people who must implement it know their roles and can act in a coordinated way.”
He proposed independent reviews, regular emergency drills and checks on each stadium’s capacity to respond as possible measures to help prevent such tragedies.
The clash happened during a second division professional football match but questions still remain about procedures in lower division games, where provision of resources and medical response predate De Miguel’s death.
After Colindres goalkeeper Raul Ramirez suffered a fatal injury in the Spanish fifth division in September last year, AFE challenged the provisions in the lower tiers. The ground where he was injured had a defibrillator, but did not have a doctor or ambulance on site.
AFE president David Aganzo has now renewed calls for medical professionals and ambulances across national categories.
According to Ortega, protection also requires a bereavement procedure agreed with players.
Decisions on postponements, the criteria and how teams participate should be made with those stepping on the pitch. Psychological support, he argues, should continue beyond the first week.
For Tenerife fan president Diaz Muros, thoughts must return to those who will continue to grieve for their lifetimes.
“After the tributes, when the attention disappears, they will still be living with that absence. I would like the support to continue then.”
At Tenerife’s Estadio Heliodoro, as the Catholic prayer song Ave Maria played, those gathered stood for a final round of applause.
Above them beamed a monochrome image of Tenerife’s number nine, frozen in celebration, as tears streamed down the faces of his teammates and loved ones.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Gavin Newsom commutes more than 500 death sentences in California
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Gavin Newsom, California’s governor, has commuted the death sentences of more than 500 people on the state’s death row on Thursday, a move that ensures they can never be executed under future administrations.
The Democrat’s mass commutation at the end of his term has converted all of the state’s death sentences to life without the possibility of parole, the largest clearing of any US death row in modern history.
The move comes after the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee sparked global outrage and renewed calls for a nationwide pause on capital punishment.
His decision impacts 529 men and 19 women who were sentenced to death in the state, making up the largest death row in the western hemisphere, the governor said in a letter announcing his decision.
“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” he wrote. “I know we cannot execute people in our imperfect legal system and remain true to our core values, first among them justice and human decency.”
Newsom, considered a probable candidate for president in 2028, has long opposed the death penalty and issued a moratorium on executions in 2019. He also dismantled the state’s physical death row chamber in the infamous San Quentin prison, transferring people with death sentences to other facilities where they had more freedom of movement and access to programs – for some, a dramatic change after decades isolated in solitary cells.
The last execution in California was in 2006, but hundreds of people incarcerated in the state’s prisons have continued to live under death sentences, making California home to the largest death row population in the nation.
Newsom’s office noted on Thursday that of the 548 people sentenced to death, 220 of them have waited 15 years or more to be appointed habeas counsel, the legal representation they are entitled to access to fight their cases. And 139 people have waited 20 years or more for representation. If there were no moratorium in place, there are 45 people in the state who are considered to have exhausted their appeals and would be immediately subject to execution.
“This decision is among the most difficult of my career, not because I doubt its necessity for our state but because I know its announcement may surface excruciating memories for victims’ families,” Newsom said. “I hold this painful truth along with the belief that this is a righteous action.”
The California supreme court will have to review and approve the clemency grants for cases where the individual was convicted of multiple felonies, Newsom said.
The announcement was praised by the American Civil Liberties Union and prominent advocates who oppose the death penalty, including Martin Luther King III, the eldest son of the civil rights icon, and Bryan Stevenson, an internationally renowned death penalty lawyer.
Jeanne Woodford, a former California prisons director who oversaw four executions, applauded Newsom in a statement, noting that more than 200 people nationwide have been exonerated after being sentenced to death: “As someone who has carried out executions in California, I am haunted by the fear that we will execute an innocent person.”
A relative of a victim killed by one man on California’s death row also spoke out in favor of the commutations. Jess Nichol is the sister of Polly Klaas, a 12-year-old killed in 1993 in a notorious case that paved the way for tough-on-crime laws. She said in a statement Thursday that she used to support the execution of the man who killed her sister. “But over time I’ve realized that whether he’s executed has absolutely nothing to do with my recovery or with real public safety. The system tells survivors that execution matters to our healing. It doesn’t. It’s a distraction from what we actually need,” she said.
Governors of both parties have taken bold measures to oppose capital punishment over the years, including an Illinois Republican who commuted all 167 death sentences in 2003 before leaving office. In 2024, North Carolina’s Democratic governor, Roy Cooper, commuted 15 death sentences in the state in his final day in office.
Support for the death penalty has been declining across the US, but Democrats at times have been reluctant to do mass commutations out of fear that Republicans will paint them as “soft on crime” politicians who sided with people convicted of brutal murders.
Newsom has supported criminal justice reform efforts, including changes to prioritize rehabilitative programs in prisons. But some advocates over the years have accused him of caving to political pressures on the issue, including when he has vetoed the release of high-profile prisoners even after they have been granted parole.
California is one of 27 states that still have the death penalty on the books.

https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California to block law protecting children from addiction risk
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.author: Johana Bhuiyan and agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text:
Google, Meta and TikTok have sued California to block enforcement of a new state law intended to limit the risk of addicting children under 16 to social media platforms.
The law, known as Assembly Bill 1709, prohibits such platforms from offering underage children “psychologically exploitative features” that could lead to compulsive use, such as providing personal recommendations and sending videos through autoplay features. It also requires the deletion of children’s accounts with those features.
In separate lawsuits on Wednesday, Google, Meta and TikTok said the law wrongly compels them to honor California’s preferred means of presenting content to children and substitutes the state’s judgment for that of parents.
They said the law violates the US constitution’s first amendment free speech protections, as well as Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act, which broadly shields online platforms from liability over user content.
The office of Rob Bonta, the California attorney general, who enforces the state’s laws and is the only defendant, said on Thursday it was reviewing the lawsuits. “Our office is committed to defending California’s commonsense laws to protect kids online,” it added.
Google owns YouTube and is a unit of Alphabet, while Meta owns Facebook and Instagram. TikTok is a unit of China’s ByteDance.
Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law on 10 September, saying children’s safety should be central to any discussion about technology, and California “will not stand by while unregulated technology puts our children at risk”.
The law takes effect on 1 January 2027, unless a judge voids it or puts it on hold.
“Parents are best positioned to make the right decisions for their families,” Jose Castaneda, a Google spokesperson, said on Thursday. “Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we’ve built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos.”
In its lawsuit, Meta said California cannot override its editorial judgments about how to curate and display billions of posts, while leaving children free to spend unlimited time on other online platforms that offer similar services.
TikTok, meanwhile, said protected speech “cannot be suppressed solely to protect the young from ideas or images that a legislative body thinks unsuitable”.
Other critics also accused California of overreaching. The Electronic Frontier Foundation, a non-profit digital rights advocacy group, called the law “a massive privacy and free speech nightmare”.
Many US states regulate children’s access to social media. Countries around the world have similar restrictions, including a ban in Australia on social media for children under 16.
In August, Meta agreed to pay up to $18bn and limit teenagers’ use of Facebook and Instagram under agreements with nearly all US states, which accused it of violating privacy and consumer protection laws.
In the aftermath of whistleblower revelations that showed Meta was aware of the way its platforms harmed teens, Meta launched a suite of teen safety tools aimed at giving parents more oversight. The company has previously tapped influencers to promote these features around the world as an alternative to social media bans or limitations similar to Australia’s.
Google has come under fire more recently over the use of its AI tools on school devices. On Thursday, parents in California filed a lawsuit against the company alleging their teen daughter made plans to end her life after multiple interactions with AI mode on Google Search. She had access to the AI mode through her school-issued Google Chromebook. The company was also recently forced to backtrack on its decision to cut off a school or classroom’s access to Google Search if teachers or administrators decided not to enable Google’s other AI features for schools.
Google filed its lawsuit in federal court in San Jose, California. Meta sued in San Francisco, and TikTok sued in Los Angeles.
The companies and Snapchat parent Snap still face thousands of lawsuits by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities claiming they sought to addict children and caused a mental health crisis that resulted in such harms as anxiety, depression and suicide.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Who is Nithya Raman, the democratic socialist who will be Los Angeles’s next mayor?
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Lois Beckett in Los Angeles
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Nithya Raman on Thursday unseated Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass after a neck-and-neck race for the leadership for the US’s second largest city.
The young progressive’s victory means that the two largest cities in the US, as well the nation’s capital, Washington DC, have now all elected democratic socialist mayors.
Though Raman’s political ascendance in Los Angeles has sparked many comparisons to New York City’s mayor Zohran Mamdani, her political profile in her home town is very different from Mamdani’s, as is her often tense relationship with the local chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America.
Here’s some key facts about LA’s new mayor:
Raman broke into politics in 2020 by unseating an establishment Democrat on LA’s powerful city council.
When Raman, an urban planner and political outsider, won a seat on LA’s city council in 2020, it was the first time that a sitting city council member had been ousted in 17 years. One LA political analyst called her win “a political earthquake”. Raman, whose campaign was endorsed by Bernie Sanders, was also the first DSA-endorsed candidate elected to office in Los Angeles. Raman credited her 2020 win to on-the-ground grassroots organizing, telling the Guardian at the time: “We knocked on 80,000 doors, which as far as we know, is a record. By the general election, we had 2,000 volunteers over all. We had 1,000 people just in our Slack.”
She has close ties to Hollywood progressives, including an endorsement from the Hollywood writers’ guild.
At the height of the #MeToo era, Raman served as the entertainment director for the Time’s Up, the organization founded by powerful women in Hollywood that created a legal defense fund for women in all professions to fight back against pervasive sexual assault and sexual harassment.
While older Hollywood celebrities such as Jane Fonda and Samuel L Jackson endorsed Bass, Raman secured endorsements from younger celebrities and comedians such as Mindy Kaling, Adam Scott, and Jaboukie Young-White. Raman’s husband, Vali Chandrasekaran, is a longtime TV writer.
She has also received attention from one very prominent celebrity Republican, former California governor Arnold Schwarzenegger, with whom she had “a widely publicized private meeting”.
Raman’s key issues are housing policy, homelessness and tenants’ rights.
Raman, an urban planner, has said she joined DSA-LA, which she did in 2019, not because of an “ideological drive”, but “because it was one of the only organizations that was meaningfully talking about housing affordability in the city”. Her mayoral platform calls for building more housing “at all income levels, everything from deed-restricted affordable housing to market-rate housing to social housing to homeless shelters”.
Her goal is to triple annual housing construction in the city, an approach that earned her an endorsement from advocacy group Yimby Action, which believes the best answer to housing affordability is simply building as much housing as possible.
Before she ran for office, Raman co-founded a still-active volunteer organization to help unhoused people in north-east LA.
In 2017, Raman was one of five co-founders of the SELAH Neighborhood Homeless Coalition, a group that organizes local volunteers in north-east LA to do outreach and advocacy with their unhoused neighbors. The group, which is still active and now claims 800 volunteers, is focused on recognizing “unhoused individuals as fellow members of our community worthy of the same dignity, respect and representation afforded to any housed person”.
Raman won the mayoral race despite a conspicuous lack of support from her city council colleagues – even the fellow democratic socialists on the council.
In a mayoral debate with Raman, Bass, her opponent, brought up Raman’s lack of support from other city council members and city leaders, saying: “Your colleagues have a very difficult time working with you.” The three other democratic socialists who were elected to the LA city council after Raman all endorsed Bass for mayor.
“So the establishment doesn’t like Raman: so what?” Los Angeles Times columnist Gustavo Arellano wrote, arguing that Raman’s outsider status was precisely what voters frustrated with LA’s Democratic political establishment wanted.
Raman, who was among the politicians revealed to have been targeted by establishment Democrats in the 2022 LA city hall audio tape leak scandal, won reelection to the city council in 2024 by a large margin.
At Raman’s election night party, “the political class of Los Angeles was absent,” Kurt Peterson, one of the leaders of hospitality union Unite Here local 11, which endorsed Raman, told Politico. But, he added: “Even though every city councilperson said they were standing with Karen Bass, not very many of the people they represent followed them to the polls.”
While DSA-LA ultimately did endorse Raman for mayor, the endorsement was … complicated.
The local chapter of the DSA did not endorse Raman during the primary, when she entered the race at the last minute after previously endorsing Bass.
After she beat out reality star Spencer Pratt for second place and advanced into the runoff against Bass, DSA-LA did “enthusiastically” endorse her, but noted that “Councilmember Raman’s relationship with DSA-LA, and the broader Angeleno grassroots left, has had some ups and downs”. Among Raman’s downs was “an inconsistent position on Palestine, which eventually resulted in conflict with the chapter over a 2024 endorsement from a pro-Israel Dem club”, the group wrote in its voter guide, noting that they believed she had since “worked with us to improve on this issue”.
But Raman’s DSA-LA endorsement was almost rescinded in a vote of national DSA organizers over her stance on Israel, the Los Angeles Times reported, with a national political committee voting 14-13 against rescinding the local endorsement in early November.
Despite the endorsement drama, DSA-LA was quick to celebrate Raman’s victory, posting a photo captioned, “YUP, that’s our mayor!!!” even before the Associated Press had called the election in her favor.
Raman is proud of her willingness to break with allies and take ‘unpopular’ positions.
Raman touts her political independence – including her willingness to vote against her allies on key policy issues – as the heart of her political identity.
She broke with the DSA on her belief that LA’s mansion tax, which brought in less revenue than supporters had hoped, needed to be reformed, which she called an “extremely unpopular sentiment”.
One Hollywood comedian who supports Raman contrasted her with Mamdani by saying, “She’s not ideological. She’s a wonk,” Vanity Fair reported.
Raman said she was “grateful” for comparisons to Mamdani, but “I am myself”.
In recent interviews, Raman has emphasized her political distance from the DSA.
“The mayoral candidate said she favors the Scandinavian model of social democracy, signaling a belief in a regulated free-market economy rather than the more explicitly anti-capitalist vision embraced by many in the DSA,” Vanity Fair wrote in an October profile.
Asked about comparisons to New York’s democratic socialist mayor, Raman said: “Mamdani is one of the most popular politicians in America right now, and I’m very grateful to be compared to someone who is that skilled as a communicator and a leader. But I am different. I am myself.”

https://apache.be/2026/10/26/hoe-servisc.title: Hoe de Servische studentenbeweging uitgroeide tot verkiezingsoverwinnaar
https://apache.be/2026/10/26/hoe-servisc.author: Simon Clément
https://apache.be/2026/10/26/hoe-servisc.text:
Wie vandaag de faculteit Filosofie in het Servische Novi Sad binnentreedt, merkt nog weinig van de blokkade die er maandenlang standhield. De Studentenlijst groeide hier uit tot de grote volksbeweging tegen de regering en de overheidscorruptie die afgelopen zondag (25/10) de verkiezingen won. Verdwijnen Vučić en zijn aanhangers na de nederlaag van dit weekend helemaal van het toneel?
Gejuich op de straten en pleinen in Servië gisteren (25/10): de Studentenlijst, die al twee jaar lang tegen het beleid van president Aleksandar Vučić protesteerde, heeft de parlementsverkiezingen gewonnen.
Deze lente trok fotograaf Simon Clément naar Servië om er de lokale verkiezingen te volgen, toen de studentenbeweging zich voor het eerst als politieke partij positioneerde.
Deze fotoreportage werd in juni 2026 gepubliceerd in Apache Magazine.
Op 1 november 2024 stortte een pas vernieuwd afdak van het treinstation in Novi Sad volledig in na een renovatie, waarop de regering nalatigheid verweten werd. Zestien mensen kwamen om het leven.
“De eerste dag was er een van shock. Iedereen stuurde sms’jes naar hun geliefden om te vragen of ze veilig waren”, herinnert Jelena Kleut zich, hoogleraar mediastudies aan de faculteit waar de studenten in opstand kwamen. “De tweede dag kwam de leugen.”
President Aleksandar Vučić verklaarde daags na de ramp dat de overheid de overkapping nog niet had aangepakt – iets wat verklaringen van betrokken ingenieurs en beelden van de burgemeester en minister van Transport die het net gerenoveerde station inhuldigden, onmiddellijk tegenspraken. “En dus braken er op de derde dag protesten uit”, vertelt Kleut.
Op de nationale dag van de studenten zei de huidige minister van Informatie, Boris Bratina, nog dat “de politie het recht heeft om studenten te slaan en zelfs te doden”
Meer dan twintigduizend mensen verzamelden zich aan het station van de kleine stad om hun woede te uiten over het feit dat de overheid de verantwoordelijkheid voor de ramp zo vlotjes van zich afschoof. In amper een jaar tijd groeide het aantal manifestanten tot 160.000 à 300.000.
“Samen met duizenden anderen waren we aan het wachten op de studenten alsof we wachtten op Tito, de voormalige Joegoslavische leider”, zegt de oudere Marica geëmotioneerd.
Anderhalf jaar na de ramp aan het stationsgebouw ligt het puin er nog steeds bij alsof het gisteren gebeurd is, slechts omringd met enkele hekken, talloze brieven, herdenkingsbordjes en verwelkte bloemen.
Sinds de Servische Progressieve Partij (SNS) van Vučić in 2014 de macht overnam, glijdt het land alsmaar meer af naar een dictatuur. “In Servië is werkelijk iedereen intussen getroffen of benadeeld door zijn beleid”, hekelt student literatuur Marco.
“Wanneer er zoveel politieke gevangenen zijn, onafhankelijke journalistiek zwaar onder druk staat en de rechterlijke macht haar autonomie verliest, kun je Servië moeilijk nog een democratie noemen”, meent Kleut. “Ze zijn het pad aan het effenen voor een complete machtsovername na de volgende nationale verkiezingen. De strijd is nog lang niet voorbij.”
Medeplichtige van Milošević
In de eerste jaren van zijn politieke carrière was Vučić minister van Informatie onder het nationalistische bewind van Slobodan Milošević. Hij was medeverantwoordelijk voor het ontkennen, verbergen en goedpraten van Servische wreedheden in Bosnië, Kosovo en Servië zelf. Kritische journalisten golden als buitenlandse spionnen, terwijl gedode burgers als terroristen werden omschreven.
Onafhankelijke media konden nog maar moeilijk overleven. Die zorgwekkende trend van intimidatie duurt ook onder de huidige minister van Informatie, Boris Bratina, voort. Op 4 april, Dan studenata of nationale dag van de studenten, zei hij nog dat “de politie het recht heeft om studenten te slaan en zelfs te doden”.
Vooral de demonstraties en campagnes tegen de geplande lithiummijnen inspireerden de huidige studentenbeweging
In zijn jaarverslag van 2025 spreekt Human Rights Watch van onwettig gebruik van geweld tegen demonstranten, intimidatie, inbreuk op de privacywetgeving en onmenselijke omstandigheden in de gevangenissen.
Het beleg van Belgrado
Voor Serviërs is protest niets nieuws. In het laatste decennium alleen al lijkt er elk jaar wel een kleine of grote protestgolf over het land te spoelen. In 2016 tegen vermeende verkiezingsfraude, in 2018 de “Een van de vijf miljoen”-protesten, toen Aleksandar Vučić zei dat zelfs als er vijf miljoen mensen op straat zouden komen, hij niets zou veranderen.
Maar vooral de demonstraties en campagnes tegen de geplande lithiummijnen inspireerden de huidige studentenbeweging. In 2024 trokken meer dan 100.000 mensen de straten op tegen de geplande mijnen.
Er werden treinsporen geblokkeerd en net als de studentenbeweging genoot het protest heel wat steun bij de bevolking, zelfs bij de SNS-achterban. Door de massale druk werd het mijnproject tijdelijk stop-
gezet, tot ongenoegen van de EU, die het als strategisch belangrijk ziet.
“Eten, protesteren, plenum en slapen. En dat vijf maanden lang”
“Al die ervaring heeft de studentenbeweging geërfd en getild naar een nieuwe protestbeweging”, vertelt student Milica Klajn. Ze organiseerden bijna dagelijks wakes om slachtoffers van de ramp in het treinstation te herdenken. Terwijl het dodental klom, blokkeerden de studenten eerst 14, dan 15 en uiteindelijk 16 minuten lang de straat in alle stilte.
In december viel een knokploeg kunststudenten uit Belgrado aan. “Ik ging meteen naar mijn faculteit omdat ik hoorde dat er een plenum was (een open vergadering waarin op gedecentraliseerde manier wordt gedebatteerd, red.). Daar besloten we om onmiddellijk ook onze faculteit te bezetten”, zegt Tatjana, een student biologie in Belgrado. Al snel volgden andere universiteiten en faculteiten over het hele land.
Ook buiten de traditioneel politiek actieve faculteiten groeide de mobilisatie: in Novi Sad daagden meer dan 3.000 studenten op voor het eerste plenum van de ingenieursfaculteit. “Ik hoop echt dat onze blokkades een verschil hebben gemaakt. Ik heb er zo veel voor gegeven, ik leefde er praktisch. Eten, protesteren, plenum en slapen. En dat vijf maanden lang”, zegt Milica met een zucht.
Vervroegde verkiezingen
Zelfs gewelddadige ontzettingen en een lange zomervakantie kregen de geest niet meer in de fles. “Vučić dacht echt dat deze beweging, net als eerdere protestgolven, gewoon zou uitdoven. Maar doordat hij ons bleef aanvallen in de media, maakte hij ons juist nog strijdvaardiger”, zegt Tatjana lachend. Tot op vandaag staat het plenum centraal in de horizontale manier van organiseren van de studenten.
Ondertussen hebben ook burgers het concept overgenomen. In Novi Sad komen sympathiserende groepen periodiek bijeen en bespreken zij zowel hoe ze hun lokale buurt kunnen verbeteren als hoe ze de protesten kunnen ondersteunen. Hoewel deze aanpak zorgt voor brede betrokkenheid, brengt ze ook vertraging met zich mee: het kostte de studenten maanden om te beslissen om als politieke partij voort te doen.
Tot grote verbazing werd er gehoor gegeven aan de eis tot vervroegde nationale verkiezingen, die er voor het einde van 2026 moeten komen. Volgens sommige peilingen genieten de studenten alvast van een meerderheid: zo’n 58% van de bevolking zou op hen stemmen.
Met als eerste cruciale tussenstop de lokale verkiezingen in ongeveer tien districten, die de lakmoesproef zijn voor zowel Vučić als de studenten. Maar ze zijn op hun hoede. “Want eerlijk verlopen de verkiezingen in Servië allerminst”, stelt Tatjana.
Waar blijft Europa?
Het verbaast de studenten dan ook wel dat er bijzonder weinig steun uit Europa komt. “Vroeger had ik een geïdealiseerd beeld van Europa”, geeft Tatjana toe.
“Ondertussen vertrouw ik die instituties niet meer. Al te vaak primeren strategische belangen op mensenrechten. Het lijkt alsof ze een andere taal spreken als het gaat over Oekraïne en Rusland dan wanneer het Israël en Palestina betreft. Europa wil nog steeds ons lithium voor goedkope batterijen in militaire drones.”
“Ze zetten wel druk, maar lang niet genoeg”, vertelt Kleut. “In het voorjaar vroegen negen Europese parlementariërs Vučić nog om de mensenrechten te respecteren. De EU ziet dat Vučić de controle verliest, en maakt zich tegelijkertijd zorgen over toekomstige lithiumaanvoer. De EU vreest dat als de banden met Vučić worden doorgesneden, hij zich volledig tot Rusland en China zal wenden. Dan verlies je elk middel van druk en invloed. De studenten blijven wat op afstand van die grotere vraagstukken over de EU. Maar je kan zulke beslissingen niet blijven uitstellen.”
Als de toren valt
Tijana Nešić (63) was een van de duizenden vrijwillige observatoren die de lokale verkiezingen hebben gemonitord. Ze ging eind maart naar Kula, wat in het Servisch ‘toren’ betekent, een klein stadje met net geen 50.000 inwoners. Hier hebben de studenten ervoor gekozen om zelf deel te nemen aan de lokale verkiezingen, terwijl ze in andere steden de bevolking aanmoedigen om op de oppositie te stemmen.
Voor haar vertrek verklaarde Tijana: “Als we Kula winnen, valt de rest als een kaartenhuis in elkaar.” Wellicht is ze een van de oudste studenten die aan de protesten deelnamen. Tijana besloot op latere leeftijd terug te studeren en belandde zo midden in de studentenprotesten. “Wat de studenten vooral doen met hun protesten is de bevolking weer verenigen, en dat is net de grote angst van Vučić. Het geeft ons opnieuw hoop, ik zie het ook bij mensen van mijn generatie”, getuigt ze.
Biologiestudent Tatjana: “Vučić heeft ons alleen maar strijdvaardiger gemaakt”
En dat is voelbaar in Kula zelf. “De enige manier waarop Vučić de verkiezingen hier wint, is door ze te stelen”, meent Dayin, inwoner van Kula. Dat wantrouwen is verre van ongegrond. Enkele dagen voor de verkiezingen eind maart duiken er plots heel wat nieuwe bewoners op in de stad.
“’s Nachts lopen er mannen met maskers rond om mensen te intimideren en op een avond weerklonken schoten. Twee weken geleden werden we zelfs met de dood bedreigd”, vertelt Vladica Klajić, een student die opkomt bij de verkiezingen.
“Normaal stellen de lokale verkiezingen helemaal niets voor. Maar de voorbije twee weken is de president al twee keer campagne komen voeren en waren er bezoeken van ministers in elk naburig dorp. In de media is dit het enige waar ze het over hebben.”
Op de verkiezingsdag rijden grote bussen rond zonder nummerplaten en een grote groep motoren baant zich een weg door de stad naar de stembussen. Rond de middag verlaat een gemaskerde knokploeg het lokale voetbalstadion. Ze vallen omstanders, onder wie journalisten, aan met stokken en keren terug naar het stadion, waar ze politiebescherming genieten.
Klokslag 23.00 uur bindt Vučić er geen doekjes om: zijn SNS-partij heeft in Kula gewonnen. Nochtans zijn de meeste stemmen op dat moment nog niet aangekomen in het stadhuis om geteld te worden. Uiteindelijk behalen de studenten de hoogste score, maar geen meerderheid – die is voor de SNS en haar coalitiepartners.
“We hebben voor onszelf uitgemaakt dat we nu kalm moeten blijven en ons moeten focussen op de nationale verkiezingen. Het feit dat ze zoveel energie hebben gestoken om in Kula te winnen, toont duidelijk dat ze aan het panikeren zijn”, vindt Vladica. “Dat is het teken dat we goed bezig zijn.”
Ondanks hun eerste nederlaag op lokaal niveau heeft de Studentenlijst de parlementsverkiezingen gisteren (25/10) gewonnen. De partij werd gevormd door universiteitsstudenten, maar geen van hen stond daadwerkelijk op de lijst. De kandidaten waren weinig bekende experts, sporters, boeren en kunstenaars. Deze fotoreportage werd in juni 2026 gepubliceerd in Apache Magazine, voor de nationale verkiezingen.
