https://taz.de/Wer-reinigt-unsere-oeffen.title: Ausbeutung von Reinigungskräften: 16 Stunden Putzen am Tag
https://taz.de/Wer-reinigt-unsere-oeffen.author: Sophie Fichtner und Malene Gürgen
https://taz.de/Wer-reinigt-unsere-oeffen.text:
Ausbeutung von Reinigungskräften: 16 Stunden Putzen am Tag
Menschen aus Osteuropa werden nach Deutschland gelockt, um für einen Hungerlohn Toiletten sauber zu machen. Einblicke in ein kriminelles System.
D ie Männer und Frauen kommen mit dem Flixbus aus Bulgarien nach Deutschland, zum Busterminal am Hauptbahnhof Frankfurt am Main. Die Anreise haben sie selbst bezahlt, aber das Geld, so denken sie, wird ihr neuer Arbeitgeber erstatten. In einem Wohnhaus im Norden der Stadt bekommen sie einen auf Deutsch verfassten Arbeitsvertrag vorgelegt. Niemand von ihnen spricht Deutsch. Sie unterschreiben trotzdem. Denn die Informationen aus dem Werbevideo, das ihnen die Vermittlungsagentur geschickt hatte, klangen überzeugend: ein gut bezahlter Job in Deutschland, mit einem deutschen Arbeitsvertrag, geregelten Arbeitszeiten, Krankenversicherung und Weihnachtsgeld.
Mehr als tausend Bulgarinnen und Bulgaren wurden mit diesen Versprechen nach Deutschland gelockt. Die Realität sah anders aus: Toiletten putzen, 10 bis 16 Stunden am Tag, für 3 bis 5 Euro die Stunde.
2026 steht ihr ehemaliger Chef in Koblenz vor Gericht: Svetoslav Petrov, Geschäftsführer der Reinigungsfirma Terra Cleaner. Das Unternehmen war für die Reinigung von rund 150 Sanitäranlagen in ganz Deutschland zuständig, hauptsächlich in Einkaufszentren, teils auch in Bahnhöfen, Raststätten oder in Museen.
An einem Donnerstag Anfang Mai nimmt Petrov in der ersten Reihe des riesigen Gerichtssaals Platz, hinter ihm sitzt sein Sohn Nino. Beide Männer tragen Jogginganzüge und die Haare kurz rasiert. Was Richter und Anwälte sagen, wird ihnen von Dolmetschern übersetzt, die dicht in ihre Ohren sprechen. Neben den beiden Petrovs sind zwei leitende Angestellte der Firma angeklagt: Nikolay Videnov, wie Svetoslav Petrov ebenfalls aus Bulgarien stammend, und Bettina Freise, die als das Gesicht der Firma in Deutschland auftrat und als Ansprechpartnerin für die Einkaufszentren fungierte.
Dem Gerichtsprozess gingen aufwendige Ermittlungen voraus. Allein die Anklage umfasst 179 Seiten, es geht um Menschenhandel, Zwangsarbeit, Steuerhinterziehung und die Veruntreuung von Arbeitsentgelten. Der Prozess gibt einen seltenen Einblick in ein weit verbreitetes Geschäftsmodell, das die Firma Terra Cleaner über Jahre hinweg in einem Ausmaß betrieben hat, das weit über das hinausgeht, was über ähnliche Fälle bekannt ist.
Der Fall offenbart ein größeres System
Nach mehreren Monaten Verhandlung fällt im August das Urteil. Für den Kopf der Firma, Svetoslav Petrov, gibt es fünfeinhalb, für seinen Sohn und Stellvertreter viereinhalb Jahre Haft, Videnov bekommt dreieinhalb und Freise zweieinhalb Jahre Haft. Ursprünglich hatte die Staatsanwaltschaft noch deutlich höhere Strafen gefordert, dass die Angeklagten geständig sind, wirkt sich jedoch strafmildernd aus. Während die beiden Petrovs und Nikolay Videnov auch für Menschenhandel verurteilt werden, reicht es bei Bettina Freise nur für das Vorenthalten von Arbeitsentgelten in 200 Fällen und Beihilfe zur Steuerhinterziehung.
Doch die ausbeuterischen Zustände in der Reinigung von Sanitäranlagen sind damit keineswegs beendet. Denn hier geht es um mehr als eine einzelne Firma. Bei unseren Recherchen zum Fall Terra Cleaner sind wir auf ein kriminelles System gestoßen, in dem seit fast 20 Jahren die Situation von Menschen aus Osteuropa ausgenutzt wird, um sie für einen Hungerlohn in Deutschland Toiletten putzen zu lassen, während die Einnahmen zu einem großen Teil am deutschen Staat vorbeigeschafft werden. Immer wieder stehen Menschen deswegen vor Gericht – und immer wieder tauchen neue Firmen auf, die dieses Geschäftsmodell weiterführen.
Grundlage für das Geschäftsmodell ist die Pachttoilette: In Einkaufszentren, Kaufhäusern, Raststätten, Bahnhöfen, teilweise auch in kommunalen Einrichtungen werden die Toilettenanlagen an externe Reinigungsfirmen verpachtet. Im Gegenzug behalten die Firmen das Tellergeld, das Kund:innen zahlen, um auf die Toilette zu gehen. Heutzutage sind es meist 70 Cent, fast jeder hat sie schon einmal auf so einen Teller gelegt.
An stark frequentierten Standorten kommen dabei bis zu 1.000 Euro pro Tag zusammen. In bar und ohne, dass dafür eine Quittung herausgegeben werden muss. Ideale Voraussetzungen für mehrfachen Betrug. Betrug am Kunden, der davon ausgeht, dass das Tellergeld direkt an die Reinigungskräfte geht. Betrug an den Angestellten, die weit unter Mindestlohn bezahlt werden. Betrug an den Verpächtern, denen gegenüber sich die Firmen in der Regel auf die Einhaltung gesetzlicher Standards verpflichten. Und Betrug am Staat, dem durch Steuerhinterziehung Millionen entgehen.
Die Menschen, die unter diesen Bedingungen arbeiten, haben Angst. So viel Angst, dass uns vereinbarte Interviews mit Beschäftigten immer wieder kurzfristig abgesagt werden. Zu groß ist die Sorge vor persönlichen Konsequenzen, und das anscheinend zu Recht. Der taz ist ein Fall bekannt, bei dem ein Mitarbeiter eines solchen Reinigungsunternehmens, der in einem Medienbericht anonym zitiert wurde, anschließend von seinem Arbeitgeber ausfindig gemacht und sanktioniert wurde.
Anhand des Gerichtsprozesses, durch Gespräche mit Mitarbeiter:innen von Beratungsstellen und durch interne Dokumente aus den Ermittlungen, die der taz vorliegen, lässt sich die Vorgehensweise der Firma Terra Cleaner dennoch nachzeichnen.
Über Vermittlungsagenturen und Anzeigen warb die Firma in Bulgarien gezielt Menschen mit geringer Bildung an, die kein Deutsch sprechen. Von Frankfurt aus wurden sie auf die verschiedenen Einsatzorte in Deutschland verteilt und in eigenen Wohnungen untergebracht.
Sechs Tage pro Woche, zehn Stunden pro Tag
In der Regel mussten die Angestellten bei Terra Cleaner mindestens zehn Stunden am Tag an sechs Tagen in der Woche arbeiten, an einigen Standorten sogar an sieben Tagen. Dafür erhielten sie maximal 50 Euro Lohn plus 5 Euro Verpflegungsgeld pro Tag bar ausgezahlt. Ein streng hierarchisches System aus einfachen Angestellten, Objekt- und Gebietsleiter:innen sorgte für Disziplin. Dazu kamen hohe Umsatzziele für die einzelnen Standorte und regelmäßige Bestrafungen in Form von Geldstrafen, fristlosen Kündigungen und, nach Angaben der Angestellten, teils auch körperlicher Gewalt.
Die Vernehmungen der Angestellten durch den Zoll geben Einblick darin, wie genau dieses System funktionierte. Beschäftigte, die aus Sicht der Firmenleitung zu wenig Tellergeld erwirtschafteten, bekamen bis zu 500 Euro von ihrem Lohn abgezogen. Die teils verwahrlosten Unterkünfte, in denen die Angestellten untergebracht waren, wurden regelmäßig von der Firmenleitung kontrolliert. Wurden dabei teurere Lebensmittel in den Kühlschränken gefunden, galt das als Beleg dafür, dass die Angestellten Tellergeld geklaut hätten. Wer in welcher Region putzte, legten Petrov und seine leitenden Kollegen fest, oft wurden Angestellte von einem Tag auf den anderen in ein anderes Einsatzgebiet verfrachtet.
Für einen Mitarbeiter, der verdächtigt wurde, Tellergeld gestohlen zu haben, wurde ein „Schlägertrupp organisiert“, der den Mann verprügelte und sein Auto zerstörte. In den Sanitäranlagen selbst wurde anhand des Wasserverbrauchs berechnet, wie viele Toilettengänge in etwa an einem Tag stattgefunden hatten. Diese Zahl wurde mit dem eingenommenen Tellergeld verglichen, bei Abweichungen gab es Strafen.
Im Fall von arbeitsrechtlichen Kontrollen gab es genaue Anweisungen, wie die Reinigungskräfte auf welche Frage antworten und über ihre eigenen Arbeitsbedingungen lügen sollten. In auf Bulgarisch verfassten Aushängen mit der Überschrift „Fragen bei einer Inspektion“ war etwa festgehalten, dass die Angestellten angeben sollten, nie mehr als acht Stunden am Tag zu arbeiten. Außerdem wurde ihnen verboten, bei etwaigen Kontrollen Protokolle der Vernehmungen zu unterschreiben.
Das eingenommene Tellergeld mussten die Angestellten am Ende des Tages in beschriftete Plastiktüten verpacken, sogenannte Safebags, ein Foto davon an ihren Gebietsleiter schicken und die Tüten anschließend in Tresoren in den Unterkünften verschließen. Einmal in der Woche wurde das Tellergeld von den Gebietsleitern der Toilettenanlagen abgeholt und nach Mommenheim bei Mainz gebracht. Das dortige Wohnhaus der Familie Petrov diente als inoffizielle Firmenzentrale.
In der Garage wurden die Münzberge mit zwei Geldzählmaschinen gezählt: Der kleinere Teil ging in eine offizielle, bei der Bundesbank registrierte Maschine und wurde danach auf das Firmenkonto eingezahlt und regulär versteuert. Der größere Teil wurde mit einer zweiten, unregistrierten Maschine gezählt und anschließend in den Restaurants der Einkaufszentren und anderen Geschäften gegen Scheine eingetauscht. Die Reinigungskräfte bekamen davon ihre 50 Euro Tageslohn, der Rest ging an die Familie Petrov und ihre leitenden Angestellten. So erhielt etwa Bettina Freise nur 200 Euro pro Monat offiziell als Lohn überwiesen, weitere 3.800 Euro bekam sie als „Bonus“ bar ausgezahlt – in Münzen.
Betrogen wurden durch dieses Geschäftsmodell nicht nur die Reinigungskräfte, sondern auch der deutsche Staat. Das Gericht bezifferte den Schaden, der durch nicht gezahlte Steuern und Sozialversicherungsbeiträge entstand, auf fast 11 Millionen Euro.
wochentaz
Dieser Text erschien zuerst in der wochentaz, unserer Wochenzeitung von links!
In der wochentaz geht es jede Woche um die Welt, wie sie ist – und wie sie sein könnte. Eine linke Wochenzeitung mit Stimme, Haltung und dem besonderen taz-Blick auf die Welt. Jeden Samstag neu am Kiosk und natürlich im Abo.
Zum Geschäftsmodell gehört, die prekäre Situation der Angestellten in Bulgarien auszunutzen. Viele von ihnen sind Roma, die auch in Bulgarien diskriminiert werden. Ein Grund dafür, dass es auch Angestellte gibt, die nach einem Heimaturlaub in Bulgarien – für den ihnen bei Terra Cleaner gekündigt wurde – erneut bei der Firma in Deutschland anheuern, obwohl sie mittlerweile wissen, was sie dort erwartet. Für den Vorwurf der Zwangsarbeit, den die Anklage im Prozess gegen die Reinigungsfirma erhoben hatte, reicht es daher im Urteil nicht.
Die Vorgehensweise von Terra Cleaner ist dabei kein Einzelfall, sondern steht symptomatisch für eine Branche, in der solche und ähnliche Geschäftsmodelle der Normalfall sind.
Schon 2015 ergeht ein Gerichtsurteil gegen die beiden Betreiber der Reinigungsfirma The Cleaning Company, die im Jahr 2007 gegründet wurde, dem Jahr, in dem Bulgarien und Rumänien der EU beitraten. Die Firma soll ab 2008 osteuropäische Reinigungskräfte als Scheinselbstständige beschäftigt und so weniger als den Mindestlohn gezahlt haben, auch Sozialversicherungsbeiträge wurden umgangen. Für beide Firmeninhaber gibt es Bewährungsstrafen. Der eine heißt Udo R., ist ehemaliger Polizeibeamter und betreibt noch weitere Reinigungsfirmen. Der andere heißt Svetoslav Petrov.
Ihn hält das Urteil offenbar nicht davon ab, dieses Geschäftsmodell weiter voranzutreiben, im Gegenteil. Bereits seit 2012 ist er offiziell Miteigentümer der Firma Terra Cleaner, die 2009 von seiner Schwägerin noch unter einem anderen Namen gegründet wurde. Die Firmengeschichte ist auffällig: Mehrfach gibt es Wechsel unter den Gesellschaftern und Geschäftsführern, immer wieder wird die Geschäftsadresse verlegt.
Im Laufe der Jahre entsteht eine verschachtelte Struktur aus verschiedenen Gesellschaften, auf dem Papier teilweise von Petrovs Frau geführt. Das Unternehmen, das in Zeitungsartikeln von 2014 noch als „Firma mit tadellosen Ruf“ mit „vergleichsweise guten“ Arbeitsbedingungen beschrieben wird, expandiert dabei stetig und ist schließlich in Einkaufszentren in ganz Deutschland tätig, von Wilhelmshaven bis Ulm. Terra Cleaner betrieb etwa Toiletten bei Galeria Karstadt, im Skyline Plaza in Frankfurt, im Hamburger Billstedt Center, in der Duisburger Königsgalerie oder im City Rondell in Villingen-Schwenningen.
Der Zoll beendet die kriminellen Geschäfte
Im Frühling 2025 ist es damit schlagartig vorbei: Am 31. März führt der Zoll bundesweit Razzien in Sanitäranlagen durch, die von Terra Cleaner betrieben werden, auch mehrere Unterkünfte der Angestellten und der Geschäftssitz der Firma werden durchsucht. Mehr als 100 Angestellte werden zu ihren Arbeitsbedingungen befragt. Vorausgegangen waren umfangreiche Ermittlungen, für die ein anonymer Hinweis eines Beschäftigten der Auslöser gewesen sein soll. Mehrere Monate wurden die Telefone der Betreiber und leitenden Angestellten von Terra Cleaner abgehört.
Die Razzien bedeuten das Ende von Terra Cleaner – aber nicht das Ende der Ausbeutung. Das Unternehmen wird einem Insolvenzverwalter unterstellt. Dieser verkauft die Betriebsausstattung an ein anderes Reinigungsunternehmen: Die Bulger Service GmbH, der Name steht für Bulgaria-Germany, geführt vom Bulgaren Viktor Rushanov.
Rushanov scheint eine Art Doppelleben zu führen. Für ein deutsches Publikum präsentiert er sich im Karrierenetzwerk LinkedIn als Chef der Bulger Service GmbH. Auf seiner Facebook-Seite, wo er ausschließlich auf Bulgarisch Beiträge veröffentlicht, tritt er hingegen als Lokalpolitiker auf. Dort kritisiert er, wie es in der Region an „Möglichkeiten, Perspektiven und Unterstützung mangelt“. Gerade er als Unternehmer wisse, wie wichtig es sei, „schon von klein auf Disziplin, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und Werte zu vermitteln“. Dass Rushanov als Unternehmer selbst von der Perspektivlosigkeit seiner Landsleute profitiert, lässt er unerwähnt. Auch sonst fehlt jeglicher Hinweis auf seine Geschäfte in Deutschland, nur nebenbei erwähnt er, dass er auch in Deutschland Erfahrungen gesammelt habe.
Wie die Staatsanwaltschaft Koblenz auf Anfrage der taz mitteilte, wird seit Ende 2025 auch gegen die Bulger Service GmbH ermittelt. „Es besteht der Verdacht, dass die neue Firma das Geschäftsmodell der ersten Firma nahezu unverändert – und somit ebenfalls in strafrechtlich relevanter Weise – fortführte“, so die Pressesprecherin. Mindestens 23 ehemalige Terra-Cleaner-Standorte soll Bulger Service übernommen und teilweise mit demselben Personal weitergeführt haben. Ermittelt wird nun gegen 52 Beschuldigte, wieder geht es um Ausbeutung und Steuerhinterziehung. Ende August wurden bereits erste Haftbefehle vollstreckt.
Ermittlungen wie die gegen The Cleaning Company, Terra Cleaner und Bulger Service gibt es immer wieder. 2011 wird der Fall einer Frau aus Bonn bekannt, deren Firma für die Reinigung von 50 Toiletten in ganz Deutschland zuständig war. Steuerfahnder fanden in ihrer Garage 40.000 Euro in Münzen, um das Geld zu beschlagnahmen, rückten sie mit einem Lkw an. In Cottbus musste sich 2022 die Geschäftsführerin einer Toilettenreinigungsfirma wegen Steuerhinterziehung vor Gericht verantworten, aktuell läuft ein Prozess am Landgericht Krefeld, wo ein Unternehmer mit seiner Reinigungsfirma Angestellte aus Ghana in der Toilettenreinigung ausgebeutet haben soll.
Nicht der erste Fall in der Branche
Juristisch wird also immer wieder gegen diese Branche vorgegangen. Doch wie kann es sein, dass ein offensichtlich kriminelles Geschäftsmodell trotzdem immer weitergeführt wird?
Das hat auch damit zu tun, dass die Einkaufszentren keine Verantwortung für die Arbeitsbedingungen in den Sanitäranlagen übernehmen, die sie verpachten. Die taz hat stichprobenartig mehr als 20 Einkaufszentren angefragt, die ihre Toiletten an Terra Cleaner verpachtet hatten, dazu die beiden größten Auftraggeber, den Einkaufszentren-Betreiber ECE und den Kaufhauskonzern Galeria. Die Antworten klingen ähnlich: Mit den Reinigungsfirmen werde vertraglich vereinbart, dass diese sich an gesetzliche Vorschriften halten müssen. Weitere Prüfungen seien nicht durchgeführt worden, in die „internen Beschäftigungsverhältnisse eines externen Dienstleisters“ habe man „nur begrenzte Einblicks- und Einflussmöglichkeiten“.
Selbst strafrechtliche Ermittlungen führen offenbar nicht in jedem Fall dazu, dass die Verträge mit den Reinigungsfirmen gekündigt werden. Im Bikini Berlin, einer Shoppingmall direkt am Zoologischen Garten, sitzt Anfang November ein Mann am Tresen vor den Toiletten im ersten Obergeschoss. Es ist derselbe, der schon bei Besuchen im Juni und im Oktober dort saß. Wortlos wechselt er das Geld, auf dem Teller liegen ein paar Münzen. 70 Cent kostet der Toilettengang auch hier. „Bulger Service“ steht auf dem Schild neben ihm. Das Bikini Berlin möchte auf Anfrage keine Auskünfte über Verträge mit anderen Unternehmen geben. Beauftragte Dienstleister würden sie aber „zur Einhaltung aller gesetzlichen Bestimmungen und Vorschriften verpflichten“. Trotzdem verdient der Mann hinter dem Tresen vermutlich deutlich weniger als den gesetzlichen Mindestlohn.
Mitarbeit: Joanna Khandjieva, Philipp Nierle, Timur Vorkul
Gemeinsam für freie Presse

https://taz.de/Volkabstimmung-ueber-Reic.title: US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien: Volksabstimmung über Reichensteuer scheitert
https://taz.de/Volkabstimmung-ueber-Reic.author: Hansjürgen Mai
https://taz.de/Volkabstimmung-ueber-Reic.text:
US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien: Volksabstimmung über Reichensteuer scheitert
Die „Proposition 40“ sah vor, dass kalifornische Milliardäre eine einmalige Abgabe auf ihr Vermögen zahlen sollen. Auch von links gab es an dem Vorstoß Kritik.
Wähler im US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien haben eine Reichensteuer auf das Nettovermögen von Ultrareichen abgelehnt. Eine entsprechende Volksinitiative, über die die Wähler in der vergangenen Woche abgestimmt hatten, ist laut vorläufigen Hochrechnungen gescheitert. Auch wenn die Auszählung der Stimmen noch nicht abgeschlossen ist, liegen die Nein-Stimmen mit mehr als sechs Prozentpunkten uneinholbar vorne.
Die als „Proposition 40“ bekannte Initiative sah vor, dass Einwohner in Kalifornien, deren Nettovermögen eine Milliarde US-Dollar übersteigt, eine einmalige Steuer in Höhe von 5 Prozent auf ihr Vermögen zahlen müssen. Ein Großteil dieser Einnahmen sollte dazu dienen, Kürzungen bei den staatlichen Gesundheitsmitteln auszugleichen. Befürworter der Steuer erklärten, dass damit innerhalb von fünf Jahren geschätzte Einnahmen von mehr als 100 Milliarden Dollar hätten erzielt werden können.
Der Senator Bernie Sanders aus Vermont, einer der Vorreiter in der progressiven linken Politikszene, bezeichnete den Vorschlag im Vorfeld der Wahl als einen bedeutenden Schritt, um die extreme Vermögensungleichheit einzudämmen und sicherzustellen, dass die Superreichen ihren fairen Beitrag leisten. Der demokratische Gouverneur des Bundesstaats, Gavin Newsom, warnte hingegen, dass die Maßnahme die wohlhabendsten Einwohner dazu bewegen könnte, Kalifornien zu verlassen – und so auch ihre Steuergelder abzuziehen.
Kalifornien ist abhängig von den Einkommenssteuern der Reichsten
Die Gegner der Maßnahme hatten laut Washington Post etwa 250-mal mehr Geld aufgebracht als deren Befürworter. Einige reiche Einwohner des Bundesstaates, darunter die Google-Mitbegründer Sergey Brin und Larry Page, hatten bereits vor der Abstimmung begonnen, ihre Verbindungen zum Bundesstaat zu kappen. Brin selbst hatte mehr als 100 Millionen Dollar aus seinem Privatvermögen beigesteuert, um die Vermögenssteuer zu besiegen. Auch Facebook-Gründer Mark Zuckerberg hatte gewarnt, dass er Kalifornien den Rücken kehren würde, sollte die Steuer eingeführt werden.
Die Befürworter der geplanten Steuer – darunter die einflussreiche Gewerkschaft SEIU United Healthcare Workers West – argumentieren, dass sie notwendig sei, um Kürzungen bei den Bundesmitteln auszugleichen. „Es ist an der Zeit, diese Steuern zu erheben, damit wir sicherstellen können, dass unser Gesundheitssystem weiterhin stabil bleibt“, sagte Lorena Gonzalez, Präsidentin der kalifornischen Arbeitervereinigung CFLU.
Doch einige traditionelle Verbündete der Demokraten, darunter Planned Parenthood und die kalifornische Lehrergewerkschaft CTA, sprachen sich gegen das Vorhaben aus. Sie äußerten Bedenken hinsichtlich der Verteilung der Steuereinnahmen sowie der möglichen Auswirkungen auf den Haushalt des Bundesstaates. Der kalifornische Haushalt ist nämlich in hohem Maße von der Einkommenssteuer der reichsten Einwohner des Bundesstaates abhängig.
Bislang scheiterten Vermögenssteuern zumeist
Vermögenssteuern auf Reiche wurden weltweit schon früher erprobt – mit einer überaus enttäuschenden Bilanz. Selbst der französische Ökonom Gabriel Zucman, ein vehementer Befürworter der Vermögenssteuer, schreibt in seinem neuesten Buch, dass frühere Vermögenssteuern „im Großen und Ganzen kläglich gescheitert“ seien. Ein zentrales Problem bestehe darin, dass Vermögenssteuern häufig Schlupflöcher aufwiesen, die es den Reichen ermöglichten, ihr Vermögen in Sicherheit zu bringen, schrieb er. Auch bei der Debatte um den kalifornischen Vorschlag ging es darum, dass manche Superreiche ihren Wohnsitz verlegen würden, um der Steuer zu entgehen.
Um diese Mängel aus früheren Vermögenssteuern zu vermeiden, haben die Initiatoren von „Prop 40“ versucht, potenzielle Schlupflöcher zu schließen. So wurde die Steuer als eine einmalige, rückwirkende Abgabe konzipiert, die an den Wohnsitz der Milliardäre zum Stichtag 1. Januar 2026 geknüpft ist. Damit sollte verhindert werden, dass sich die Betroffenen der Steuerlast einfach durch einen Wohnsitzwechsel entziehen.
Neben den bereits erwähnten Google-Mitgründern Brin und Page hatten auch mehrere andere wohlhabende Personen Kalifornien bereits vor dem Stichtag verlassen. Bei diesen weiteren Milliardären handelt es sich etwa um den umstrittenen deutsch-amerikanischen Tech-Investor Peter Thiel oder den Regisseur und Filmproduzenten Steven Spielberg. Allein die bisherigen Abwanderungen hätten die möglichen Einnahmen der Vermögenssteuer um etwa 30 Milliarden Dollar reduziert, so Stanford-Ökonom Joshua Raugh.
Das Scheitern der Steuer auf Superreiche in Kalifornien dürfte weitere Pläne dieser Art erst mal auf Eis legen – zumindest bis zum Präsidentschaftswahlkampf 2028.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Most Americans want Democrats focused on ending Iran war, lower costs: Poll
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
US voters want Democrats focused on ending Iran war, lowering costs: Poll
Poll shows Americans want the US Congress to address the cost of living in its first 100 days, and 71 percent want an end to war with Iran.
A new poll shows that the majority of Americans want the Democrats in Congress this January to deliver an end to the war in Iran, reverse US President Donald Trump’s trade policies, and bring down the high cost of living.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday found that 71 percent of Americans supported Congress passing legislation to end the war with Iran, including 93 percent of Democrats and 51 percent of Republicans. About 62 percent backed repealing Trump’s import tariffs, while nine in 10 respondents said Congress should focus on the cost of living during its first 100 days.
The war with Iran and Trump’s tariffs have both contributed to economic pressures, linking voters’ concerns about living costs to the administration’s foreign and trade policies.
Americans also expect some degree of cooperation between the White House and the incoming Congress. Large majorities of respondents from both parties said it was important for Trump to work with Democrats, and for Democratic leaders to try to work with the president.
Political retaliation against the Trump administration is a lower priority. Forty-two percent said it would be bad for the country if the new Congress tried to impeach Trump, compared with 33 percent who thought it would be good.
Democrats will have between 54 and 56 Senate seats next year, depending on results from uncalled races in Mississippi and Alaska. But delivering on voter priorities could still be difficult. Most bills need 60 votes to overcome a Senate filibuster, and Trump can veto legislation that passes both chambers.
Repealing tariffs or reversing other administration policies would therefore require either sufficient Republican support or a willingness to confront the president politically.
Seth Masket, a political science professor at the University of Denver, said voters are motivated by opposition to the Trump administration on several fronts, including the economy, the war, corruption and immigration enforcement.
“They want to see Democrats working to fix these things. And also to some extent, to hold the Trump administration accountable,” Masket told Al Jazeera.
A fight over who leads the Democrats
The pressure to deliver on those priorities is unfolding alongside a growing dispute over who should lead the Democratic Party.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll did not measure public support for individual congressional leaders. It did, however, find that the Democratic Party itself remains unpopular, with 45 percent of respondents viewing it favourably and 51 percent unfavourably.
Hakeem Jeffries is widely expected to become speaker of the House, despite calls for an alternative. No challenger has publicly emerged, but a Change.org petition urging Democrats to reject his leadership has attracted more than one million signatures. House Democrats are due to hold leadership elections on November 18 and 19.
The Senate contest is less settled. Chuck Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since 2017, faces calls to step aside. Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen has said Schumer should not receive a “blank check” and is considering a possible challenge. Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has backed Van Hollen.
The backlash reflects broader dissatisfaction with the party’s direction. Jeffries and Schumer have been criticised over their positions on Israel and Gaza, their relationships with corporate donors and pro-Israel lobbying groups such as the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), and what voters see as a failure to confront the Trump administration forcefully.
The Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), which counts several elected officials among its members, has not backed Jeffries or Schumer for their respective leadership posts. In a statement to Al Jazeera, the DSA said Democrats must reject “half-measures” and deliver on popular policies.
“We the people must be a counterweight both to the internal politics of Congress and the corporate donors who want to keep business as usual,” DSA spokesperson Priscilla Yeverino wrote to Al Jazeera.
Political commentator Bea Neilson said some progressives see the two leaders as representing an older Democratic establishment that is out of step with the party’s base.
“They want an avatar of a fighter,” Neilson told Al Jazeera.
But Neilson argues that the role of the House speaker is not simply to dictate the party’s legislative agenda. Rather, they respond to the positions of lawmakers across the caucus, working with policy committees and other groups to identify legislation that can secure enough votes to pass.
Individual members or blocs of lawmakers can withhold their support, making the job an exercise in negotiating competing interests as much as setting political direction.
Masket agreed that the effectiveness of congressional leaders is often measured less by their public speaking than by their ability to manage their caucuses and get legislation through Congress.
“People wanting their speaker or a Senate majority leader to be a more inspiring leader, I think they’re just asking for the wrong person,” Masket said. “That’s the wrong title for that role.”
That role, he suggested, may fall more naturally to the next generation of presidential contenders, who are expected to begin emerging early next year.
The leadership elections will take place before the new Congress begins in January. The larger question for Democrats is whether their leaders can turn a sweeping electoral mandate into tangible change.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Trump administration seeks to cut food aid for more than six million people
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Trump administration seeks to cut food aid for more than six million people
Trump’s proposal builds on earlier cuts to federal food aid programme used by more than 36 million low-income Americans.
The administration of United States President Donald Trump has proposed new eligibility requirements for the country’s largest food aid programme that would see some 6.3 million people removed from it.
The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) published a proposed rule (PDF) on Tuesday that would end automatic eligibility in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), doing away with current provisions that automatically make households eligible for the programme if they meet state-administered requirements for another programme, called Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF).
“These revisions would ensure that SNAP benefits are targeted to needy households that have qualified for TANF assistance while still aligning categorical eligibility’s statutory purpose of simplifying program administration,” the agency said in the proposal, which will be open to public comments for 30 days.
More than 36 million people are currently enrolled in SNAP, which is the largest federal food aid programme for low-income families. An individual in the programme receives an average of about $190 each month, while a household receives an average monthly benefit of $356 in groceries.
The SNAP programme itself requires that households earn less than 130 percent of the federal government’s poverty level to qualify. Currently, households that qualify for the TANF programme – which has requirements that vary by state and can accommodate households earning up to 200 percent of the federal poverty level – are also automatically eligible for SNAP.
According to the USDA, the proposed changes would remove about 17 percent of SNAP beneficiaries from the programme, some 6.3 million people. The cuts would also have other one-off effects, including removing 1.8 million children from a federal programme providing them with free school lunches, because they would no longer qualify for the SNAP programme.
Democratic lawmakers have criticised the Republican administration’s attempt to cut the federal food aid programme.
“The proposed rule would make it harder to meet basic needs and roll back efforts to streamline federal programs,” Minnesota Democratic Representative Angie Craig said in a statement on Monday.
“SNAP is a highly effective and efficient program when it is allowed to work as designed,” Craig’s statement continued. “Unfortunately, the Trump administration and the outgoing Republican majority in Congress have undermined the program’s integrity at every turn, harming millions of vulnerable Americans in the process.”
Democratic Senator Cory Booker from New Jersey called the proposal “despicable” in a social media post on Monday.
“Trump is set to kick millions more people off of SNAP, when Americans are already struggling with grocery prices. It is despicable. We need to be helping people afford groceries, not deepening cuts to the safety net that keeps families from going hungry,” Booker said.
Builds on previous Trump moves targeting food aid
The new cuts build on previous changes to the SNAP programme by the Trump administration, which has said many of those receiving aid through the federal government are not in need of it.
Some 5.5 million people lost access to SNAP benefits under Trump already, due to changes mandated by the July 2025 Big Beautiful Bill. The legislation expanded work requirements for beneficiaries and made certain categories of immigrants ineligible for the aid. States struggled with new administrative changes and with covering additional costs the federal government passed on to them under the bill.
Then, in November 2025, Trump briefly withheld funding for the SNAP programme entirely, using it as leverage to force Democrats to agree to passing a federal budget. The Democrats refused, and as a result, the federal government was shut down for more than a month. Towards the end of that impasse, Trump refused to use emergency funds to cover the SNAP programme.
At the time, Trump said the administration of former President Joe Biden had been responsible for burdening the government with “billions of billions” of dollars in more spending because of the programme. The benefits, Trump claimed in a Truth Social post without evidence, had been “haphazardly ‘handed’ to anyone for the asking, as opposed to just those in need, which is the purpose of SNAP!”
The Supreme Court eventually struck down lower court rulings, saying Trump could not legally withhold the funding for SNAP, just as lawmakers in Congress reached an agreement to pass a new federal budget and reopen the government.
The Trump administration has continued to push for changes to SNAP.
In December 2025, the administration threatened to withhold funding for the programme from 21 states that refused to hand over data on beneficiaries to the federal government, which the administration said it needed to examine in order to cut fraud.
The new proposal is now open for public comment for the next 30 days.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: FDA warns of rare eye condition causing blindness from GLP-1 weight loss medications
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Maya Yang
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a new warning on GLP-1 medications – which can facilitate weight loss – over a rare eye condition that could lead to sudden and permanent blindness.
On Monday, the FDA announced that it is requiring all GLP-1 medications – including Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Wegovy, Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound, as well as Sanofi’s Soliqua – to include information about the potential risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, also known as NAION, on warning labels.
NAION is a rare condition involving sudden reduction of blood flow to the optic nerve, in turn resulting in acute, painless, decreased vision in one eye, including permanent vision loss, the FDA warned.
Common risk factors of NAION include diabetes, smoking, hypertension, as well as hypercholesterolemia. It is the most common cause of acute optic nerve injury in individuals over 50 years old, with an annual average of 2.3 to 10.2 cases out of 100,000 people above that age. There is for now no treatment to reverse vision loss from NAION.
According to the FDA, the agency began looking at potential links between GLP-1s and NAION after a 2024 study published in the journal JAMA Ophthalmology. The study found an increased risk of NAION among patients using GLP-1 medications.
Despite identifying several limitations of the study, the FDA said it “determined that further assessment of the potential increased risk for NAION was warranted”.
The agency proceeded to review 126 clinical trials involving over 134,200 patients and identified 15 probable NAION cases, including 10 among GLP-1 patients; five in patients receiving placebo; and none in patients who were on glucose-lowering medications that were not GLP-1.
The FDA found a NAION incidence rate of 6.4 cases per 100,000 person-years among GLP-1 patients, compared to 3.8 cases among patients on placebo or alternative glucose-lowering medications.
“NAION cases have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 RA products,” the FDA said. “FDA concluded that there is a potential increased risk of rare NAION events in patients taking GLP-1 RAs.
“Based on these findings, FDA is requiring that application holders add information about the risk for NAION to the Warnings and Precautions section of labeling of all GLP-1 RAs.”
In response to the FDA announcement, a Novo Nordisk spokesperson told the Guardian that the pharmaceutical company “continues to believe the data do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship and we remain confident in the benefit-risk profile of our GLP-1 medicines.”
The statement also said: “Patient safety is a top priority for Novo, and we continue to monitor the safety of our medicines, review new research and work with health authorities around the world.”
The Guardian has reached out to Eli Lilly and Sanofi for additional comment. Eli Lilly had previously said it is aware of publications on the risk of NAION among GLP-1 patients.
GLP-1 medications are mainly used by people with type 2 diabetes managing their blood sugar – or glucose – levels. Some of the medications are also used to help treat obesity. And some have been known to seek access to such drugs for cosmetic reasons rather than legitimate medical ones.
The FDA’s announcement comes amid warnings from the Netherlands-based non-profit Access to Medicine Foundation that the pharmaceutical focus on GLP-1 weight-loss drugs risks putting global insulin supply at risk.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Republicans elect Trump ally Jim Jordan as new US House minority leader
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Republicans elect Trump ally Jim Jordan as new US House minority leader
Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to succeed Mike Johnson as GOP House minority leader, promising unity and a robust opposition.
Washington, DC – One week after losing their majority in midterm elections in the United States, Republicans in the US House of Representatives have chosen Congressman Jim Jordan as their new minority leader.
In a secret ballot vote held on Tuesday, the Ohio lawmaker, who was first elected to the US Congress in 2007, won the support of his fellow party members to succeed Mike Johnson as the chamber’s top Republican.
The high-stakes decision comes as Republicans try to chart a path forward after a bruising midterm defeat in which Democrats flipped at least 40 seats nationwide.
Jordan had been vying with current House Majority Leader Steve Scalise for the role, which will carry a host of responsibilities as Republicans prepare to message against at least two years of Democrat-led investigations into US President Donald Trump’s administration and pick a 2028 presidential nominee.
In a reported letter to his fellow Republicans before Tuesday’s vote, Jordan described himself as a “battle-tested” leader who was ready to take on those challenges.
“I know what it will take to lead our Conference in the minority, to stay unified, and to coordinate and calibrate our response to the Democrats’ tactics”, he wrote. “We need a Leadership team that is active and engaged, forward-thinking and straight-shooting”.
Jordan, a top Trump ally, has been an influential voice in the Republican caucus. He cofounded the conservative House Freedom Caucus, which has frustrated many former and current Republican leaders and thwarted party-backed legislation.
The group’s chairman, Republican Congressman Andy Harris, congratulated Jordan after the vote, calling him “a fierce fighter, uniter, principled conservative, and relentless advocate for the American people”.
“Jim is exactly the right man for the job to fight back against the radical, crazy agenda of Democrats”, Harris said in a statement.
As the current chairman of the House Oversight Committee, Jordan has used his power to look into what he has argued is the weaponisation of government against Trump. He has led the panel’s investigations into former special counsel Jack Smith and Fulton County, Georgia, District Attorney Fani Willis, who both have unsuccessfully prosecuted the president.
Jordan’s allies on the panel were quick to praise his selection.
“Jim is a fighter and a convicted conservative”, Republican Congressman Brandon Gill wrote on social media. “He’s the original congressional brawler and is exactly what our Conference needs to lead us back to the majority”.
Jordan, who once worked as an assistant wrestling coach at Ohio State University, had faced allegations that he had knowledge of sexual abuse of student-athletes by the team’s physician, Dr Richard Strauss, from 1978 to 1998. Jordan has denied the allegations.
He previously made a short-lived bid for US House Speaker after Kevin McCarthy was ousted from the role in 2023.
Since then, Jordan has taken a less adversarial approach and aligned himself with Johnson and other member of current House Republican leadership.
Before Jordan’s victory was sealed, McCarthy went on a podcast after last week’s midterm results to offer some advice to the future leader of the US House Republican conference.
“You can’t just play it day by day”, he told his former aides on Glory, Grief and the Gavel. “You’ve got to have a strategy, because it’ll knock the Democrats off base”.
McCarthy added: “You better have an acknowledgement of what transpired in this last election. Because you got to tell the American people I heard you and it’s going to take time to earn your trust again”.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, cut off his ankle monitor, DoJ says
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
The 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, just days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California, authorities said on Tuesday.
Thomas Markle was in custody awaiting a hearing in federal court in Tampa, Florida, first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli said.
He was arrested shortly after he cut off the ankle bracelet at 145am, Essayli said.
Markle’s arrest on Friday followed the seizure of approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images in storage in the Los Angeles area, Essayli said.
During his arrest last week, he was taken from a senior care center in Lakeland by ambulance. Hours later, a judge allowed Markle to be released on the condition that he be electronically monitored, which typically means wearing an ankle tether.
The judge also ordered a mental competency exam and a report by 20 November.
His daughter, Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex married Prince Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. She is an American citizen and actor who starred in the US television drama “Suits”.
Meghan recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father’s former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to police in London in 2019.
“It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” Meghan said of the letter. “I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.”
Thomas Markle was living in the Philippines this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US.
His arrest followed reports by The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, that Meghan’s half brother found a collection of child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. That discovery led to information about two US storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
US Senate advances major bill boosting energy infrastructure
Rare bipartisan bill requires data centres to pay for infrastructure, but environmental groups say it falls short.
The United States Senate has voted to move forward on a bipartisan bill that would speed up the process to build new data centres and energy infrastructure in the country.
Nearly all of the chamber’s Republicans, as well as more than a dozen Democrats, voted 73-25 on Monday to take up the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which supporters, including US President Donald Trump, have said is necessary to meet the nation’s growing demand for electricity.
“This Bill is a BIG WIN for U.S. ENERGY INDEPENDENCE and DOMINANCE”, Trump posted on social media Monday as he encouraged lawmakers to support it.
The legislation would overhaul the permitting process for major energy projects – both clean energy and fossil fuel-run – across the US, reduce deadlines for environmental reviews and impose restrictions on when projects can be challenged in the country’s courts. It would also force owners of energy-hungry data centres to pay for the infrastructure that is needed to power them.
Growing anger in the US over those facilities’ use in powering artificial intelligence (AI), which has resulted in rising electricity bills for customers across the country, helped fuel last week’s takeover of the US Congress by Democrats.
“The people sent us a very clear message on Tuesday that they expect us to lower the costs in their daily lives,” Democratic Senator Martin Heinrich, the ranking member on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, said on Monday. “We don’t have to wait for the new Congress to start lowering costs. We can do that today.”
Authors of the bill claim it will provide $19bn in savings on residential electricity bills through 2040. The number of solar and wind projects connecting to the US electric grid would be doubled, with data centres paying $55bn over the next 10 years to cover their power usage.
But despite the bill’s claims of increasing clean energy projects, environmental organisations are opposed to the legislation. They argue it would also lock in development of fossil fuels, weaken environmental laws and make it harder for US residents to challenge projects in their communities.
Earlier this year, a coalition of national groups – including the Climate Justice Alliance, Indigenous Environmental Network and Western Environmental Law Center – issued a joint statement opposing the bill.
“We cannot allow the lies to continue, as the facts are clear: If this backroom permitting reform deal is pushed through, it will enable a no-guardrails buildout of dangerous projects that will harm our health and environment, drive up energy costs, and violate our rights,” they said in September.
“This will be especially harmful for communities of color and lower income neighborhoods already overburdened by pollution and climate impacts.”
While the legislation received rare overwhelming support from both major political parties, the Democrats’ midterm win could complicate its final passage.
Some in the party argue that the legislation should be shelved until new Democratic majorities in the US House and Senate are sworn in early next year.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is on track to become the body’s new speaker in January, criticised the bill last week, warning it “falls short” in several areas.
“We must once again support the clean energy economy and combat the climate crisis with the fierce urgency of now,” a Jeffries spokesperson said in a statement released to the Associated Press.
Jeffries’s office added: “Leader Jeffries will not rubber-stamp legislation that emerges from the Senate without more constructive involvement with our Caucus as we fight to make life more affordable for the American people.”

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Israeli opposition hurries to seize control as new Knesset is sworn in
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
Opposition lawmakers have wasted no time after Israel’s new Knesset was sworn in, deploying their majority to seize control of the legislature from Benjamin Netanyhau and his allies.
Although they are still too divided to form a government, the opposition requested a vote for a new speaker, who sets the Knesset’s agenda. Once Netanyahu loyalist Amir Ohana has been replaced, the six opposition parties will be able to work on key legislation even if they broker a coalition.
Priorities include setting up a state commission of inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attacks and introducing term limits for Israel’s prime ministers, which could block Netanyahu from taking power again. He has ruled Israel for 19 of the last 30 years.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, now has the presidential mandate to try to form a government. If he fails to broker a deal within six weeks, a second candidate – probably Netanyahu – will get a second chance. Further failure is likely to lead to another election.
Netanyahu responded to the swearing in of the new Knesset on Tuesday with a racist attack on two Palestinian-led opposition parties, whose voters were key to unseating his coalition, calling their lawmakers “terror supporters”.
Eisenkot denounced his speech as a “delusional, divisive, hate-filled and shameful” exploitation of a state occasion, that showed the prime minister was unfit for office.
Yair Golan, leader of the centre-left Democrats, and Yoav Segalovich, a Jewish-Israeli former police chief who ran on the slate of Islamist Ra’am party, both walked out of Netanyahu’s speech in protest.
Palestinian citizens of Israel make up about 20% of the country’s population. Netanyahu put attacks on these voters and their parties at the heart of his campaign, and since polling day has promoted groundless accusations of fraud in their communities in a bid to undermine results.
Election officials say there was no evidence of irregularities that affected the election outcome or compromised its integrity.
A period of prolonged, difficult coalition negotiations or even a new round of elections would extend Netanyahu’s hold on power as caretaker prime minister. But if the fractured opposition can make progress on key legislation, his grip on the state would be weakened.
Eisenkot’s Yashar party submitted a series of bills to the Knesset moments after the swearing in, with backing from other opposition parties.
In addition to term limits and the 7 October inquiry, legislation includes several bills designed to revoke the “judicial overhaul” pursued by Netanyahu, which weakened the power of Israel’s judiciary and the attorney general.
Ohana has tabled the vote on a new speaker to replace him for next Tuesday, the latest date possible. The opposition have also nominated candidates to take over key defence and finance committees.
Eisenkot has admitted the path to power is “extraordinarily complex”, because of incompatible election promises made by different parties, but described ousting Netanyahu as a national emergency that could require breaking promises.
At the swearing-in ceremony, the president, Isaac Herzog, warned lawmakers they should do everything in their power to avoid a second election.
“Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals … Look upon one another with generosity. There is much work to be done here, and it requires the ability and experience found in every part of this House.“

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Parents sue to stop Washington state trans sports ban that could require ‘invasive’ genital exams
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Sam Levin
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Parents of student athletes in Washington state have sued to block a ballot initiative banning transgender girls from women’s sports teams, calling the measure discriminatory and warning it would lead to “invasive” genital examinations for female athletes.
Last week, voters in the solidly Democratic state passed Initiative 638, a major setback for LGBTQ+ rights amid the “blue wave” of the US midterm elections. Nebraska, Colorado and Arizona adopted similar anti-trans sports bans, though advocates say Washington state’s policy is particularly extreme due to its medical sex verification requirement for all girls who want to play team sports.
The lawsuit was filed in state court on Monday by parents of trans and cisgender girls; TransFamilies, a non-profit Washington advocacy group; and the Washington Education Association, the teachers’ union. They are represented by the American Civil Liberties Union of Washington; Legal Voice, a group that fights gender discrimination; and Pacifica Law Group, a local firm.
Washington’s measure mandates that girls provide documentation from medical providers about their sex before they join women’s teams, either through hormone or genetic tests or examinations of their “reproductive anatomy”. The policy does not apply to boys.
Doctors, teachers and parents have raised alarms about the potential of forcing girls to undergo genital exams, saying the enforcement mechanism was a severe privacy violation and would discourage all girls from joining sports. Proponents argue that the ban, funded by Brian Heywood, a conservative hedge fund manager, protects “fairness” in girls’ sports.
The law applies to students in elementary, middle and high school. School officials said earlier this year that they were aware of only about 10 trans sports players statewide, a tiny fraction of the state’s 200,000 student athletes.
The suit argues that the measure violates Washington’s constitution, including by infringing on students’ privacy and violating equal rights protections by only applying to girls. The ban also violates an anti-discrimination law that protects trans people, the suit says.
Tiffani Lennon, executive director of Legal Voice, noted that Washington state has for 20 years allowed trans youth to play on teams that match their gender: “This is a fabricated issue being manufactured to create alarm. They’re intending to send a message to trans youth that we don’t want you visible, and they are willing to put in place really extreme measures to ensure that it terrifies enough people to go run and hide.”
The plaintiffs include a parent of a 17-year-old trans girl who participates in team sports at her high school and who fears being outed and kicked out of athletics under the measure. Parents of two cisgender female athletes also joined the suit, saying they oppose the “intrusive” sex verification requirements.
“If you really want fairness in sports, why would you subject girls to sex verification? Why would you dissuade girls from participating in sports?” said Lennon. “It’s clearly discriminatory.”
On Monday, the Seattle public schools board of directors also voted in favor of allowing the district to take legal action against the ban, which is due to go into effect on 3 December.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Hegseth lays it on thick for Trump to shave off fallout from Iran war
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Robert Tait in Washington
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
There was no talk of “weirdos or beardos” – two among several categories whom Pete Hegseth has made it known are unwelcome in the US armed forces under his watch.
But a man with a beard had to be uppermost in his mind for him to meet journalists in the Pentagon at the ungodly hour of 8am on Tuesday.
Why else would he be addressing a group he commonly disses as the “fake news”? Consorting with the fourth estate is not the sort of thing this defense secretary does first thing in the morning – or indeed, any time of the day.
He had ostentatiously avoided holding a single press briefing in nearly six months – thus driving an armored personnel carrier through all normal notions of accountability as an unpopular war with Iran rumbled on during an election campaign.
Yet here he was summoning media attention at a time when he – and they – should have been having breakfast.
For this sudden departure from type, praise belongs to Thomas Massie, the outgoing – and lusciously hirsute – Republican representative from Kentucky, who has launched articles of impeachment against Hegseth, citing high crimes and misdemeanors in his scattergun stewardship of the US’s mighty military.
It was this that had driven the self-anointed secretary of war to call an unaccustomed news conference.
Hegseth, who has railed against beards and poor grooming in the military, presumably feels deep contempt for Massie’s facial follicles.
But he made no mention of them in a 25-minute appearance bristling with affronted indignation. In fact, he contrived to omit mention of Massie’s name at all.
Instead, Hegseth applied the adjective “disgruntled” to his nameless nemesis several times in an address that seemed to throb with his own feelings of disgruntlement – not least with the journalists he was meeting for the first time in months.
Syntactically, that probably represented an upgrade on Donald Trump’s description of Massie the day before as “a stone cold loser”.
Massie, a contrarian in Republican congressional ranks, has introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth that are likely to find support from Democrats – and maybe some fellow Republicans.
Among them lie serious charges, including violating the US constitution and waging war against Iran without congressional authorization.
Hegseth also stands accused of violating Congress’s war powers resolution, which requires the withdrawal of US forces from unauthorized hostilities after 60 days.
There are also accusations of carrying out illegal military strikes against suspected drug traffickers in the Caribbean, unlawfully capturing Venezuela’s president, Nicolás Maduro, unauthorized military strikes against Yemen and ignoring laws intended to minimize civilian casualties.
Finally, he is accused of abusing his power by retaliating against Mark Kelly, a Democratic senator, who had urged members of the military to disobey illegal orders.
For Hegseth, it was all a “farce and a stunt”.
“In the 250 years of our American republic, no secretary of war or secretary of defense has ever been impeached for carrying out lawful military operations, and in our case, successful ones at that,” he complained.
“Not once, war powers resolution or not, not under Reagan in Lebanon, not under Clinton in Kosovo, not under Obama in Iraq and Syria, not under Biden in Iraq and Syria. That’s the standard.”
But the “disgruntled” Massie wanted to turn all that upside down “over policy disagreements”.
“That’s what it is,” Hegseth said. “Not high crimes, not misdemeanors, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offenses the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause.”
They hadn’t done it to Lloyd Austin, his Democratic predecessor at the Pentagon after he oversaw a botched withdrawal from Afghanistan and then disappeared for several days to undergo treatment for cancer, the defense secretary wailed.
But lest anyone thought he was playing the victim, he asserted the disclaimer “this isn’t about me”.
It was – at least partly – about America’s “brave warriors”.
“Put the secretary on trial today and the men and women who carry out the orders tomorrow,” Hegseth said. But be warned, if they want to go after the warriors, “they are going to have to come through me”.
But most of it all, it was about Trump, who was impeached twice in his first presidency and who Hegseth now said he was proud to serve as a proxy target.
“Now they’re trying a third time, this time against a member of his cabinet,” he said. “If standing with President Trump puts me in that company, I’ll take that company every day of the week.”
Then it was time to attack the very class of people he had reluctantly invited to the Pentagon. The media could not admit Trump’s military success against Iran, he claimed, “because they hate the president more than they love our country or our troops”.
It was at that point that it became clear the audience Hegseth was primarily addressing was not in the Pentagon briefing room, but in the White House.
By fervently defending Trump – who has so far stuck by Hegseth as a man who “won two wars” – he was shielding himself, all the more so amid rampant speculation that the president could still make him a fall guy for last week’s Republican midterm debacle.
Then it was to the hazardous territory of journalists’ questions. One was about Stephen Miller, Trump’s chief policy adviser and newly appointed chief of staff.
“An incredible American patriot,” Hegseth gushed, no doubt wisely, given his delicate predicament. “We’ve got no better friend at the department of war than Stephen Miller. He’ll be a fantastic chief of staff.”
The tone changed markedly when someone asked about Vice-President JD Vance, who has blamed the Iran war for the Republicans’ defeat, and who everyone assumes harbors fierce presidential ambitions.
“I respect the vice-president greatly, and I’m certainly not going to exchange any finger pointing,” Hegseth said.
And then, in an aside uttered so quickly it could almost have passed unnoticed were it not such a well-aimed blow, he added: “Thankfully, politics is not really my thing.”
The audience of one in the White House would surely have heard – and understood whose “thing” it was.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in tit-for-tat move
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in tit-for-tat move
Relations between Moscow and Chisinau have worsened since the 2022 Ukraine war.
Russia has expelled a Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Chisinau’s expulsion of a Russian embassy employee over the crash of a drone in Moldova.
Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Tuesday that it had summoned Moldova’s ambassador, Lilian Darii, and informed him that a member of the Moldovan embassy’s staff had been declared unacceptable “on the basis of the principle of reciprocity”.
“A strong protest was lodged with the ambassador after the Moldovan authorities on October 23 declared an employee of the Russian embassy in Chisinau persona non grata,” the ministry said in a statement.
It said Moldova’s decision was made “under the formal pretext of the alleged discovery on the territory of the republic of debris of an unmanned aerial vehicle carrying explosives”, calling it “another unfriendly step”.
The ministry said the “true goal” of the move was “to further undermine the centuries-long history of Russian-Moldovan relations”.
‘Crashed near homes’
Last month, Moldovan President Maia Sandu said a “Russian attack drone” had violated the country’s airspace and “crashed near homes and an energy facility”.
Moldova then declared a staff member of the Russian embassy “persona non grata”.
Drones have penetrated Moldovan territory on multiple occasions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Since then, Russia’s relations with former Soviet states, such as Moldova, have hit an all-time low, compounded by the push by some of those states to join the European Union.
On Sunday, Moldova officially launched a new power line connecting the country to neighbouring Romania and the European grid to reduce its dependence on Russian energy.
The 400-kilovolt extra-high-voltage line, which runs from the city of Vulcanesti to Chisinau, allows Moldova to cut reliance on the Cuciurgan thermal power plant in Transnistria.
Other European-aligned states in the Black Sea region say they are experiencing renewed attacks allegedly carried out by Moscow, such as a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast in October.
