“We believe the Speaker should represent the Democratic voters, not just the Democratic establishment,” says the petition put forward by social media influencer Nicole Whitted.
The petition calls on representatives to examine Jeffries' public record, policy positions, campaign donor record, and leadership.
'It’s not enough to criticise the war we need to defund it'
- Etan Mabourakh, National Iranian American Council
An Economist/YouGov poll published last month found that Jeffries had just a 26 percent approval rating among registered voters.
Critics say that one reason Jeffries' popularity has taken a hit is that he is an avid supporter of Israel.
The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) ranks among his top campaign-financing contributors.
Israel's favourability among Americans has plummeted in recent years, according to a poll from the Chicago Council on Global Affairs, which shows Israel has its lowest favourability since 1978.
According to Track AIPAC, Jeffries has taken $1.5m in donations from the pro-Israel lobbying group. Aipac took to social media platform X to congratulate Jeffries on his win.
A resurfaced clip of Jeffries speaking at a United Jewish Appeal event where he says “Israel today, Israel tomorrow, Israel forever” is making the rounds online, with influencers urging people to call their representatives.
New Yorkers protest against Jeffries
On Monday, Brooklyn For Peace held a rally outside of Jeffries' office in New York City's Brooklyn borough.
Dozens of protesters gathered holding signs that read “Stop weapons to Israel” and chanting “hey hey, ho ho, this genocide has got to go”, in reference to the war on Gaza, where over 74,500 Palestinians have been killed.
The organisers handed a letter to one of the lawmaker’s staffers, urging Jeffries to oppose all further funding for the war on Iran, oppose supplying weapons to Israel, block and cut Trump’s Pentagon war budget, and abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), among other demands.
Brooklyn for Peace chair Charlotte Phillips had a message for Jeffries saying, “We need you to stand up and take action to protect us and our children from what's happening now, which is of such tremendous harm to us future generations and to our entire community.”
Etan Mabourakh, the group's executive director, says Jeffries’ foreign policy stance is making him unpopular with constituents.
“Anyone seeking to lead not just the Democratic Party but the American people must back broadly popular and urgent positions: defunding the illegal war on Iran, blocking weapons used in war crimes by the Israeli government, blocking the proposed merger of the US and Israeli militaries, and welcoming immigrants and abolishing ICE.”
Jeffries has previously called the Iran war illegal and unconstitutional, but Mabourakh says those words are not enough.
“It’s not enough to criticise the war; we need to defund it.”
Among the protesters was New York resident Mitty Owens, who says Jeffries represents “profit over people and Israel over the US”.
Owens believes that Jeffries is standing on the wrong side of history.
“Holocaust experts and academics say this is genocide. It’s obvious that Israel targets and kills civilians, aid workers, and journalists. There's no excuse whatsoever why a single dollar more should be going to Israel with no conditions whatsoever.”
He blames lobbying groups for the reason politicians like Jeffries have not stood against Israel.
Owens is calling for a new Democratic leader in the House, saying that Jeffries has “lost his way”, going so far as to call him Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's puppet.
“Why is he veering so far from what he knows is right? Because of the level of money that's in there, he's listening to Aipac and following corporate interests over listening to constituents”.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘O Brasil tem sido o adulto na sala’, afirma jurista da USP sobre política internacional de Lula na COP31 e G20
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Larissa Bohrer
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A participação do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na 31ª Conferência do Clima da Organização das Nações Unidas (COP31), em Antália, na Turquia, nesta semana, será marcada por dois importantes elementos: a passagem de bastão da presidência provisória do evento e a divulgação de números positivos a respeito da queda no desmatamento e nas emissões de gases.
Em conversa com o Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, Paulo Borba Casella, professor de Direito Internacional da Universidade de São Paulo (USP), avalia que o Brasil “naturalmente tem protagonismo na agenda ambiental”. Setores ambientais internacionais vinham observando as eleições brasileiras com certa preocupação em caso de vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), justamente por possíveis retrocessos.
“[É muito importante] Ter Lula reeleito e ter a passagem do embaixador Correia do Lago para o colega turco na presidência da conferência, tanto pela agenda interna do Brasil como pela representatividade que o Brasil teve com o fato de sediar a COP30 e as sugestões que foram feitas”, analisa.
O evento no Brasil terminou com a confecção do “Mapa do Caminho”, que indica passos para que cada nação contribua para uma transição energética justa.
Além da ida à COP31, Lula participará do encontro da Asean (Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático), nas Filipinas, para fortalecer acordos comerciais com países asiáticos. Casella considera que buscar novos mercados é importante para diminuir a dependência com os Estados Unidos, que segue com a política tarifária sobre produtos brasileiros.
“O Brasil manteve e aumentou o seu volume de exportações no ano passado e, provavelmente, caminhamos para conseguir um resultado equivalente este ano. E o segredo está justamente em ampliar mercados e procurar parceiros que sejam mais confiáveis do que os Estados Unidos tem se mostrado com a atual administração”, pontua.
O professor avalia que, neste quarto mandato, Lula seguirá com sua habilidade diplomática cada vez mais apurada e que o Brasil, diante de tantas tensões globais, “tem sido o adulto na sala”. “O governo brasileiro tem sido muito mais razoável, sensato, enfatizando a necessidade de negociar e de manter os canais de diálogo abertos. Contrariamente às provocações e grosserias que têm sido feitas pelo governo Trump contra o Brasil e contra o governo brasileiro”, afirma.
Com relação à Cúpula de Líderes do G20, prevista para ocorrer nos dias 14 e 15 de novembro, em Miami, em que Trump e Lula terão o primeiro encontro após as eleições nos dois países, Paulo Borba Casella avalia que o presidente brasileiro chega fortalecido diante da comunidade internacional. O professor considera que é possível haver alguma farpa por parte de Trump, que tem se mostrado “alguém instável e temperamental”, mas que isso não deve ser considerado. Ele aposta, certamente, em uma postura dialogal e diplomática por parte de Lula.
“A relação entre os dois países é importante demais para ser excessivamente maltratada. Eles [EUA] já fizeram isso com as tarifas, com comentários sobre possíveis erros na eleição”, pontua. Quem deveria se preocupar com erros na eleição são eles, que não conseguem totalizar os votos tão rapidamente quanto o Brasil faz com o sistema de urnas eletrônicas. Esse sistema maluco de delegados que recebem votos para depois escolherem os dirigentes cria uma enorme incerteza. Então, em matéria de eleições, o Brasil tem um sistema eleitoral muito mais confiável e consolidado do que o dos Estados Unidos”, analisa.
Para ouvir e assistir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: House Republicans urge DoJ to further investigate ‘key witnesses’ in Epstein case
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Anna Betts
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Republicans on the House oversight committee released a report on Tuesday criticizing the federal government’s handling of the investigations into Jeffrey Epstein and his associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, and called on the Department of Justice to interview “key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records”.
“The federal government has failed the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s horrific crimes for decades,” James Comer, the Republican congressman who chairs the committee, said in a statement.
Comer also urged Congress to pass legislation he introduced that he said would “ensure witnesses and survivors and sexual crimes are not deterred from speaking freely by nondisclosure agreements”.
“We cannot undo the horrific harm inflicted on these women” he said. “But we must ensure that allegations of criminal activity are thoroughly investigated, survivors are protected, and those responsible are held accountable. The failures of the past must not be repeated.”
In a statement, a justice department spokesperson said: “The chairman’s recommendations have already been addressed.
“The attorney general has repeatedly said that the Epstein case is not closed and there is no statute of limitations on human trafficking.”
Shortly after Comer released the report, Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the committee, called the report “misleading” and “partisan”.
“Oversight Republicans have released a report based on an incomplete investigation and zero public hearings on Jeffrey Epstein” Garcia said. In his statement, he accused the justice department of continuing to “illegally withhold over 2.5m pages of documents” and said that there has been “no investigation of Ghislaine Maxwell’s transfer, and Attorney General Todd Blanche has yet to testify”.
The majority’s report outlines some of the findings that the oversight committee has come to during their 15-month long investigation into Epstein, including how Epstein cultivated and leveraged relationships with powerful people, and the failures of federal investigators and prosecutors, perhaps most notably the brokering of the controversial non-prosecution agreement and plea deal for Epstein in 2008, which led to his federal case at the time being shelved.
The panel’s investigation has included 19 transcribed interviews and seven depositions.
The report also claims that after the enactment of the Epstein Files Transparency Act last year, the justice department “failed to adequately communicate about document releases and failed to sufficiently protect survivors”.
It adds that “questions remain as to whether the DoJ has released all relevant documents”. Moreover, it states “given the speed with which EFTA records were released, several instances of deficient redaction exposed sensitive information of survivors”.
Among the recommendations, Comer is urging the justice department to further question and investigate Epstein’s longtime assistant, Lesley Groff, who testified before the panel earlier this year. Groff told lawmakers that she had no knowledge of Epstein’s crimes while working for him.
Comer also urged the justice department to investigate sexual assault allegations involving two men made by another one of Epstein’s former assistants, Sarah Kellen. Both men have denied any wrongdoing.
The Republican congressman also said the justice department should establish an “appropriate process for Epstein survivors and their representatives to access their personal files and records in unredacted form”, and more.
In a matter of weeks, Democrats will take over the committee in the 120th Congress. Garcia said: “We intend to hold real public hearings uplifting survivors and asking tough questions of the powerful men who associated with Epstein, including Donald Trump. Our work is just getting started.”

https://taz.de/Oezdemir-ueber-Roth/!6229.title: Özdemir über Roth: Alte Doppelspitze, neuer Streit
https://taz.de/Oezdemir-ueber-Roth/!6229.author: Benno Stieber
https://taz.de/Oezdemir-ueber-Roth/!6229.text:
Özdemir über Roth: Alte Doppelspitze, neuer Streit
Cem Özdemir kritisiert seine frühere Co-Vorsitzende: Ihre Aussage bediene das Narrativ einer Lobby, die die deutsche Politik bestimme.
Schon als sie noch zusammen die Grünen führten, waren Claudia Roth und Cem Özdemir öfter unterschiedlicher Meinung. Jetzt hat der baden-württembergische Ministerpräsident seine frühere Co-Vorsitzende wegen ihrer Aussagen in einem Podcast kritisiert: „Zu sagen, dass der Zentralrat der Juden Druck auf sie gemacht habe, halte ich für schwierig“, sagte Özdemir. Er selbst könne nur sagen, dass er mit dem Zentralrat immer gut zusammengearbeitet habe. Die Aussagen Roths seien vor allem deshalb problematisch, „weil es dieses Narrativ bedient: Da gibt es eine Lobby, die bestimmt die deutsche Politik.“ Und weiter: „Damit sollten wir sehr vorsichtig umgehen.“
Özdemirs Kritik greift in eine Debatte innerhalb der Grünen ein, die seit dem Wochenende tobt und das Verhältnis der Partei zu den Juden in Deutschland berührt. Im Podcast „Jung & Naiv“ hatte es die frühere Kulturstaatsministerin Claudia Roth vergangene Woche als persönlichen Fehler bezeichnet, in ihrer Amtszeit Akteure rund um den Film „No Other Land“ kritisiert zu haben. Das bereue sie heute. Bei der Abschlussgala der Berlinale 2024 hatten Äußerungen mehrerer Preisträger zum Krieg in Gaza eine Debatte über Antisemitismus in der Kulturbranche ausgelöst. Auch Claudia Roth war für ihr Verhalten damals in die Kritik geraten.
Der mediale Druck sei „massiv“ gewesen, sagte die langjährige Bundestagsabgeordnete im Podcast. „Es war so ein unfassbarer Druck vom Zentralrat, von unglaublich vielen Kreisen“. Im weiteren Gespräch hatte sie berichtet: „Manche gute Freunde von mir, ausländische Freunde, sagen: Wann befreist du dich endlich von dieser Schuld der Geschichte? Oder wann gehst du anders damit um?“
Problematische Aussagen korrigieren
Daraufhin hatten am Wochenende 50 Grüne Parteimitglieder einen offenen Brief an die Parteiführung geschrieben, in dem sie einen klaren öffentlichen Widerspruch des Bundesvorstands verlangten. Die Parteispitze müsse einer „Delegitimierung des Zentralrats der Juden“ entgegentreten, so die Verfasser. Zugleich würdigten die Unterzeichner Roths Engagement bei der Auseinandersetzung mit dem Nationalsozialismus. Gerade deshalb ginge es nicht darum, Roth „pauschal eine Gesinnung zuzuschreiben“, sondern darum, „problematische Aussagen zu korrigieren“.
Derweil stellte sich die Parteispitze hinter Claudia Roth. Die Parteivorsitzende Franziska Brantner bezeichnete Roths Äußerung als eine unglückliche Formulierung. „Sie hätte diese Aussagen von Dritten einordnen sollen, damit diese missverständlichen Interpretationen nicht möglich sind“, sagte Brantner.
Gegenüber dem Stern hatte Roth selbst bereits einen Teil ihrer Aussagen relativiert. Sie habe sich diese Aussagen ihrer Freunde „nicht zu eigen gemacht“, sondern lediglich zitiert.

https://www.thenation.com/article/societ.title: The EEOC Is Failing Workers While Hunting for Discrimination Claims From White Men
https://www.thenation.com/article/societ.author: Bryce Covert
https://www.thenation.com/article/societ.text:
The EEOC Is Failing Workers While Hunting for Discrimination Claims From White Men
Investigators are rapidly closing out claims of workplace discrimination so that they can search for the kinds of cases chair Andrea Lucas most wants to find.
Earlier this year, Sebrina, a direct-care worker in Pennsylvania who works in group homes assisting clients with disabilities with everyday tasks, was discussing a client’s medications with a coworker. When she told her coworker that one of the clients does in fact need seizure medications, despite her coworker’s claim to the contrary, the coworker called Sebrina a “bitch,” she recalled. Another time, that same coworker called her “colored.”
Sebrina, who asked to use only her first name because she’s in the middle of legal action, reported the incidents, as well as the fact that one of her clients told her that he was being abused by a different caretaker, to her boss. That’s when she was abruptly suspended. She was accused of not following instructions for a particular client, but she says she had been begging to get the relevant instructions for months to no avail. Meanwhile, the coworker who called her the slurs was simply told to apologize to her. Eventually Sebrina was fired on July 13 for, she says, failing to attend a meeting scheduled for July 18.
On June 29, Sebrina filed an inquiry with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the federal agency tasked with protecting private-sector workers from discrimination, claiming she had been illegally discriminated against. An agency investigator started looking into it on August 14. When an EEOC investigator investigates a case, they typically spend months probing whether the case has merit, soliciting the employer’s response and gathering documents to either pursue an EEOC lawsuit or help the employee do so. Instead, five days later the agency sent Sebrina a “right-to-sue” letter, which closed out the EEOC case without any investigation and left her to pursue justice in the courts. “It just happened so fast,” Sebrina said. “I wanted him to investigate.” Instead, she was on her own with no more information than when she had started.
Related Articles
Three sources within the EEOC, plus three employment lawyers who regularly bring claims to the agency, told The Nation that what Sebrina experienced is increasingly common. Their comments and statements from the agency’s chair demonstrate that under the second Trump administration, the EEOC, created by the Civil Rights Act of 1964, has focused on representing aggrieved white men and people with anti-trans complaints while shutting out those whom it has historically served. Since she was appointed to lead the EEOC by President Donald Trump, chair Andrea Lucas has increased pressure on agency staff to field far more inquiries without growing the backlog of cases, three agency sources tell The Nation. At the same time, she’s pushed them to spend disproportionate resources on her personal priorities. The combination of those factors means that more and more people are experiencing what Sebrina did: Investigators in EEOC field offices are rapidly closing out claims of workplace discrimination without thoroughly investigating them so that they can search for and sink time into the kinds of cases Lucas most wants to find.
Democrats in Congress can hold hearings and bring Lucas in to testify about her priorities, but they aren’t empowered to change agency policies. In fact, Trump just nominated Matt Zandi, who most recently served as chief of staff to Harmeet Dhillon, until recently the head of the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division, as an EEOC commissioner, which if confirmed will give the Republican members of the commission a quorum and majority for at least two more years. It would also allow President Trump to fire the remaining Democratic commissioner, Kalpana Kotagal, as he did with the other two Democratic commissioners, while still maintaining enough members for Lucas to set the agency’s rules and agenda.
Workers get only 90 days after receiving an EEOC right-to-sue letter to file a case in court. Sebrina spent sleepless nights googling and scouring TikTok and YouTube for someone who might take her case in time. “Any and everything,” she said. Over 20 attorneys turned her down. “I cried,” she said. “My little baby saying, ‘Mom, you got to close your eyeballs or they’re going to dry.’” With just 30 days left, she decided to go pro se and try to file the paperwork in court on her own, but she had to figure out how to get the $200 filing fee waived. Her blood pressure was sky-high from the stress; her psychiatrist recently advised her to take a break to protect her mental health. “I’m just trying to stop the timer from ticking,” she said. “It’s just a lot that’s dropped on me.”
Early last year, Lucas created a list of her own personal priorities for the EEOC—including claims from people who believe they were adversely affected in the workplace by so-called diversity, equity, and inclusion programs, such as white men who believe a woman or person of color unfairly got a promotion instead of them, and claims that are “defending the biological and binary reality of sex,” such as cisgender women who feel discriminated against for sharing a bathroom with a trans woman—and told agency officials to seek out cases that lined up with them. Prior EEOC commissioners said that violated the agency’s processes and exceeded her authority. Lucas has also prioritized religious bias and national-origin discrimination against American citizens who believe a foreign-born person unfairly got an opportunity instead of them. She posted a direct-to-camera video on X.com last year soliciting complaints from anyone who is “a white male who has experienced discrimination at work.”
In response to a request for comment, an EEOC spokesperson, “Under Chair Lucas’s leadership, the EEOC continues to deliver significant results for American workers.”
The EEOC, which has a budget of just $455 million to cover the country’s 136 million private-sector employees, has always had to prioritize some complaints over others. Before Lucas became chair, however, those priorities were determined by looking at data showing what kinds of discrimination were most prevalent, an EEOC staffer with knowledge said. “Historically, people of color and women file the greatest number of charges, because they disproportionately face discrimination in the workplace,” so those complaints were prioritized (though the EEOC has always pursued discrimination claims of all kinds). Now the determination is driven by the administration’s political priorities. But the focus on white men, for example, is “not what our body of data reflects,” the EEOC employee said.
According to The New York Times, cases from white men claiming so-called reverse discrimination have been “accelerated through the process,” and the director of at least one district (the EEOC divides the country into 15 districts) told staff that such cases should be designated as deserving the highest level of resources and time. The director also said that such cases can’t be sent to mediation—a process in which the EEOC helps try to broker a settlement—and require “special permission” to dismiss. The EEOC employee I spoke with has heard from people directly involved that Lucas has fought back against staff attempts to reach settlements in these cases because she instead wants to bring litigation. Cases involving DEI and gender identity are getting extra resources, the EEOC employee said, and are all being assigned attorneys. Lucas herself has gotten far more actively involved in them than previous chairs would get in specific cases, according to the EEOC staffer with knowledge.
And yet staff told the Times that they have struggled to find complaints Lucas wants that have merit or strong evidence. That requires them to spend even more time trying to put a flimsy case together. So complaints without merit that fall into Lucas’s priorities are now supplanting other kinds with merit, the staffer with knowledge said, and staff is focusing on the demographics of who filed the complaint instead of whether the complaint itself is worthy.
In addition to being directed to find cases that Lucas wants to focus on, expectations for field staff have been raised to unrealistic levels, the EEOC employee said. Beginning October 1, Lucas directed EEOC investigators in the agency’s field offices to complete five intake appointments every day, two EEOC staffers said. An effective intake typically takes an hour and a half to two hours to complete, the staffer with knowledge said. At the same time, Lucas and Thomas Colclough, the EEOC’s director of field management, have told the directors of the agency’s field offices that anyone who walks through their office doors must be served. The change appears at least in part to be Lucas’s attempt to make it easier for white men to access the agency. Lucas herself has assured people on X.com alleging the kind of discrimination she’s focused on that they can walk into EEOC field offices and get quick responses. In one post, she said she was “aware of & working to increase our interview availability.” In another, she said she was working on ensuring that “all field offices are equally welcoming and available to walk-in appointments.” Prior to Lucas’s becoming chair, goals for the number of intakes completed each day were set by each local field office based on their capacity, and most workers had to get initial online appointments to ensure that there was enough staff capacity for each. Outside of rare instances, employees have never before been asked to do five a day, the staffer with knowledge said.
In response to a request for comment, an EEOC spokesperson said, “Chair Lucas is proud of the agency’s efforts to serve more workers by expanding intake appointments and walk-in availability. In Fiscal Year 2026, charge inquiries reached an all-time high, while charge receipts increased 11 percent—the highest level in more than a decade. These results underscore the growing demand for the EEOC’s services and the importance of Chair Lucas’s commitment to evenhanded enforcement, expanded outreach, and ensuring all American workers understand their rights under federal civil rights laws.”
All the extra time diverted to intakes is less time that staff can spend investigating inquiries and charges or developing promising cases to litigate. “People are spending so much time putting out the immediate fires,” the EEOC employee said.
Meanwhile, staffing is at a nadir. The agency received 270,000 inquiries last fiscal year, a 9 percent increase over 2024, but it had the lowest number of staff to handle that work since at least 2005. Staffing has continued to decrease this year—the agency has just 1,693 employees to police discrimination in all private workplaces, a 26 percent decrease from its peak under President Joe Biden and down by a third since a high-water mark in 2010. Just a few hundred of those employees are the investigators who both handle new inquiries and investigate them if they become actual charges.
At the same time, aggressive goals have been put in place for making sure the backlog of inquiries and charges doesn’t grow beyond a certain length, the EEOC staffer with knowledge said, even as employees are being forced to field more inquiries. That’s led to a mass closure of inquiries—in which EEOC investigators don’t even look into a complaint and simply issue a right-to-sue letter—and the neglect of complaints with merit or even the potential to make systematic change.
“Staff are closing charges in order to meet the goals, in order to keep the inventory [of pending inquiries and charges] artificially low,” the EEOC employee said. “The agency has become sort of a right-to-sue machine.”
The impact on Americans who have experienced discrimination at work has been stark. Steve Auerbach, founding attorney at the Law Office of Steven T. Auerbach, and Rachel McElroy, an attorney at the McElroy Law Firm, say that clients have received right-to-sue letters before the agency has even asked their employers for a position statement, which is typically the first step in assessing all inquiries. Charges Auerbach has filed with the agency have been closed out incredibly rapidly. “We’re looking at days, when in the past it was months, if not longer,” he said. “It was rare for me to even hear back for six months.” One inquiry that he filed in mid-June was issued a right-to-sue letter 18 days later; another filed in early August got one in just eight days. McElroy has similarly seen clients get right-to-sue letters in a matter of weeks, while a previous case waited years.
Popular
“swipe left below to view more authors”Swipe →
Beginning last year, Nathan Simmons, an attorney at Kaplan Law Firm, would file an inquiry only to receive an e-mail demanding more information—information that had already been included in his inquiry on behalf of his client. The agency has sometimes ignored his response and then immediately issued a right-to-sue letter. “The new policy completely undermines the purpose of the EEOC,” he said.
“I can’t rely on them to do their job right now,” Auerbach said of the EEOC. And, he said, it’s happening even to cases that appear to have merit. “I’m seeing it in instances where it’s both clear-cut and a pretty good case,” he added. McElroy agreed that the cases getting closed out are surprising. “They’re just your average EEOC charges,” she said.
Both Auerbach and McElroy have simultaneously experienced a huge increase in calls from workers seeking legal help after being quickly issued a right-to-sue letter by the agency—the week we spoke, McElroy had gotten three, when before she would only get such calls “every once in a while.” Auerbach called it “frightening” given that workers only get 90 days to file a lawsuit after getting such a letter.
Even when the EEOC decides not to take a case, its investigation is a crucial component of getting justice for employees. Auerbach noted that he’s reluctant to file a lawsuit without having heard the employer’s side of the story—something the agency is skipping over now as it scrambles to issue right-to-sue letters. “I’m counting on that to see if this is a meritorious claim, and I’m being deprived of that,” he said. “Not every dispute belongs in front of a federal jury.” Meanwhile, without the agency’s having done any investigation of a charge, attorneys must compile all the necessary documents and evidence before the 90-day window closes, which is not always possible.
It’s already difficult for workers to find an employment lawyer to take a case like this. First, there just aren’t enough of them. “A lot of the big billboard attorneys, they’re personal injury attorneys and medical malpractice attorneys,” McElroy pointed out. There are far fewer lawyers who take civil rights cases, and those that exist can only take on so many cases at a time. Many won’t respond to every call that comes into their office.
Many workers also can’t afford to take their employers to court on their own, even if they can find lawyers. Few workers who represent themselves get a favorable ruling. If the EEOC isn’t even looking into whether to pursue their cases itself, they may end up with no recourse in a worthy case. “To be shut out and ignored by the agency that’s congressionally tasked with listening to them,” Auerbach said, “it’s insult to injury.”
“Workers that are most in need of the agency’s services can’t in fact benefit from those services and get left behind,” the EEOC employee said. “If you have no actual way to enforce your civil rights, are they meaningful?”

This is an entry from: Live: US Republicans derail bid to impeach Pentagon chief over Iran war
US says no need for new attacks but calls Iran's peace terms 'absurd'
10 November 2026 20:59 GMT
The US is downplaying the chances of a fresh attack against Iran even as it characterises Tehran’s conditions for a political settlement as “absurd”.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House that the war was “effectively over” and that there was “momentum” to end the conflict.
Trump has used deescalatory language since the Republican Party was badly defeated in US midterm elections on 3 November by the Democrats, who campaigned against the war and rising energy prices.
But Trump’s characterisation of ongoing talks was directly disputed by Mohsen Rezaei, a former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) commander who is secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Cesta básica em BH sobe 0,96% em outubro e compromete 54% do salário mínimo
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O preço da cesta básica em Belo Horizonte (MG) subiu 0,96% em outubro, na comparação com setembro, e chegou a R$810,73. Em um ano, o aumento acumulado na capital mineira foi de 13,15%. O encarecimento dos alimentos fez com que o trabalhador remunerado pelo salário mínimo precisasse comprometer 54,07% da renda líquida para comprar os 13 produtos que compõem a cesta.
Os dados são da Pesquisa Nacional da Cesta Básica de Alimentos, realizada pelo Departamento Intersindical de Estatística e Estudos Socioeconômicos (Dieese) em parceria com a Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento (Conab), divulgada nesta terça-feira (10).
Na prática, quem recebe o piso nacional de R$1.621 precisou trabalhar 110 horas e 2 minutos durante o mês de outubro para adquirir os alimentos básicos. Em setembro, eram necessárias 108 horas e 59 minutos. Já em outubro de 2025, o tempo exigido era de 103 horas e 50 minutos. Depois de pagar pela alimentação, restam menos da metade da renda líquida para despesas como aluguel, transporte, gás de cozinha, energia elétrica, saúde, educação e vestuário.
O levantamento aponta que a cesta básica ficou mais cara nas 27 capitais brasileiras pesquisadas. Belo Horizonte registrou o 11º maior valor do país. As cestas mais caras foram encontradas em São Paulo (R$951,37), Rio de Janeiro (R$939,39) e Florianópolis (R$927,82). Na outra ponta, os menores valores foram registrados em Aracaju (R$618,61), Maceió (R$661,69) e Salvador (R$677,77).
Em Minas Gerais, além da alta de 0,96% em outubro, a cesta acumula aumento de 12,09% entre dezembro de 2025 e outubro de 2026. Embora tenha apresentado uma das menores variações mensais do país, ficando atrás apenas de Macapá (0,95%), Belo Horizonte mantém uma trajetória de encarecimento dos alimentos ao longo do ano.
Tomate dispara e pressiona orçamento das famílias
Entre os produtos pesquisados, o tomate foi o que apresentou a maior alta acumulada em Belo Horizonte. Desde dezembro de 2025, o preço subiu 119,75%. Apenas em outubro, o aumento foi de 11,87%. Na comparação com o mesmo mês do ano passado, a alta chega a 85,44%.
Outros alimentos também registraram aumentos expressivos no acumulado do ano. O feijão carioca ficou 31,30% mais caro, seguido pela batata (28,77%), pelo leite integral (15,80%) e pelo arroz (13,97%). Também tiveram elevação a manteiga (13,14%) e a carne bovina de primeira (8,18%).
Na comparação entre setembro e outubro, oito dos 13 produtos pesquisados apresentaram aumento na capital mineira. Além do tomate, subiram o açúcar cristal (4,78%), o arroz (3,84%), a manteiga (2,88%), a carne bovina (1,24%), o feijão carioca (0,89%), o óleo de soja (0,26%) e o pão francês (0,05%). As reduções foram registradas na banana (-9,37%), no café em pó (-5,35%), na batata (-3,85%), no leite integral (-2,71%) e na farinha de trigo (-2,01%). Apesar das quedas pontuais, parte desses produtos continua mais cara do que no fim de 2025.
Salário mínimo necessário deveria ser de quase R$ 8 mil
O comprometimento da renda com a alimentação também evidencia a distância entre o salário mínimo vigente e o necessário para garantir condições dignas de vida aos trabalhadores e suas famílias.
Segundo o Dieese, o salário mínimo necessário para uma família de quatro pessoas deveria ter sido de R$7.992,47 em outubro. O valor corresponde a 4,93 vezes o piso nacional de R$1.621. O cálculo considera o custo da cesta básica mais cara entre as capitais pesquisadas, a de São Paulo, além das despesas com moradia, saúde, educação, transporte, lazer, vestuário, higiene e previdência.
Reforma tributária prevê alimentos com imposto zero a partir de 2027
Uma possível redução no custo dos alimentos poderá começar a ser sentida pelos consumidores a partir de janeiro de 2027, com a implementação da primeira etapa da reforma tributária aprovada durante o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). A mudança prevê alíquota zero da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), novo tributo federal, para os produtos que integram a Cesta Básica Nacional.
Uma simulação realizada pela Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV), em parceria com o Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS), estima que a mudança na tributação poderá reduzir entre 6% e 7% o custo da cesta de alimentos consumida pelas famílias beneficiárias do Bolsa Família.
O estudo aponta uma redução potencial de 6,6% nos preços de alimentos in natura e minimamente processados. Para ingredientes culinários processados, a estimativa é de aproximadamente 3,4%, enquanto os alimentos processados e industrializados poderiam apresentar queda de 7%.
A projeção considera efeitos semelhantes nas cinco regiões brasileiras: Norte (-6,7%), Nordeste (-6,8%), Centro-Oeste (-6,6%), Sudeste (-6,7%) e Sul (-6,7%). O exercício utiliza uma alíquota de referência de 7% e leva em conta a composição da cesta consumida pelas famílias atendidas pelo Bolsa Família.
A lista de alimentos com alíquota zero inclui produtos essenciais como arroz, feijão, leite, pão comum, macarrão, carnes, café, açúcar, farinha de mandioca, farinha de trigo e determinados tipos de queijo, entre outros.
A desoneração faz parte da transição para o novo sistema tributário, que prevê a substituição do PIS e da Cofins pela CBS em 2027. A mudança busca reduzir a carga tributária sobre os alimentos e ampliar o poder de compra da população, especialmente das famílias de menor renda.
Apesar da perspectiva de redução, a estimativa da FGV não significa que os preços necessariamente cairão na mesma proporção ou de forma imediata. O impacto efetivo dependerá também de como a redução dos tributos será repassada ao consumidor.

https://taz.de/Sitzung-des-schwarz-roten.author: Stefan Alberti
https://taz.de/Sitzung-des-schwarz-roten.text:
Sitzung des schwarz-roten Senats: Gaebler ganz gelassen
Der SPD-Bausenator gilt nicht als Freund der Linkspartei, verhandelt aber über eine Koalition mit. Bei Enteignung setzt er aufs Bundesverfassungsgericht.
Stadtentwicklungssenator Christian Gaebler (SPD) hat den vielfach als Einknicken empfundenen SPD-Umgang mit der Enteignungsfrage am Dienstag als quasi notwendig dargestellt. „Solange das Bundesverfassungsgericht dazu nicht Maßstäbe gesetzt hat, wie mit Vergesellschaftung nach Artikel 15 des Grundgesetzes und möglichen Enteignungen umzugehen ist, wird uns diese Diskussion weiterverfolgen“, sagte Gaebler. „Und das behindert Investitionen und Wohnungsbau.“ Dieses Thema müsse jetzt durch ein Landes- oder Bundesgesetz „soweit getrieben werden“, dass das Gericht sich damit befassen kann, äußerte sich Gaebler bei der Pressekonferenz nach der Senatssitzung.
Die SPD hatte in Person ihres Spitzenkandidaten Steffen Krach vor der Abgeordnetenhauswahl am 20. September durchweg zu verstehen gegeben, dass sie die Enteignungspläne der Linkspartei ablehnt. Doch am Ende der Sondierungen über eine rot-grün-rote Koalition stimmten die Sozialdemokraten einem Abschlusspapier zu, dessen Konsequenz die Vergesellschaftung von 160.000 Wohnungen großer Immobilienunternehmen wäre. Dieser Schritt würde sich in einem Berliner Landesgesetz wieder finden.
Offiziell sitzt Gaebler Dienstagmittag nur deshalb im Presseraum des Roten Rathauses, um aus der vorangegangenen Senatssitzung zu berichten. Doch einer Frage zu seiner Rolle bei den rot-grün-roten Koalitionsverhandlungen mag er trotzdem nicht ausweichen. Weil ihm die Antwort ja merklich die Gelegenheit gibt, der Diskussion einen neuen Dreh zu verpassen. Bei den Koalitionsgesprächen führt er die SPD-Verhandler in der Arbeitsgruppe Stadtentwicklung an, obwohl er in früheren Zeiten mehrfach andere Positionen als die bislang vereinbarten vertrat.
Gaebler äußerte sich auch auf die mehrfach aus der Berliner Wirtschaft zu hörende Kritik, allein die Debatte über Enteignung schade dem Wirtschaftsstandort und mindere Investitionsbereitschaft. „Das ist pures Gift für den Wirtschaftsstandort“, sagte etwa vorige Woche Handwerkskammerchef Jürgen Wittke. Laut Gaebler gibt es beim Bauen derzeit ohnehin „eine gewisse Zurückhaltung, auch ohne jede Vergesellschaftung“. Die Enteignungsdebatte hat für ihn eine verstärkende Wirkung.
Verordnung zu angespanntem Wohnungsmarkt
In der vorangegangenen Senatssitzung hatte die bis zur Bildung einer neuen Koalition weiter amtierende schwarz-rote Landesregierung sich selbst mit dem problematischen Wohnungsmarkt beschäftigt. Sie verlängerte eine Rechtsverordnung um fünf Jahre, die Berlin als „Gebiet mit angespanntem Wohnungsmarkt“ ausweist. Das soll Vorkaufsrechte zu begründen helfen und generell dazu beitragen, schneller mehr Wohnungen zu schaffen. Dazu gehört auch die sonst eingeschränkte Möglichkeit, die Umwandlung von Miet- in Eigentumswohnungen zu verbieten.
Gaebler rechnete vor, dass der Neubau der vergangenen beiden Jahre gereicht habe, um Neuzuzug nach Berlin auszugleichen. 2024 etwa hätten rund 16.000 neue Wohnungen ungefähr 15.000 neue Haushalte gegenübergestanden. Dass es dennoch weiter etwa 100.000 Wohnungen zu wenig in Berlin gebe, führte Gaebler auf den starken Zuzug 2015/2016 und 2022 – nach dem russischen Überfall auf die Ukraine – zurück.
Für die bis Ende 2031 verlängerte Verordnung müssen laut Baugesetzbuch Voraussetzungen erfüllt sein, etwa im bundesweiten Durchschnitt überdurchschnittlich stark steigende Mieten und ein geringer Wohnungsleerstand bei hoher Nachfrage. Berlin erfüllt laut Gaebler drei von vier Kriterien, nötig sei nur eins gewesen.

https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.title: « On baigne dans une angoisse permanente faite pour nous empêcher de réfléchir » : entretien avec Cédric Kahn, le réalisateur de « 15/18 »
https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.author: Michaël Mélinard
https://www.humanite.fr/culture-et-savoi.text:
Stress, exclusion, climat, Covid… Ces crises et pressions fragilisent la jeunesse. En tournant auprès d’adolescents soignés dans une unité psychiatrique, le réalisateur Cédric Kahn signe un tableau collectif passionnant sur la santé mentale des jeunes mais pas seulement. Documentaire et fiction se répondent avec malice dans « 15/18 », un film puissant et enthousiasmant.
Cédric Kahn explore sans relâche la trajectoire d’individus aux comportements border-line : la marge et la folie qui entourent un certain activisme politique dans le Procès Goldman, la paternité dysfonctionnelle dans Vie sauvage, la dérive criminelle dans Roberto Succo. Et la liste n’est pas exhaustive. Dans 15/18, le cinéaste s’attarde sur la santé mentale vacillante des adolescents en s’invitant dans l’unité psychiatrique d’un établissement public où arrive Lucia (excellente Malou Khebizi), une jeune fille de 17 ans, habituée du service.
Vie quotidienne, réunions de service des soignants, tensions, violences et solidarités entre les patients… Cédric Kahn, qui s’est judicieusement octroyé le rôle du psychiatre, dessine un tableau collectif quasi documentaire avant que le film entre goulûment dans la fiction lorsque le loup entre dans la bergerie.
Ce trublion a la malice d’Enzo, petit délinquant en bisbille avec la justice qui vient de faire une tentative de suicide. Sa présence menace l’équilibre fragile instauré jusque-là. Hommage aux soignants et au personnel de ces unités, le cinéaste signe un film puissant, parfois éprouvant qui se réinvente plusieurs fois au cours du récit.

https://taz.de/Amtsenthebung-Hegseths-im.text:
Antrag scheitert an Repubilkanern: Amtsenthebung Hegseths im US-Repräsentantenhaus gestoppt
Ein Konressabgeordneter wollte US-Verteidigungsminister Hegseth des Amtes entheben lassen. Sein Vorhaben wird allerdings bereits im Anfangsstadium gestoppt.
dpa | Die republikanische Mehrheit im US-Repräsentantenhaus hat den Versuch einer Amtsenthebung von Verteidigungsminister Pete Hegseth zunächst gestoppt. Mit 211 zu 204 Stimmen verfehlte der Vorstoß des Republikaners Thomas Massie gegen seinen Parteikollegen schon bei einer ersten Abstimmung die notwendige Mehrheit. Damit wurde das Anliegen formell an einen Ausschuss überwiesen, noch bevor die Parlamentskammer in der Sache über die gegen Hegseth erhobenen Vorwürfe abstimmen konnte.
US-Präsident Donald Trump zeigte sich nach der Abstimmung hocherfreut. Der Versuch sei „kläglich gescheitert!“, schrieb er auf seiner Plattform Truth Social.
Seine Republikaner haben im Repräsentantenhaus weiterhin die Mehrheit. Die vorige Woche bei den Midterms gewählten neuen Abgeordneten werden erst ab Januar ins Parlament einziehen. Dann werden die Demokraten in beiden Kammern eine Mehrheit haben – und könnten Hegseths Amtsgeschäfte erneut unter die Lupe nehmen.
Demokratin: „Es wird sehr, sehr viele Ermittlungen geben.“
Der aktuelle demokratische Minderheitsführer im Abgeordnetenhaus, Hakeem Jeffries, zeigte sich Reportern gegenüber kämpferisch. „Das ist nicht das Ende davon, es ist nur der Anfang“, zitierten ihn unter anderem die US-Sender CNN und CBS News. Die linke Kongressabgeordnete Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez sagte zudem: „Es wird sehr, sehr viele Ermittlungen geben. Ich gehe von vielen Vorladungen aus.“
Am Dienstag (Ortszeit) stimmten elf Abgeordnete der Demokraten nicht mit ab – damit stand zumindest die Möglichkeit im Raum, dass die Abstimmung über das Amtsenthebungsverfahren vielleicht auch anders hätte ausgehen können.
Doch selbst bei einem Erfolg im Repräsentantenhaus wäre für eine Amtsenthebung die Zustimmung des Senats, der zweiten Parlamentskammer, erforderlich. Dort bräuchte es eine Zweidrittelmehrheit – was aktuell und auch nach den neuen Mehrheitsverhältnissen im Januar als unwahrscheinlich gilt.
Vorwürfe auch wegen des Iran-Kriegs
Der aus dem Kongress ausscheidende Republikaner Massie hatte zuvor im Repräsentantenhaus Vorwürfe gegen Hegseth wegen dessen Vorgehen im Iran-Krieg erhoben. Streitkräfte seien in Kampfhandlungen gegen die Islamische Republik entsandt worden, obwohl der Kongress keine Ermächtigung erteilt habe, hieß es.
Dabei habe er auch Gesetze zur Minimierung ziviler Opfer missachtet. Zudem macht er Hegseth Vorwürfe im Zusammenhang mit Einsätzen des US-Militärs gegen die Boote mutmaßlicher Drogenschmuggler. Kritiker betrachten das Vorgehen als rechtswidrige außergerichtliche Tötungen.
Der Pentagon-Chef selbst wies die Anschuldigungen zurück. Bei einer Pressekonferenz vor der Abstimmung hatte er mit Blick auf den Iran gesagt, er werde sich nicht dafür entschuldigen, dass das US-Militär die militärischen Kapazitäten eines Landes zerstöre, das „Tod den USA“ skandiere. „Das Ganze ist eine Farce und es ist eine Inszenierung – und jeder weiß das“, sagte er.

Cérémonie du 11-Novembre imposée à l'école : le monde éducatif s'insurge
Publié le 11 novembre 2026
Depuis l'été 2026, une circulaire du ministère de l'Éducation nationale rend obligatoire l'organisation d'une cérémonie en hommage aux « morts pour la France » autour du 11 novembre, du CM1 jusqu'à la classe de terminale. Minute de silence, Marseillaise et port du Bleuet de France, cette directive suscite une vive contestation chez les enseignants et les syndicats.
Oui, on s’en doute : vous en avez assez
Voir ces messages d’appel au don, ça peut être pénible. Nous le savons. Et on doit bien vous avouer que nous préférerions ne pas avoir à les écrire…
Mais voilà : c’est crucial pour l’Humanité. Si ce titre existe toujours aujourd’hui, c’est grâce au financement régulier de nos lectrices et lecteurs.
- C’est grâce à votre soutien que nous pouvons exercer notre métier avec passion. Nous ne dépendons ni des intérêts d’un propriétaire milliardaire, ni de pressions politiques : personne ne nous dicte ce que nous devons dire ou taire.
- Votre engagement nous libère aussi de la course aux clics et à l’audience. Plutôt que de chercher à capter l’attention à tout prix, nous choisissons de traiter les sujets que notre rédaction juge essentiels : parce qu’ils méritent d’être lus, compris, partagés. Parce que nous estimons qu’ils vous seront utiles
À l’heure actuelle, moins d’un quart des lectrices et lecteurs qui viennent plus de 3 fois sur le site par semaine nous aident à financer notre travail, par leur abonnement ou par leurs dons. Si vous voulez protéger le journalisme indépendant, s’il vous plaît, rejoignez-les.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120379.title: USA nach den Midterms | Republikaner wenden Amtsenthebungsverfahren gegen Hegseth ab
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120379.text:
- Politik
- USA nach den Midterms
Republikaner wenden Amtsenthebungsverfahren gegen Hegseth ab
Ein Republikaner wollte US-Verteidigungsminister Hegseth des Amtes entheben lassen. Sein Vorhaben wird allerdings bereits im Anfangsstadium gestoppt.
Washington. Die Republikaner im US-Repräsentantenhaus haben ein Amtsenthebungsverfahren gegen US-Verteidigungsminister Pete Hegseth abgewendet. Die Abgeordneten stimmten am Dienstag mit 211 zu 204 Stimmen dafür, einen Antrag zur Einleitung eines sogenannten Impeachment-Verfahrens an den Ausschuss zurückzuverweisen. Der Antrag war am Montag von dem Trump-kritischen republikanischen Kongressabgeordneten Thomas Massie eingereicht worden. Hegseth steht nach der Wahlpleite der Republikaner bei den Midterms vor allem wegen des unpopulären Iran-Kriegs massiv unter Druck.
Die bei der Kongresswahl siegreichen Demokraten unterstützten das Amtsenthebungsverfahren. Da das US-Parlament bis Jahresende noch in seiner alten Zusammensetzung tagt und die Republikaner in beiden Kammern eine Mehrheit haben, hätte Massie für die Einleitung des Verfahrens aber auch die Stimmen einiger weiterer Republikaner gebraucht. Der US-Sender NBC berichtete, kein anderer Republikaner habe Massie offen Unterstützung für seinen Vorstoß signalisiert.
Eine Abstimmung der Kongresskammer über den Antrag ist somit vorerst vom Tisch. Wenn die Demokraten nach ihrem Sieg bei den Zwischenwahlen im kommenden Jahr die Mehrheit im Kongress bekommen, können sie ein neues Amtsenthebungsverfahren anschieben.
US-Präsident Donald Trump bekam durch das Scheitern von Massies Vorstoß kurz nach seiner krachenden Niederlage bei der Kongresswahl vergangene Woche nun wieder Rückenwind. Er bezeichnete das abgewendete Impeachment als »Freispruch für einen großen amerikanischen Patrioten« und betonte, der Amtsenthebungsversuch sei »unbegründet«.
Trump hatte sich nach dem Antrag umgehend hinter seinen »Kriegsminister« Hegseth gestellt und erklärt, dieser habe »sehr gute Arbeit« geleistet und zwei Kriege »gewonnen«. »Er gab die Befehle«, betonte der US-Präsident. Massie nannte er einen »Verlierer«.
Hegseth selbst sprach mit Blick auf den Amtsenthebungsversuch am Dienstag in seiner ersten Pressekonferenz seit rund sechs Monaten von einem »Schauprozess gegen den Präsidenten und seinen Kriegsminister« und von einem »politischen Spektakel«, das zum Scheitern verurteilt sei.
Massie wirft Hegseth Amtsverstöße in acht Bereichen vor. So habe der 46-Jährige ohne Zustimmung des Kongresses den Krieg gegen den Iran vorangetrieben und seine Befugnisse als Verteidigungsminister überschritten. Außerdem wirft der republikanische Abgeordnete dem früheren Fox-News-Moderator die »außergerichtliche Tötung« mutmaßlicher Drogenschmuggler durch Luftangriffe auf ihre Schiffe in der Karibik und im Ostpazifik vor.
Hegseth zählt zu den umstrittensten Ministern in Trumps Kabinett. Den größten Wirbel verursachte er im vergangenen Jahr mit der sogenannten Chatgruppenaffäre. Er teilte geheime Militärinformationen über den Handy-Messenger Signal, unter anderem mit seiner Frau und einem versehentlich zugeschalteten Journalisten. Nach der Signal-Affäre schränkte er den Zugang von Journalisten zum Pentagon massiv ein, was zum Auszug dutzender protestierender Reporter führte.
Im Iran-Krieg musste sich Hegseth gegen Vorwürfe verteidigen, er habe den Angriff auf eine Schule zu verantworten, bei dem nach iranischen Angaben mindestens 170 Menschen getötet wurden. Die Demokraten werfen dem Minister deshalb »Kriegsverbrechen« vor.
Zuletzt sorgte Hegseths Ankündigung für Empörung, die für Anfang Dezember angesetzte Hinrichtung des Attentäters von Fort Hood, Nidal Hasan, durch ein militärisches Erschießungskommando live übertragen zu wollen. Nach einem öffentlichen Aufschrei sagte Trump die geplante Liveübertragung ab. Agenturen/nd

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Netanyahu fights to stay relevant as Israel’s opposition closes in
A new Knesset shaped by October 7 prepares to convene as Netanyahu fights to prevent an opposition-led government
In the last few days, in marked contrast to an election campaign defined by its bitterness and the closeness of its personal attacks, Israel’s current prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of national unity and coming together with the opposition bloc that edged out his ruling coalition in October’s election.
On Saturday, the same day that Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasked former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government capable of commanding the Knesset, Netanyahu published a video on his social media account claiming Israel to be facing the genuine risk of civil war if a government were established with the support of Arab parties which he accused of wanting to “eliminate the State of Israel”.
Two days later, Netanyahu returned to the theme of existential threat in a further video, calling upon the leaders of the more successful bloc to recognise the “needs of the hour” and join, under his leadership, a single unified government that would also include the ultra-Orthodox parties, at least one of which is understood to be in talks with Eisenkot, as well as the prime minister’s controversial allies on the far right, Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir.
“It’s all a game at the moment. It’s leverage, it’s one-upmanship, it’s psyops, it’s spin, it’s counter-spin,” former Israeli government adviser Daniel Levy said of the invariably long and complex negotiations that take place ahead of establishing a government,
Currently, with the new Knesset being sworn in on Tuesday, speculation is focussing on the role of the Ultra Orthodox, or haredim, parties, which have traditionally offered support to Netanyahu in return for measures shielding their young male yeshiva students from the military draft in defiance off a Super Court ruling of June 2024.
Strategy
Nevertheless, irrespective of the past political cover offered to their members by Netanyahu, there are suggestions that one of the Ultra Orthodox parties United Torah Judaism (UTJ) – which refused to endorse Netanyahu’s selection to build a government by the President – is preparing to throw in behind Eisenkot, with the objections of one of the opposition’s principal figures Avigdor Lieberman said to be quieted in the face of either partnering with one of the Arab parties or the continued rule of Lieberman’s nemesis, Netanyahu and the prospect of further elections.
“‘It’s political strategy, that’s all,” Netanyahu’s former aide, Israeli pollster Mitchell Barak said from Jerusalem. ‘But he’s negotiating from a weakened position. With the UTJ, Eisenkot’s got 67 seats,’ he said of the numbers needed to gain a working majority in the 120 seat Knesset, “so, of course, Netanyahu’s going to do all he can to reinforce his bloc; Barak said of negotiations regarded by many as critical to Netanyahu’s personal future.
Netanyahu faces a number of challenges that speak directly to both his political legacy and personal freedom that he will lose all influence over should Eisenkot succeed him.
Foremost are like to be the multiple corruption charges that is is presently on trial for and, despite his claims of innocence that he has already preemptively petitioned the country’s President and his former political rival, Isaac Herzog for. Secondly, and more pressingly is the question of his and his government’s culpability for the alleged failings ahead of the October 7 Hamas led attack that triggered the genocide unleashed upon Gaza by Israel and the multiple strikes and attacks launched by Israel non regional neighbors in the years since.
New Knesset, new danger
Many of the new MKs being sworn in on Tuesday, including bereaved family members, reservists, advocates for the 250 or so Israelis taken captive that day and Eisenkot himself, who lost a son and two nephews in the genocide that followed, are all tied directly to October 7 and the wars that followed together creating a chamber where feelings over the October 7 attack and where culpability for its lies are said to run close to the surface.
In particular, attention is likely to focus sharply on Netanyahu himself, whose supposed miscalculations ahead of the attack, stories of numerous missed warnings and who was subsequently accused of dragging out the war, or sacrificing the welfare off the captives for his own political ends. Key among the opposition’s aims for the first day of parliamentary business is set to be the installation of Matan Kahana, a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar (“straight”) party and a keen advocate of a state inquiry into Netanyahu and the government’s failings ahead of the Hamas led attack.
“Having so many people connected so directly to October 7 is going to increase the temperature, but it’s become so politicized that a win for one side automatically becomes a loss for the other, so the bereaved family on the right can say we need to increase our militarism in honor of my son, and the bereaved family in the center says we need to enlist more people.
“Netanyahu can try to influence that but for the first time in a long time, he seems a bit lost,” Israeli political analyst Nimrod Flaschenberg said.
However, how lost Netanyahu may be, or how grounded his claims of pending civil war or destruction at the hands of regional adversaries may be, ultimately, his political and potentially personal fate now lies with an opposition that outstrips his own numerically and a volatile Knesset eager to comb over the mistakes of the past.
“There’s no appetite on the other side to go in with Netanyahu for a unity government,” Levy said,
“The only real circumstances under which that happen is if he can create a security emergency,” he said following a weekend where the UK press had reported daily phone calls from Netanyahu to the Trump administration urging renewed war on Iran.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Baby found alive after being buried in dog crate for 24 hours, South Carolina police say
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Guardian staff and Reuters
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
An 11-month-old boy was found alive in South Carolina after he was believed to have been buried for about 24 hours, local police said.
The infant, Koah Sharpe, was found on Tuesday wrapped inside a dog crate that was in turn wrapped in a towel and buried just under the surface in the woods, according to the Lexington county sheriff’s department.
“Certainly God is good. Just a few moments ago, we found little Koah, 11 months old, buried alive, clinging to life, crying – the most joyful sound you ever heard of a crying baby,” sheriff Jay Koon told a news conference.
Koon said the infant’s father, Michael Comer, 25, was arrested on Monday night on suspicion of burglary. The sheriff’s department is working with prosecutors to determine additional charges.
Koon said the towel wrapped around the crate had “by the grace of God, probably provided enough air for [Koah] to survive by our estimation the last 24 hours under that dirt”.
Koah went missing on Monday after he was left in his father’s care at his mother’s home while she ran an errand, Koon said.
The boy was later reported missing and authorities launched an expansive search, the sheriff said.
Koah was found after a search party discovered “freshly disturbed” dirt in the woods about 50 yards (45 metres) from Comer’s father’s house, Koon said.
“As they started digging you could hear little Koah crying. So as you can imagine the race was on, everybody was down there trying to get him out.”
Koah has been hospitalized and will “hopefully” recover, Koon said.
Koon said about 100 people had been searching for Koah.
“We want to thank everybody and celebrate the fact today that an 11-month-old baby is alive.”

https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/11/f.title: Feds Characterize Trump As Mercurial King In Latest Bid to End Congestion Pricing
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/11/f.author: Dave Colon
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/11/11/f.text:
New court, same losing argument.
The federal Department of Transportation continues to insist that the president and his agencies can do whatever they want, whenever they want, as the Trump administration tries without success to destroy congestion pricing in New York City.
In June, U.S. DOT appealed Judge Lewis Liman’s March decision in favor of the MTA, which sued the federal government over President Trump’s attempt to kill the Manhattan toll. In their brief, the feds asked court, not for the first time, to endorse the idea that Trump’s whims, rather that the law, have the final say over his government’s actions.
The brief contained two main arguments. The first, which will be familiar to longtime followers of this increasingly absurd legal saga, is that Liman never had the authority to hear the MTA’s lawsuit because it involves a dispute over a financial contract. If that were true, the entire case should have been heard by the smaller and more specialized Court of Federal Claims, not the larger and more general Article III court system.
The second and newer argument is similar to what the Trump administration argued in lower court: that the FHWA can do whatever it wants at any time. But instead of arguing that the president is a de facto sovereign who enjoys unlimited powers, Department of Justice attorneys argued that the FHWA can simply change its mind at any time.
“[E]ven if the Agreement were considered in [Administrative Procedure Act] terms — not as a contract but as a ‘regulatory grant of approval to build toll infrastructure on a federal aid highway,’ or perhaps as a similar agency action granting a benefit or establishing a federal program—the agency would have the inherent power to reconsider and revoke it,” the attorneys wrote.
The argument is consistent with the federal government’s longstanding position from the moment President Donald Trump kicked off his attempt to kill congestion pricing: that the president has inherent king-like powers to do whatever he likes. After Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy sent his first letter demanding New York end the toll in February 2025, Trump dubbed himself the King of New York. Ever since, the rest of the federal machinery has scrambled to stand up his argument.
Last January, in a hearing before Judge Liman, DOJ lawyer Eric Hamilton argued unconvincingly that the president and his agents possessed an absolute power to cancel contracts or agreements the federal government signs with other parties. Liman described that argument as “breathtaking” and “wrong.”
So the brightest legal minds still willing to work for the Department of Justice tried once more to convince the judiciary that American law allows the federal government to be an unreliable partner. Instead of insisting that the president can cancel contracts, DOJ lawyers argued that federal agencies can just change their mind about previous approvals. “The government must be empowered to adjust to changing circumstances or to changed priorities,” they wrote.
The problem with the new argument, as one legal expert pointed out, is the very same problem that tripped up Duffy when he tried to end congestion pricing: the agreement that authorized congestion pricing, the Value Pricing Pilot Program, lacks a kill switch and the overall law authorizing the program lacks a “revoke whenever you want” clause. 
Among the cases the federal government cited as precedent was California Sea Urchin Commission v. Bean, which involved a dispute over sea otter relocation program. That program followed an agreement with a specific clause that allowed the program to end under certain conditions — an arrangement found nowhere in the VPPP.
“It’s a stretch to say they have any inherent authority just to change their mind,” said NYU law professor Roderick Hills, Jr. “I don’t know of any case that said an agency can just always change its mind, regardless of the statute under which the initial decision was made, regardless of the correctness of the original decision.”
Hills said that precedent does allow for an agency to reverse itself if it can prove that it authorized a program based on an actual error. But since the FHWA didn’t rely on Duffy’s very first argument — which is that the VPPP never actually authorized cordon pricing — Hills was perplexed as to why the government cited case law that’s hinges so strongly on human error.
“Almost all the cases they cite involve an initial agency decision that was a mistake, or that the agency claimed was a mistake,” he said. “Since they don’t claim or identify any error that was made in the initial decision here, it’s hard to see how they can claim they have power to correct an error that they don’t indicate. How can you correct an error that doesn’t exist?” 
The argument is also out of place because the federal government didn’t raise it when the MTA sued the FHWA in district court. A district court will hear all sorts of weird legal arguments that a plaintiff or defendant puts forward. But at the appeals court level, judges only consider whether there the lower court’s ruling committed a legal error. A requirement known as “appellate preservation” requires a party in a suit raise the specific issue if it wants to be able to raise it on appeal.
Since the government never suggested in the lower court that it ordered an end to congestion pricing because a federal agency can just change its mind, the judges hearing the case could decide to ignore the argument entirely.
“The simplest thing to do would be not to rule on the merits at all, but say on second argument, you didn’t raise it below. It’s waived,” said Hills.
Because of these discrepancies, the Second Circuit may choose to exclusively analyze the federal government’s argument that the original VPPP contract, between the MTA and the FHWA, should be reviewed by the Federal Court of Claims, which considers federal disputes over contracts for money. Liman rejected that argument in the lower court.
There is no strong evidence that shows the dispute over congestion pricing is a contractual dispute over money. Furthermore, the MTA has been levying the tolls for nearly two years now and New York City has yet to fall. Both of these elements bode well for the MTA and the future of congestion pricing.
“Sean Duffy is the one who’s trying to change the status quo,” said Hills. “For almost two years, the MTA has been chugging along, and Sean Duffy’s been on the sideline saying, ‘Judge, stop that guy.’ In general, judges, like everybody else, don’t like to get involved with something unless there’s a good reason to get involved and change the status quo. 
Hills continued: “In this case, the legal arguments are weak, and the policy here seems fine. The Second Circuit has to hear the case. They have mandatory review, so they’ll have to say something, but after two 100-page opinions, I imagine that they won’t think they need to say a whole bunch.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.title: A gente não quer só comida! Crônicas de Viagem XX
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.author: Cidade das Letras: literatura e educação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/colunist.text:
Para Carmem, Natália, José Edimar, Edson e Beatriz, pela generosidade dos gestos
Por Luciano Mendes
Quando eu era criança, em minha casa não havia livros em abundância. Havia a Bíblia, por suposto, e um ou outro livro escolar dos irmãos e das irmãs mais velhas, estes mais supostos do que lembrados. E havia também, deste eu me lembro, As mais belas histórias, que a família inteira, ou quase, já que é muito grande, leu.
Depois veio a escola e os livros escolares passaram a fazer parte da rotina, ainda que continuassem escassos em minha casa e na casa de outros alunos, o que obrigava as professoras a recorrerem continuamente ao ponto, ditado ou passado no quadro.
Mas, em algum momento do início de minha adolescência, um meu irmão mais velho, o Anselmo, me transmitiu o gosto pela leitura de revistas em quadrinhos e livrinhos de faroeste. Eu os lia compulsivamente. Quando nos mudamos, a família toda, para Contagem, na Grande Belo Horizonte, eu andava uma boa distância para ir até algumas bancas do Barreiro que trocavam revistinhas e os tais livros quase sem exigirem algum dinheiro de volta.
Anos depois, já jovem adulto, troquei as bancas pelos sebos e pelas feiras de livros, usados e novos, e continuei a garimpar livros e outros objetos impressos para formar uma pequena biblioteca. E deles usufruo a companhia e as belezas ainda hoje.
Minha memória fez este périplo outro dia quando, em Porto Alegre, eu estava na feira, ou melhor, no Brique da Redenção, onde se encontra de um tudo, inclusive livros para comprar. Estava na capital gaúcha para trabalhar mas, desta vez, ao contrário das outras que lá estive, reservei um bom tempo para conhecer a cidade, suas entrâncias e sua gastronomia. E comecei justamente pelo brique. E foi ótimo!
Passando pelas bancas, não pude evitar pensar sobre o quanto de história aquelas milhares de pequenas – e algumas um pouco maiores – peças atualizavam e transmitiam de uma história que remonta a décadas e, mesmo, séculos. Muitas pessoas, muitas famílias, muitas cidades, milhares de caminhos para chegarem até aqui e ficarem assim, disponíveis, a um esticar de braços, a uma mão cuidadosa, a um olhar fortuito… ficava eu pensando.
Mas há quem frequente feira só para conversar, jogar conversa fora, papear com amigos ou desconhecidos. Eu não sou muito deste tipo, mas desta vez foi muito bom conversar com o artista plástico Cristian Massa que, bem no meio do brique, expunha seus quadros, lindos quadros, e com quem pude trocar ideias sobre suas inspirações, suas técnicas e suas obras.
Para não dizer que não comprei nada, numa das bancas eu vi, de longe, a capa do livro Rio Grande do Sul – Terra e Povo e imediatamente me lembrei que eu tinha um exemplar, com o mesmo design da capa, só que dedicada a Minas Gerais. Vi, então, que se tratava de uma Coleção da Editora Globo e que, possivelmente, haveria volumes sobre outros estados. Comprei o exemplar exposto, já indagando quem escreveu sobre educação e como o tema foi abordado na Coleção. Depois, chegando em casa, vi que há também um volume sobre São Paulo (o qual já adquiri de um sebo na internet!!!).
Saí do Brique da Redenção portando meu livro e fiz uma boa caminhada até a Praça da Alfândega onde ocorria a Feira do Livro de Porto Alegre. Ali, como se pode imaginar, livros e leituras em profusão para alimentar todos os espíritos ávidos pelas letras.
Entrar na feira, passear pela feira, comprando ou não livros, me dá sempre a sensação mais nua e crua de uma ignorância enorme, um quase mal-estar, por saber de milhões, bilhões até, de livros que jamais lerei, de conhecimentos que jamais terei e de sensibilidades as quais jamais partilharei. Um horror! Mas para não dizer que saí de mãos vazia, comprei um livro lindo: Kabuki – verão, outono, inverno, primavera, de Guilherme Petreca e Tiago Minamisawa (Editora Pipoca & Nanquim, 2025).
Saí de lá, já com fome, e me pus a caminho do apartamento em que eu estava hospedado, na Avenida Independência. No meio do caminho, ali bem perto da Santa Casa, num daqueles pequenos restaurantes de esquina que vendem prato feito, uma cena. Numa mesa do canto, uma mulher e uma criança pequena, de não mais de 10 anos. Não pareciam estar confortáveis no ambiente, mas pareciam se entender, pareciam uma mãe e uma filha.
Enquanto compartilhavam um prato com arroz, um pouco de carne, batatinha frita e umas rodelas de tomate, a menina abre uma sacola plástica, pega um livro de capa colorida, o põe ao lado do prato e começa ler. Na avidez por conhecer os mistérios do livro, sem olhar para o prato, estica a mão para pegar uma batatinha e pega um pedaço de tomate. Olha para os dedos molhados e faz cara de nojo. “Como passar as páginas com estes dedos assim?”, imaginei ela pensando. A mãe olha a cena, sorri e lhe passa um guardanapo. Ela enxuga os dedos, pega a batatinha e volta à leitura.
Elas pareciam felizes ali, as duas, juntas, numa grande cumplicidade. A comida parecia apenas um detalhe.
Luciano Mendes de Faria Filho é pedagogo, doutor em Educação e professor titular da UFMG. Publicou, dentre outros, “Uma brasiliana para a América Hispânica – a editora Fondo de Cultura Econômica e a intelectualidade brasileira” (Paco Editorial, 2021)
